Ruins of both Gondorian watchtowers and Umbrian encampments occupy the same ridgelines, sometimes within sight of each other. The geology doesn't take sides; the limestone and granite are simply old.
Hot dry summers, brief mild winters; the wind off the desert in summer strips everything not anchored down. The salt flats on the coast are blindingly white in the afternoon sun.

Soldiers and smugglers, with a few stubborn farmers who have lived in the middle of the dispute so long they have stopped expecting resolution. Their loyalties depend entirely on who controls the nearest waterhole.

land.name: Aegardh (Fell Region)
land.biome_hint: hot dry steppe with thin grasses, canyon systems and sparse nomadic pasture
land.description: The dry, flat upland plateau of central and eastern Harondor, cut by canyons and narrow wadis (Emyn Gonngaran in the northeast); historically home to the Eraguk nomads and now a contested zone of Gondorian border control and periodic banditry.[file:73]

land.name: Bursk country (southern Harondor)
land.biome_hint: semi-arid to arid scrub desert with scattered dunes, sparse shrubs and heat-adapted wildlife
land.description: Sandy scrub desert with dunes in southern Harondor, transitional between the Aegardh steppe and the true Great Desert of Harad; dry and inhospitable, crossed only by the Harnen corridor.[file:73]

land.name: Vale of Harnen (Nan Harnen)
land.biome_hint: semi-arid river valley with volcanic soils, irrigated agriculture and riparian gallery woodland
land.description: The valley of the Harnen river running east to west across southern Harondor, enriched by volcanic Ephel Dûath soils and supporting date palm orchards and sorghum fields; the main cultural corridor between Gondor and Harad.[file:73]

land.name: Harithilien
land.biome_hint: semi-arid to dry upland with volcanic-soil fields and scrub, moderated by orographic rainfall
land.description: A distinct zone on the western face of the Ephel Dûath north of the Harnen, watered by northward bay winds and enriched by volcanic soils; relatively arable compared to the Aegardh and historically contested between Gondor and the powers of Mordor.[file:73]

facts.notes: Harondor is treated as a separate region from the Gondorian heartland due to its clearly distinct biome (steppe-desert vs. temperate coastal), political instability and frontier character; it is the transitional zone to Near Harad and should be linked with that region for route and climate continuity.[file:73] Best described in three zones: a fertile coastal strip receiving sufficient rain to support cedar, oak, juniper, and palm with domestic crops (olives, dates, grapes, pomegranates); vegetated dune-fields, badlands, and hilly shrublands inland; and an arid desert interior of active dunes and salt flats.

people.description: Harondor is a contested borderland with no stable dominant power in T.A. 1640; Gondorian border rangers, Haruze nomads, Eraguk steppe-folk and Umbarean agents all claim influence at different times.

aspect.en: Southern Gondor comprises the fertile river valleys, coastal plains, highland vales and mountain flanks between the White Mountains (Ered Nimrais) and the Bay of Belfalas, encompassing the provinces of Lebennin, Belfalas/Dor-en-Ernil, Lamedon, Anfalas and the Pinnath Gelin—the heartland of Númenórean civilization in Middle-earth.

rotation: Long shore of salt marshes, estuaries and reed-beds where sea and land blur. Fishermen in flat-bottomed boats and sheep-farming on the Pinnath Gelin sustain this region quietly forgotten by politics but essential to the south.

Salt marsh, estuary and reed-bed where the land keeps forgetting to end. Flat-bottomed boats work the channels between reed-islands; the shepherds on the Pinnath Gelin above watch the same fog every morning.
Sparse coastal oak and pine survive on the headlands, wind-scoured and stunted, rooted in rock above the fishing villages. Below them, the salt makes everything short and tough.
The Pinnath Gelin hills are the spine of the region — green enough in summer, grey in winter — with a few rivers cutting down to an Anduin estuary that smells of tidal mud at low water.
A temperate maritime climate that means grey drizzle more than dramatic weather. The coast rarely sees frost; the hills behind it sometimes do. The sea rules the mood of the land.
Fishermen who know every tide-channel and shepherds who know every pass in the Pinnath Gelin, and both groups largely indifferent to what Gondor decides in Minas Tirith.

land.name: Lebennin (Land of Five Rivers)
land.biome_hint: temperate fertile lowlands with mixed agriculture, river floodplains, boggy bottomland and mountain-fringe conifer forests
land.description: The heartland of Southern Gondor, a fertile central plain watered by the Gilnduin, Celos, Serni, Erui and their tributaries; the most populous and productive province, dominated by farmland with boggy bottomlands near the rivers and conifer-covered mountain valleys to the north.[file:73]

land.name: Dor-en-Ernil / Belfalas
land.biome_hint: rocky Mediterranean-type coast with mountain mineral wealth, pine forests and maritime influence
land.description: The rocky peninsula and coastal province of the Prince of Belfalas, containing the Ered Torthonion and the citadel of Dol Amroth; silver-rich mountains, the sacred kirinki birds and the Elven haven Edhellond define its character.[file:73]

land.name: Anfalas and Pinnath Gelin
land.biome_hint: low coastal plain with fens, salt marshes, fishing grounds and rolling highland pasture
land.description: A long, thin coastal land west of the Morthond with flat, waterlogged plains, fens and rich fishing grounds; the Pinnath Gelin highlands to the north support wool-producing sheep and a timber-mining economy.[file:73]

land.name: Lamedon
land.biome_hint: forested mountain vales and upland pastures with mineral-rich geology
land.description: Mountain province of the White Mountains rich in iron, copper and silver deposits; a militarized zone in early Third Age history, later transformed into a province supporting mining communities and highland farming.[file:73]

land.name: Cape of Andrast
land.biome_hint: wet Atlantic-type rocky cape with steep valleys, heavy rainfall and primitive settlement
land.description: The rugged, rain-battered westernmost cape of Southern Gondor where the White Mountains bend into the sea; steep-sided green valleys and bare peaks home to the Dunir (Orodbedhrim), essentially untouched by Gondorian civilization.[file:73]

land.name: Ethir Anduin (Great Delta)
land.biome_hint: subtropical-type estuarine delta with marshes, swamps, tidal channels and rich aquatic biodiversity
land.description: The vast, meandering delta of the Anduin where it meets the Bay of Belfalas, created by the Númenórean Downfall's Great Wave; a unique ecosystem of swamps, channels, marsh and tidal flats with crocodiles, fishing cats and swamp tribes.[file:73]

land.name: Tolfalas
land.biome_hint: geologically active island with volcanic soils, hot springs, endemic sacred trees and nesting sea turtles
land.description: A volcanic island in the Bay of Belfalas with dramatic topography, hot springs, active minor eruptions and the sacred oiolair trees; settlement has always been marginal due to geological instability.[file:73]

land.name: Bay of Belfalas
land.biome_hint: warm temperate sea with rich coastal fisheries, marine mammals, whale migration routes and volatile weather
land.description: The great bay forming the southern coast of Gondor, sitting on the continental shelf and rich in marine life; critical for trade, fishing and naval power but plagued by unpredictable storms and Corsair threats.[file:73]

facts.notes: Southern Gondor's natural environment has been extensively reshaped by Númenórean colonization; the biomes encoded here reflect the Third Age T.A. 1640 state, not a pristine natural landscape; the most 'wild' zones are the Cape of Andrast, Ethir Anduin delta, upper mountain vales and Tolfalas. Harondor (the arid plateau south of the Poros) is treated as a separate region.[file:73]

people.description: Southern Gondor is the most populous and civilized part of Gondor, dominated by Dúnedain nobility and the Daen-Dúnedain mixed population of the river plains, with Daen highlanders (Orodbedhrim) in the upland vales, swamp peoples in the Ethir Anduin, and Grey-elves at Edhellond.

aspect.en: Rohan is a beautiful territory and one of the jewels of the Gondorian crown, a wide land of rolling pastures and coombes dominated by the towering peaks of the White Mountains, home of the semi‑nomadic Horse‑lords who became the Rohirrim after T.A. 2510.

rotation: Western frontier of Gondor between the Fords of Isen and the Andrast. Heather-covered hills, swift rivers and a Gondorian presence that fades westward. Dunlendish farmers have filled the void left by the departed Dúnedain.
The western edge of Gondor, where the kingdom's authority thins like the heather on the hills. Dunlendish farmers fill the land the Dúnedain left; the Isen to the north is the real frontier.
Heather hills and swift rivers, the terrain of a border country that knows it is a border country. The roads are maintained but watched; the wayhouses are fortified and the innkeepers ask questions.

Hills and upland moors carry the western spurs of the White Mountains to their end above the sea. Beneath them, in the valleys, farmland that has changed hands so many times its ownership is the oldest local argument.
Cold winds from the Atlantic sweep up the coast and stall against the mountains; rain is reliable. The summers are never warm enough for Gondorian tastes, which is partly why the Dúnedain left.
Dunlendish settlers who remember their own history of displacement and farm accordingly — defensively, quietly, keeping what they hold and expecting to have to hold it harder tomorrow.

land.name: The Riddermark (Rohan proper)
land.biome_hint: broad temperate grasslands with high plains, coombes, and mountain foothills
land.description: The Green Province of Calenardhon after T.A. 2510, granted to the Othod by Steward Cirion; bounded roughly by the Anduin on the east, the Isen on the west, the White Mountains on the south, and Fangorn and the Limlight on the north.

land.name: The Wold
land.biome_hint: windy chalk downs suited to sheep pasture
land.description: Steeply folded, semi‑arid downs forming the northeastern part of Rohan; green but treeless hills of short, springy grass and heather, with porous chalky rock where rain drains off quickly.

land.name: East Emnet and West Emnet
land.biome_hint: deep fertile grasslands ideal for horse herds
land.description: Vast carpets of tall grass forming the central plains; East Emnet stretches between the Wold and the Entwash, West Emnet between Fangorn, the Misty Mountains, and the Deeping Stream.

land.name: Eastfold and Westfold
land.biome_hint: rolling foothill pastures with coombes and stream‑cut valleys
land.description: Rich, well‑watered pastures along the northern flanks of the White Mountains, cut by streams from the high valleys; Westfold holds the Deeping Coomb and Hornburg, Eastfold contains Harrowdale and the Snowbourne.

land.name: Westmarch
land.biome_hint: windswept frontier grassland with high rainfall and superb grazing
land.description: Westernmost area of Rohan, lying west and south of the Gap between the Angren (Isen) and Adorn; lightly settled, often threatened by Dunlendings, with the best grass and finest horses in the realm.

land.name: Gap of Rohan
land.biome_hint: broad, windy mountain gap with river valleys
land.description: Forty‑mile‑wide strategic pass between the southern Misty Mountains and the northwestern White Mountains, only about 3,700 feet high at its center, providing a grassy doorway between Eriador and lands east and south.

land.name: White Mountains (Ered Nimrais edge)
land.biome_hint: alpine mountains with snowfields, cliffs, caves, and conifer woods on lower slopes
land.description: Snow‑covered limestone and marble range rising steeply from Rohan’s meadows, with jagged peaks like the Thrihyrne, Starkhorn, Irensaga, and Dwimorberg; carved by glaciers into alpine valleys such as the Deeping Coomb and Harrowdale.

land.name: Major rivers of Rohan
land.biome_hint: cold snow‑fed rivers, fens in the Entwash delta, and trout streams in mountain valleys
land.description: The Isen and Adorn feed the Westmarch; the Entwash rises in Fangorn and winds through the heart of Rohan before breaking into a fen‑filled delta at its mouths; the Snowbourne rises in the White Mountains at Harrowdale; the Limlight separates the East Emnet from Lórien.

facts.notes: This region object focuses on Rohan in the Rohirric Age (T.A. 2510 onward), but the same land supports earlier Othod settlements; sub‑sites like Edoras, Helm’s Deep, and Dunharrow can be handled as separate site objects tied to this region.

people.description: The Horse‑lords are a wandering people whose history passes through three main stages—othraim in southern Rhovanion, othod in the vales of the Anduin, and Rohirrim in Rohan—remaining semi‑nomadic and horse‑centered but evolving from scattered clans to a unified kingdom at the heart of western trade and war.

aspect.en: Arthedain is the northern Dúnedain kingdom in Eriador, cradled between the Blue Mountains and the Misty Mountains and bounded by the rivers Lhûn and Baranduin, a cool, sparsely populated realm of rocky hills, downs, marshes, and the Shire, ruled from Fornost as the last Númenórean realm in the North in T.A. 1640.

rotation: The most gentle and inhabited part of Arthedain, with rolling hills, green hedgerows and the Shire of the Hobbits to the south. The Brandywine to the east and the Great East Road connect this fertile land to the wider world.

Rolling hills and green hedgerows, the most ordered and comfortable part of what remains of Arthedain. The Shire begins at the Brandywine and the Hobbits have kept their portion tidy in ways the wider world has not.

The vegetation here is the domesticated version of what Eriador once was: hedgerow elms, pasture grasses, kitchen gardens. The wildness has been gardened out of the south, which is either comforting or melancholy depending on who you are.

The Brandywine forms the Shire's eastern edge and the Great East Road divides the land cleanly — north toward Bree, south toward nothing much. The crossroads make this the most travelled part of the north.
Milder than northern Arthedain, wet enough for good grass and cold enough to keep the summers honest. Snow rarely lasts more than a week on the low ground.
Hobbits in the Shire and Dúnedain passing through; both groups have learned to be invisible in their own ways, for entirely different reasons.

land.name: Forochel and the Icy North
land.biome_hint: arctic coastal tundra and sea-ice
land.description: The far northern portion of Arthedain reaches toward the Ice-bay of Forochel and the Forodwaith, a realm of ice-plains, tundra and bitter cold, inhabited mainly by the Lossoth and visited by Dúnedain only in times of dire need.[file:25]

land.name: North Downs
land.biome_hint: rocky downs with thin soils and open grass-heath
land.description: High rolling hills east of Lake Evendim, forming rocky ridges that march across northeastern Arthedain like massive natural altars; they shelter and overlook Fornost and serve as a defensive barrier toward Angmar.[file:25]

land.name: Lake Nenuial (Lake Evendim)
land.biome_hint: cool upland lake with stony shores and reeds
land.description: A large blue lake in north-central Arthedain, sheltered on three sides by the Hills of Evendim, with the ruined first capital of Annúminas on its southern shore.[file:25]

land.name: Annúminas
land.biome_hint: ruins on windy lake-hills
land.description: Elendil’s original capital of Arnor on the southern shore of Lake Evendim, once a glittering Númenórean city and now a crumbling ruin of marble and stone razed in T.A. 1409.[file:25]

land.name: Fornost Erain
land.biome_hint: fortified hill-city in rocky uplands
land.description: The Northern Fortress of the Kings, built on the southern slopes of the North Downs, ringed by dikes and walls, now the capital of Arthedain and seat of its Royal Court and Seers in T.A. 1640.[file:25]

land.name: Baranduin / Brandywine River
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with mixed woodland and farmland
land.description: A swift yet meandering river flowing over 500 miles from Lake Evendim to the Sea south of Harlindon, forming a major barrier and artery, with key crossings at the Brandywine Bridge and Sarn Ford and providing the Shire with water and fertile valley lands.[file:25]

land.name: Southern Arthedain and the Shire
land.biome_hint: temperate lowland farmland and hedged hills
land.description: The fertile southern part of the kingdom, once neglected by Dúnedain concerned with war, now intensively farmed and settled by hobbits of the Shire, with rolling hills, rich fields and the Green Hill Country.[file:25]

land.name: Weather Hills and Amon Sûl
land.biome_hint: treeless limestone ridges and exposed summits
land.description: Barren rocky ridges in the southeast forming a natural wall along the border, culminating at Weathertop (Amon Sûl), a thousand-foot hill that once bore the chief northern palantír tower and still dominates the Great East Road.[file:25]

land.name: Midgewater Marshes
land.biome_hint: cool, insect-ridden freshwater bog
land.description: Buzzing bogs below the Weather Hills, carved in glacial times and now collecting stagnant water in treacherous pools swarming with midges, making overland travel slow and unpleasant.[file:25]

land.name: White Downs, Far Downs and Tower Hills
land.biome_hint: chalk downs with short turf and coastal influence
land.description: Chalk cliffs and downs in the west of the Shire leading up to the Emyn Beraid (Tower Hills), where three ancient white towers overlook the estuary of the Lhûn and house a westward-looking palantír.[file:25]

land.name: Bree-land and the Greenway
land.biome_hint: temperate hill-country with fields and woodland patches
land.description: Region around Bree-hill where the Great East Road crosses the old North–South road (Greenway); Bree is surrounded by ditches, dikes and hedges rather than walls, and serves as a weathered but still significant stop for travelers and traders.[file:25]

facts.notes: This Arthedain object is meant to capture the realm as described around T.A. 1640 in Rangers of the North, with climate and landforms usable as a base layer for pathfinding, biome assignment and climate modeling; more focused regions like Angmar, Cardolan and Rhudaur are handled in their own supplements.[file:25]

people.military: Royal Forces: 540 Men at Arms. 370 Cavalry. 1,000 Rangers. Noble Forces: 2,150 Men at Arms. 620 Cavalry. 3,000 Levy.
people.population: 50,000 Dúnedain (not including the Shire and Bree-land).
people.description: Arthedain’s population is dominated by the high Men of the Dúnedain, with important minorities including the hobbits of the Shire, the Lossoth of Forochel, rivermen on the northern waters, Bree-landers at the crossroads, and scattered Northmen and Dunlendish groups on the borders.

aspect.en: Cardolan, the Land of Red Hills, is the southern successor-kingdom of Arnor between the Baranduin and the Gwathló–Mitheithel, a windswept land of treeless plains, red downs, marshy river basins and the barrow‑haunted hills whose shattered Dúnedain realm never fully recovered from war, civil strife and plague.

rotation: Deforested plain between the Baranduin and the Gwathló, once dense woodland felled by the Númenóreans for their shipyards. Depopulated since the Great Plague, with abandoned villages in the scrub and Dúnedain barrows across the open land.

The plain between the two great rivers, once dense woodland that the Númenóreans felled for their shipyards. Abandoned since the Great Plague, with scrub growing back through the ruins of villages and the mounds of Dúnedain graves.
Birch and bracken on the old field-systems, bramble over the village foundations. The land is slowly making its own decisions about what comes next, with no one watching closely enough to object.
Flat, broad and waterlogged in the wet seasons, when the Gwathló and Baranduin both push their floodplains outward. In summer it dries to a country of pale grass and old earthworks.
Atlantic weather from the west meets nothing to stop it on this plain. Rain arrives in long grey curtains; the winters are damp rather than severe, which doesn't mean they're easy.
Wandering Gwathuirim tribes and the occasional Dúnedain Ranger who comes through quickly and tells no one why. No permanent settlements; the last ones died with the Great Plague.

land.name: Cardolan proper
land.biome_hint: treeless temperate plains with river basins and red downs
land.description: All lands between Baranduin and Gwathló–Mitheithel as far north as the Great East Road, roughly six hundred miles by one hundred and fifty, divided by the Old North Road into Minhiriath (Region of the Streams) and Mintyrnath (Region of the Downs). [file:31]

land.name: Minhiriath
land.biome_hint: semi‑arid temperate plain with many streams and floodplain pockets
land.description: The southwestern half of Cardolan, a nearly featureless, gently seaward‑sloping plain cut by countless small rivers and streams toward Baranduin, Gwathló and the sea, with generally poor soils suited mainly to sheep, except along streams and in the richly silted Gwathló basin.[file:31]

land.name: Mintyrnath
land.biome_hint: windswept hills and downs with thin turf and scattered woods
land.description: The northeastern half, a complex of red downs, highlands and basins including the Pinnath Ceren, Barrow‑downs, South Downs, Girithlin highlands and parts of the Gwathló basin; windswept, infertile ridges alternate with richer floodplains.[file:31]

land.name: Barrow-downs (Tyrn Gorthad) and South Downs
land.biome_hint: open chalk and limestone ridges with short turf and barrow mounds
land.description: A line of ridges running northeast with steep southwestern faces and long gentle slopes, largely treeless and infertile, famed for ancient Adan passage‑graves, royal barrows and later the Wight‑haunted mounds of Cardolan’s princes.[file:31]

land.name: Old Forest (Taur Iaur)
land.biome_hint: dense temperate old‑growth forest with hostile, uneven ground
land.description: Dark, dangerous woodland west of the Barrow‑downs between them and Baranduin, where resentful ancient trees remain from the primordial forest and house Tom Bombadil’s domain; little inhabited and largely unexplored by Cardolani.[file:31]

land.name: Pinnath Ceren and Girithlin highlands
land.biome_hint: rocky red and white ridges, thin soils, cool and windy
land.description: Red‑tinted ridges atop a small plateau and the higher Girithlin highlands, rich in iron ores and marble, historically centers of resistance and mining, but exposed to erosion and only marginally fertile beyond scattered farming pockets.[file:31]

land.name: Gwathló basin and Nîn‑in‑Eilph
land.biome_hint: rich alluvial farmland and extensive freshwater marshes
land.description: The wide, flood‑prone basin of the Gwathló, narrow near the sea but spreading to almost eighty miles near Tharbad, with extremely fertile silted farmlands on the floodplain and the four‑hundred‑square‑mile Swanfleet Marshes of alkali bogs and swans where Mitheithel and Glanduin join.[file:31]

land.name: Rast Vorn and Eryn Vorn
land.biome_hint: coastal dark forest on broken, foggy, reef‑strewn shores
land.description: A dark, mostly unexplored peninsula south of the Baranduin’s mouth with treacherous shoal‑ridden, fog‑shrouded coasts and the ancient Dark Woods inhabited by Beffraen; considered one of the most dangerous coasts known to Dúnadan mariners.[file:31]

land.name: Tharbad and environs
land.biome_hint: urban island in broad, seasonally flooded river marsh
land.description: The great river‑port city raised above surrounding fenland at the Gwathló crossing, protected by immense dikes and causeways and straddling the river with wondrous bridges; later reduced by siege, plague and flood to a decaying but still strategic free city in the marshes.[file:31]

facts.notes: This Cardolan object treats the realm at its mid‑Third Age extent around T.A. 1640 as a single climatic and cultural region node, combining Minhiriath and Mintyrnath into one macro‑region for your model; more detailed political units like Saralainn, Tharbad, individual principalities or the Warlord’s domain can be spun out later as separate objects if finer resolution is needed.[file:31]

people.military: Each Prince and Lord commands about 100 warriors in a personal retinue and can raise 200-800 levy troops in 2-3 weeks. Most often, however, the Lords rely upon mercenary bands and the Dunnish tribes in the region for military muscle. Gondor and Arthedain also maintain garrisons in Cardolan to ensure the safety of the trade routes.
people.population: 48,000 Cardolani (not including populations of Saralainn or the Cantons).
people.description: Cardolan’s population mixes Dúnedain princes and warriors, Eriadoran Northmen, Dunlendings, Beffraen and later southern refugees; after the Kingdom’s fall the land fragments into rival principalities, mercenary companies, peasant rebels, Gondorian garrisons and eventually bandit‑ridden ruins under the shadow of Angmar.

aspect.en: Cardolan, the Land of Red Hills, is the southern successor-kingdom of Arnor between the Baranduin and the Gwathló–Mitheithel, a windswept land of treeless plains, red downs, marshy river basins and the barrow‑haunted hills whose shattered Dúnedain realm never fully recovered from war, civil strife and plague.

rotation: Cape of black rock cliffs jutting into Belegaer south of the Gwathló, with an interior of old twisted oaks sheltering primitive Gwathuirim tribes. Inhospitable and forgotten, it serves as refuge for those who flee from everything.
Black rock cape south of the Gwathló, where cliffs drop into Belegaer and the interior is old twisted oak over groundwater springs. The Gwathuirim who live here are as hard as the rock they inhabit.

Coastal heath and rough moorland with pockets of oak in the sheltered valleys. The trees are old and gnarled and grow along the water rather than away from it, as if they know the only reliable thing here is the rain.

Cliffs and rocky inlets on the coast, with the sea too rough for most boats and the interior too hostile for easy travel. The capes protect the Gwathuirim from outside authority better than any wall could.
Windy, wet and cold, but not arctic. The sea keeps the winters from being brutal; it does nothing for the grey damp that lasts from autumn through spring.
Primitive clans who have lived here since before the Númenórean felling and intend to live here after whatever comes next. Their invisibility in the terrain is their main defensive strategy.

aspect.en: Harithilien is South Ithilien, a distinct, fertile, and beautiful region bordering Harondor and Mordor. It is characterized by volcanic soils enriched by the Ephel Dúath, featuring ancient ruined estates of Gondor, hidden ranger outposts, and lush vegetation.

rotation: Southern Ithilien — the garden of Gondor gone half-wild: hills of gorse and heath, woods of fir and cedar, and glades thick with herbs that the sun turns to incense.
A singing land under a shadowed sky — streams thread the glades to hidden falls and green pools, and the air is fresh with a sweetness that recalls the distant North.
Rangers' country; the paths are hidden and the lookouts are secret. The ruins of Gondor's watch-places stand among the trees, still held against the East.
The land is fair but scarred — fire-marks in the clearings, trampled glades, and always the dark line of the Ephel Dúath closing the eastern sky.
Warm and sweet in summer, grey and sleeping in winter; rain comes soft and fragrant off the mountains and the herbs answer it.
Water is the music of Ithilien — singing streams, hidden waterfalls, and dark pools under the green shade; the land will not be made ugly while the water runs.

land.name: Ephel Dúath Valleys
land.biome_hint: semi-arid to dry upland with volcanic-soil fields and scrub
land.description: The green, deep valleys on the western face of the Mountains of Shadow.

facts.notes: Harithilien is highly contested and frequently raided by Haradrim and Orcs marching north.

people.military: Ranger squads.
people.description: Populated by rangers and skirmishing Gondor/Mordor soldiers.

source.supplement: Tolkien (LotR) with Ithilien / Gondor regional material

phrases: Ithilien in summer is a garden gone half-wild — gold gorse, sweet herbs, and green glades under a warm sun, with the shadowed mountains always at the edge of sight.
Winter strips Ithilien to grey heath and dark wood; it is still fair, but a fair thing sleeping under frost, with the East waiting beyond the river.
Rain on Ithilien is soft and fragrant; it beads the gorse, quickens the herbs, and washes the smoke of the East from the clean northern air.

aspect.en: Southern Gondor comprises the fertile river valleys, coastal plains, highland vales and mountain flanks between the White Mountains (Ered Nimrais) and the Bay of Belfalas, encompassing the provinces of Lebennin, Belfalas/Dor-en-Ernil, Lamedon, Anfalas and the Pinnath Gelin—the heartland of Númenórean civilization in Middle-earth.

rotation: The Vale of Morthond — a broad green bay of grass beneath the southern cliffs of the White Mountains, where the Blackroot river comes down cold and loud out of the heights.
On the mountain's root stands the Dimholt, a wood of black trees where the light does not enter; beyond its ancient stones the Dark Door waits, and the Paths of the Dead go under the mountain.
Green upland pastures climb to long spurs and sheer cliffs; the vale is fertile and the hills are high, and the mountain's shadow fills the head of the valley through most of the day.
A mountain vale of long light and early dusk — the sun leaves it soon, the lights come on early in the dwellings below, and the sound of the Morthond fills the evening.
The folk are herdsmen and high-farmers, mountain-men of Gondor; they keep the stone circles of the older world and do not speak of the wood at the valley's head.
Deep snow on the heights in winter, green water-meadows in spring; the cold comes down off the peaks before the light fails, and the river runs loud under icy banks.

land.name: Lebennin (Land of Five Rivers)
land.biome_hint: temperate fertile lowlands with mixed agriculture, river floodplains, boggy bottomland and mountain-fringe conifer forests
land.description: The heartland of Southern Gondor, a fertile central plain watered by the Gilnduin, Celos, Serni, Erui and their tributaries; the most populous and productive province, dominated by farmland with boggy bottomlands near the rivers and conifer-covered mountain valleys to the north.[file:73]

land.name: Dor-en-Ernil / Belfalas
land.biome_hint: rocky Mediterranean-type coast with mountain mineral wealth, pine forests and maritime influence
land.description: The rocky peninsula and coastal province of the Prince of Belfalas, containing the Ered Torthonion and the citadel of Dol Amroth; silver-rich mountains, the sacred kirinki birds and the Elven haven Edhellond define its character.[file:73]

land.name: Anfalas and Pinnath Gelin
land.biome_hint: low coastal plain with fens, salt marshes, fishing grounds and rolling highland pasture
land.description: A long, thin coastal land west of the Morthond with flat, waterlogged plains, fens and rich fishing grounds; the Pinnath Gelin highlands to the north support wool-producing sheep and a timber-mining economy.[file:73]

land.name: Lamedon
land.biome_hint: forested mountain vales and upland pastures with mineral-rich geology
land.description: Mountain province of the White Mountains rich in iron, copper and silver deposits; a militarized zone in early Third Age history, later transformed into a province supporting mining communities and highland farming.[file:73]

land.name: Cape of Andrast
land.biome_hint: wet Atlantic-type rocky cape with steep valleys, heavy rainfall and primitive settlement
land.description: The rugged, rain-battered westernmost cape of Southern Gondor where the White Mountains bend into the sea; steep-sided green valleys and bare peaks home to the Dunir (Orodbedhrim), essentially untouched by Gondorian civilization.[file:73]

land.name: Ethir Anduin (Great Delta)
land.biome_hint: subtropical-type estuarine delta with marshes, swamps, tidal channels and rich aquatic biodiversity
land.description: The vast, meandering delta of the Anduin where it meets the Bay of Belfalas, created by the Númenórean Downfall's Great Wave; a unique ecosystem of swamps, channels, marsh and tidal flats with crocodiles, fishing cats and swamp tribes.[file:73]

land.name: Tolfalas
land.biome_hint: geologically active island with volcanic soils, hot springs, endemic sacred trees and nesting sea turtles
land.description: A volcanic island in the Bay of Belfalas with dramatic topography, hot springs, active minor eruptions and the sacred oiolair trees; settlement has always been marginal due to geological instability.[file:73]

land.name: Bay of Belfalas
land.biome_hint: warm temperate sea with rich coastal fisheries, marine mammals, whale migration routes and volatile weather
land.description: The great bay forming the southern coast of Gondor, sitting on the continental shelf and rich in marine life; critical for trade, fishing and naval power but plagued by unpredictable storms and Corsair threats.[file:73]

facts.notes: Southern Gondor's natural environment has been extensively reshaped by Númenórean colonization; the biomes encoded here reflect the Third Age T.A. 1640 state, not a pristine natural landscape; the most 'wild' zones are the Cape of Andrast, Ethir Anduin delta, upper mountain vales and Tolfalas. Harondor (the arid plateau south of the Poros) is treated as a separate region.[file:73]

people.description: Southern Gondor is the most populous and civilized part of Gondor, dominated by Dúnedain nobility and the Daen-Dúnedain mixed population of the river plains, with Daen highlanders (Orodbedhrim) in the upland vales, swamp peoples in the Ethir Anduin, and Grey-elves at Edhellond.

phrases: The cold of Lamedon is a mountain cold sharpened by old dread — it pours off the high snows and stops at the black eaves of the Dimholt.
Lamedon in winter is a green vale gone grey — snow on the high fields, lights early in the windows, and the Blackroot running loud under its cold banks.
Snow wraps the upper vale and the feet of the White Mountains; the Morthond runs black between white banks, and the Dimholt is a dark mouth in the white.

aspect.en: Gramuz is a rugged northern wilderland region of Dor Rhunen, situated north of Dorwinion and south of the Iron Hills. It is characterized by undulating lowlands, rolling hills, and scattered mixed woodlands. It is a harsh frontier territory populated by semi-nomadic Easterling clans and hardy Northmen who struggle for survival against the bitter cold winds blowing from the northeast Sea of Rhûn.

rotation: Land of low hills and sparse woodland between Dorwinion and the Iron Hills. Cold northeast winds and semi-nomadic Easterling clans who survive by hunting, fishing and trading furs. A harsh frontier territory.
Gloomy pine and spruce on rolling hills, with the freezing bite of the Sea of Rhûn carried on every northeast wind. A place where men grow taciturn and the trees grow crooked.
Mixed woodland of larch and stubborn oak fills the valleys between Dorwinion and the Iron Hills, but the tundra crowds in from the north and wins a little more ground each century.
Low, rounded hills that offer no shelter from the wind. The rivers run brown and fast with snowmelt in spring, then drop to cold threads between exposed stones by autumn.
The cold arrives early and stays long. Snow on the high ground before the end of the first month of autumn; the ice on the rivers doesn't fully break until the third month of spring.

Semi-nomadic Easterling clans who trap and fish and move on. Their fires smell of pine resin and smoked fish; they leave little and take less, and they watch strangers with the patience of people who have survived worse.

land.name: Wilderlands of Dor Rhunen
land.biome_hint: rolling plains and scattered pine‑oak forests with freezing winds
land.description: Undulating lowlands and scattered forests lying north of the southern plains and south of the Iron Hills.

facts.notes: Gramuz forms a vital buffer zone between the Elven woodlands of Taur Romen and the Dwarven mines of Eorstan.

people.symbol: Eothrain: White Horse on a Green Field. Gramuz: A Golden Sheaf of Grain on an Umber Field.
people.military: 800 Eothraim Cavalry. 1,200 Eothraim Levy Cavalry. 75 Gramuz Warriors. 150 Gramuz Levy Warriors.
people.description: A melting pot of hardy Gramuz Northmen tribes and semi-nomadic Easterlings (Logath, Sagath, Odhriag).

aspect.en: Dor‑en‑Ernil, the Land of the Prince, is a princely fief in south‑central Gondor encompassing Belfalas and neighboring lowlands and highlands; ruled from the coastal city of Dol Amroth, it is famed for its White‑ships, Elven‑tinged nobility, and constant tension with Umbar and the Eredrim highlanders.

rotation: Southern Gondor's princely peninsula governed from Dol Amroth, city of white towers above the sea. Silver-rich mountains, rugged cliffs, Elvish-blooded nobility and the sacred kirinki birds make this the most singular land in Gondor.

The Dol Amroth peninsula, white towers above the sea and the silver-veined Ered Torthonion behind. The Prince of Belfalas rules from the most singular city in Gondor; the Elvish blood of the Swan Knights shows in their bearing.

Silver-rich mountains descend to a rocky coast of sea-caves and natural harbors. The kirinki birds nest in the sea-cliffs and their calls carry at dawn for a mile or more; there is no sound more particular to this land.
The headland juts into Belegaer with cliffs on three sides and the mountains closing the fourth. Dol Amroth sits at the exact point where the land and sea have decided they will share it equally.
Mediterranean in character: warm and dry in summer, mild and wet in winter. The White Mountains keep the worst of the north winds off; the sea moderates everything else.

The Swan Knights of Dol Amroth and the merchants who supply them. Elvish blood that shows in the height and the pale eyes; a dignity that is not arrogance but comes close enough to annoy the rest of Gondor.

land.name: Dor-en-Ernil
land.biome_hint: coastal hills and peninsulas with river valleys, deltas, and mountain spurs
land.description: Princely fief in south‑central Gondor between the Gilrain/Serni and Morthond/Ringló rivers, including Belfalas peninsula, coastal towns, inland river vales, and Ered Tarthonion highlands.

land.name: Belfalas
land.biome_hint: rugged coastal hills with cliffs, coves, and sea‑exposed slopes
land.description: Great, hilly peninsula in southern Gondor jutting into the Bay of Belfalas; sometimes used as an alternative name for the southern half of Dor‑en‑Ernil.

land.name: Bay of Belfalas
land.biome_hint: temperate open bay with strong winds, currents, and rich marine life
land.description: Broad bay south of Gondor whose waters carry White‑ships, Elven swan‑ships, and Corsair warships; filled with islets, shoals, tides, and storms that shape the region’s seafaring life.

land.name: Ered Tarthonion
land.biome_hint: steep pine‑covered mountains and high valleys
land.description: Highlands of Dor‑en‑Ernil, forming a transverse section of the White Mountain range that rises in central Belfalas; a rugged country of pine‑clad peaks and Eredrim villages.

land.name: Morthond and Edhellond
land.biome_hint: cool river and marshy delta emptying into a temperate bay
land.description: The Morthond, or Black‑root, rises by the Paths of the Dead in the White Mountains, flows past Erech, and enters the Bay of Belfalas; its delta hosts the Elf‑haven of Edhellond with tunnel‑harbors and swan‑ships.

facts.notes: This object treats Dor‑en‑Ernil as the broader Land of the Prince; sites like Dol Amroth, Linhir, Edhellond, and Castle Amrûnaur can be represented as separate site objects referencing this region.

people.description: Dor‑en‑Ernil’s population mixes Dúnedain princes and lowland commoners with Eredrim highlanders descended from the Daen Coentis, independent Elves of Edhellond, and sailors, merchants, privateers, smugglers, and Corsair enemies across the bay.

source.supplement: Havens of Gondor: Land of Belfalas

aspect.en: Dunland is the rugged foothill and plateau country south of the Glanduin, east of the Gwathló and north of the Isen, a land of highlands and plains ruled by fractious Dunlending clans who herd, raid and scheme along the vital Old South Road and the Isen Gap.

rotation: Wild land between the Gwathló and the Isen, of heathland, peat bogs and low oaks. Depopulated since the wars of the north, the Gwathuirim tribes survive at its margins. A landscape of bleak beauty under vast Atlantic skies.

Heathland and peat bog under Atlantic skies, almost entirely depopulated since the northern wars. The Gwathuirim cling to its margins; the interior is open, bleak and genuinely beautiful in the right light.

What the Númenóreans and then Sauron didn't fell, the climate finished: Enedhwaith is now low oak and heather on rolling ground, with bogs filling the valley-bottoms. The forest is coming back, slowly, on its own terms.

The Gwathló runs the eastern edge and the Isen cuts the south; between them the land does what it likes. No roads are maintained here; only sheep-tracks and the routes the Gwathuirim memorised generations ago.
Relentless Atlantic weather that makes every season an argument. The mild temperature means it doesn't snow often, but the damp and wind are constant. The light has a particular quality in autumn.
Gwathuirim tribes on the fringes, herding and keeping themselves to themselves. They have no use for either Gondor or Rohan; their ancestral memory stretches back to before either existed.

land.name: Dunland Highlands
land.biome_hint: cool hills and ridges with mixed forest and pasture
land.description: Eastern highland zone backed by the southern Misty Mountains, with hills and ridges up to about twelve hundred feet, running in orderly lines and breaking westward into mesa‑like hills with flat tops and steep sides.[file:32]

land.name: Dunland Plains and Gwathló basin edge
land.biome_hint: temperate grasslands with scattered trees and marsh fringes
land.description: Western plateaus and low rolling hills that step down over fifty miles into the flat plains of the wide Gwathló basin, mostly grassy and nearly treeless except near settlements and stream corridors.[file:32]

land.name: Old South Road (Tiar Hariar)
land.biome_hint: engineered road across plateau edge and river valleys
land.description: The major highway skirting Dunland’s southern border, running east–west along the plateau edge from Tharbad toward the Isen Gap, carrying trade and travelers through Larach Duhnnan and clan territories.[file:32]

land.name: Larach Duhnnan
land.biome_hint: market town in upland valley with river and road access
land.description: Largest town of Dunland, built on a plateau overlooking the Dunstrem and the Old South Road, surrounded by an embankment with clan Feargan’s fortified hold on a raised hill; serves as main trade hub and neutral meeting‑ground for multiple clans.[file:32]

land.name: Caerdh Wood
land.biome_hint: cool mixed old forest in foothill basin
land.description: One of only two true forests in Dunland, a remnant of the primordial woods, considered mysterious and possibly haunted; hosts Daen Coentis temple‑observatories and three Drúedain villages.[file:32]

land.name: New Maresh marshes
land.biome_hint: freshwater marsh with raised hillocks and slow streams
land.description: Marshy area draining into the Dunstrem near its junction with the Gwathló, with hills rising above the wetlands to hold Stoor burrows and channels navigated by small boats among patches of quicksand.[file:32]

land.name: Temple of Justice valley
land.biome_hint: forested valley with religious complex and defensive works
land.description: A long dead‑end wooded valley about twenty‑five miles east‑south‑east of Cillien where the dark granite Temple of Justice stands on a low hill, with a stream and bridge at its mouth and steep walls guarded by lookout posts.[file:32]

facts.notes: Keep this Dunland object strictly for the foothills, plateaus, plains and valleys north of the Old South Road and below the alpine zone; the Southern Misty Mountains object above covers the high peaks and explicitly mountain-only flora, fauna and powers.[file:32]

people.military: Each Chief keeps from 100-400 Warriors as a permanent retinue. Each Clan can also raise 1,400-3,200 Warriors given 1-4 weeks. Tribes favor light armor and carry spears and melee weapons predominately.
people.description: Dunland is dominated by Dunlendings—Daen Lintis highlanders descended from the Daen Coentis—living in extended family bands within clans, but also includes Dúnedain estates, Stoors, Drúedain in Caerdh Wood, organized traders, bards, healers and a powerful Dark‑influenced Temple hierarchy.

source.supplement: Dunland and the Southern Misty Mountains

aspect.en: Lindon is the westernmost Elvish realm of Middle-earth, the remnant of Ossiriand that survived the War of Wrath. After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Dark isle off the northern coast of Forlindon, remnant of the highlands of Beleriand drowned beneath the waves. Black vertical cliffs, cold peat bogs of perpetual mist and the melancholy echo of a land lost under Belegaer.

Dark island off northern Forlindon, all vertical basalt cliffs and cold peat bog. What Beleriand was before it drowned is all that Tol Fuin is now — the highest peaks of a lost kingdom, still above water, still trying to remember.

Seabird colonies on every ledge of every cliff face; peat bogs inland that are permanently waterlogged; wind that comes off Belegaer without interruption for a thousand miles. A place of austere, waterlogged beauty.

The island barely rises above the sea in the south, where salt marsh grades into shore. The northern cliffs are thirty metres of pure black basalt. Nothing explains the difference except the island's own strange geology.

Cold, wet, and windy all year round. The sea moderates the temperature so it's never extreme, but it never gets genuinely warm either. The bogs are frozen at the surface for a few months in deepest winter.
No permanent settlement. Sea-birds, seals on the southern beaches, and the particular melancholy of a place that was part of something larger before the sea came.

land.name: Forlindon (North Lindon)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate coastal and lowland zone with maritime influence transitioning to colder mountain foothills
land.description: The northern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, including coastal plains and the northern Blue Mountain foothills. Historically the primary home of the Noldor (Godhellim) in the realm, it contains harbors and settlements connected to Mithlond and is treated in the government section as a distinct administrative region.[file:99]

land.name: Harlindon (South Lindon)
land.biome_hint: mild, wet coastal strip with forests and rural Elven settlements around secondary harbors
land.description: The southern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, associated with Sindar and Laiquendi (Iathrim, Laegrim). It combines coastal stretches and forested lowlands, was once a fief under Celeborn, and is portrayed as more rural and woodland-oriented than Forlindon.[file:99]

land.name: Rhûnlindon (east-of-Lhûn / Blue Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cool to cold mountain zone with conifer forests, winter snow and extensive mining
land.description: The part of Lindon’s sphere east of the River Lhûn, including the eastern Blue Mountains with Dwarven halls and some Elven refuges. Population tables assign Rhûnlindon about 10% of Lindon’s population, with climate corresponding to the Ered Luin band (colder winters, moderate summers, 30–40 inches of precipitation).[^file99]

land.name: Mithlond (Grey Havens)
land.biome_hint: maritime urban enclave with sheltered harbor, mild wet climate and intensive shipbuilding
land.description: The principal harbor city at the head of the Gulf of Lhûn, seat of Círdan in the Third Age and the main port for Elves and Ring-bearers departing to Valinor. Population tables show Mithlond comprising 20–25% of Lindon’s inhabitants in the Third Age (and 9–10% in the Second Age), emphasizing its central role in Lindon’s demography and economy.[file:99]

land.name: Taeg Lindon routes and refuges
land.biome_hint: mixed grassland, forest and hill country between the Misty Mountains and the Ered Luin, with hidden Elven refuges
land.description: The 'Bounds of Lindon' section describes the Wandering Companies’ preferred route from Imladris to Mithlond: across Eregion, the Mitheithel ford south of Fennas Drúnin, the South Downs and Barrow-downs (with stops near Tom Bombadil’s house), then either through the Old Forest and Green Hills or along the Brandywine’s eastern shore before turning west to the Ered Luin. Along roughly 600 miles they maintain rustic camps and more elaborate permanent refuges (glades, caves, small houses) 20–30 miles apart, some shared with Rangers after the fall of Arthedain.[file:99]

facts.notes: This Lindon work is an unlicensed, non-commercial fan-made Realm (version 3.2, 2023) rather than an original ICE product, but it is structured like a MERP Realm and synthesizes Tolkien canon with MERP-style material. For your Middle-earth-on-Europe map, Lindon should be treated as one macro-region with internal subregions (Forlindon, Harlindon, Rhûnlindon) sharing a maritime temperate climate, and Mithlond explicitly marked as a major harbor node. Climate numbers (temperature ranges and precipitation) from the Traveller’s Guide can be mapped directly onto your climate system for coastal vs mountain bands, while the Wandering Companies’ route description provides a canonical overland corridor from Imladris to the Grey Havens for your path and distance calculations.[file:99] Eerily beautiful remnants of Beleriand, characterized by rugged coastal hills, fertile valleys, and evergreen forests. A light rain, drizzle, or ethereal fog falls on most days of the year, allowing mosses, ferns, firs, and spruce to thrive.

people.symbol: Círdan's Device: A White Pelannun on a Blue Field
people.military: 2,000 Warriors and Sailors (Forlindon: 800 Warriors/Sailors, 800 Levy. Harlindon: 1,200 Sailors/Warriors, 800 Militia).
people.description: Lindon’s population is overwhelmingly Elvish, composed of multiple lineages (Noldor, Sindar, Laiquendi, Nandor, Falathrim) under Gil-galad and later Círdan, with a significant Dwarven presence in the Blue Mountains and peripheral contact with Men and Hobbits via routes and harbors. The Traveller’s Guide provides detailed population tables showing long-term decline through the Third Age.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

aspect.en: Lebennin, the Place of Five Waters, is the rich, river-laced heartland of Gondor between the White Mountains and the Anduin, a fertile province of rolling fields, busy ports and Sea-lords whose fleets fight Corsairs and smugglers across the Bay of Belfalas.

rotation: Volcanic island in the Bay of Belfalas with peaks, fumaroles and hot springs. The sacred oiolair trees grow only here; sea turtles nest on its dark beaches. Dramatic beauty and geological instability in equal measure.
Volcanic island in the Bay of Belfalas, with hot springs, fumaroles and the dark oiolair trees that grow nowhere else in the world. The geology is unstable; the beauty is extreme.

The oiolair trees rise thirty feet from their own heat, flowering year-round from the warmth of the volcanic ground. Sea turtles nest on the black beaches each summer without fail; the combination makes this island unlike any other place.

Peaks visible from the Gondorian coast on clear days, with steam rising from the flanks. The beaches are black volcanic sand that burns the foot in summer; the sea around them turns turquoise in shallow water.
The volcanic interior keeps the island warmer than the surrounding sea; the coastal strip is almost tropical by Gondorian standards. The centre is unpredictable — fumaroles vent without warning.
No permanent population, and Gondor has never quite decided what to do with it. Scholars visit for the oiolair trees; fishermen use the sheltered coves; the island has its own agenda.

land.name: Lebennin proper – Place of Five Waters
land.biome_hint: fertile temperate lowlands cut by multiple rivers
land.description: The central province of Gondor bounded by the White Mountains to the north, Gilrain and Dor-en-Ernil to the west, the Anduin and South Ithilien to the east, and the Bay of Belfalas and Ethir Anduin to the south, defined by five cool rivers rising in the gleaming Ered Nimrais.[file:30]

land.name: White Mountains (Ered Nimrais) above Lebennin
land.biome_hint: alpine highlands with snow peaks and forested lower vales
land.description: Snow-capped mountains forming the northern boundary of Lebennin, with gleaming peaks, remote vales, Daen and Drúedain sites, and passes leading toward Dunharrow and other ancient highland centers.[file:30]

land.name: Bay of Belfalas and coastal fringe
land.biome_hint: temperate sea-coast with bays, shoals and busy shipping lanes
land.description: Lebennin’s southern edge meets the Bay of Belfalas, where numerous ships crowd the waters off its ports, smugglers and Corsairs prowl, and storms and reefs challenge even skilled Gondorian captains.[file:30]

land.name: Ethir Anduin
land.biome_hint: large river delta with brackish marsh and sandbars
land.description: The swampy delta and marshy flanks at the mouth of the Anduin, a maze of shifting channels and shoals where smugglers avoid royal duties and Haradrim and Corsairs hunt among unpredictable waters.[file:30]

land.name: Pelargir
land.biome_hint: major river-port city on broad temperate river
land.description: The great port city on the Anduin founded in S.A. 2350 by the Faithful, oldest city of Gondor, capital of Lebennin and home of the Royal Fleet, the finest harbor in the kingdom and a focal point in the war against Corsairs.[file:30]

land.name: Balimur Swamps and Balibogach
land.biome_hint: freshwater marsh with narrow channels and smuggler paths
land.description: Marshy region associated with smugglers’ stronghold Balibogach in southern Lebennin, where Balimur Runner boats with shallow draft slip along hidden waterways.[file:30]

land.name: Road network – Gondor Road and coastal routes
land.biome_hint: well-travelled roads across rolling farmland and river crossings
land.description: The Gondor Road runs through Lebennin to Linhir and points west, with busy inns along the routes to Dol Amroth and Lamedon; traffic remains brisk despite raids and war.[file:30]

facts.notes: This Lebennin object treats the province as the central Gondorian coastal heartland described in Sea-Lords of Gondor, suitable as a single climatic and cultural region node: sub-areas like Pelargir’s urban districts, Balimur Swamps or individual mountain valleys can be broken out later as separate region or site objects if you want finer resolution.[file:30]

people.description: Lebennin’s population is a layered mix: Númenórean-descended Dúnedain and urban Gondorians in the cities and ports, rural folk and Dunnish highlanders in the uplands, Drúedain in remote mountain valleys, Marshmen in the Ethir Anduin, and a constant presence of Sea-lords, sailors and smugglers bound up with the Bay of Belfalas.

aspect.en: The Grey Mountains (Ered Mithrin) form a long, cold northern range between Mirkwood and the Forodwaith, with abrupt cliffs above the Wilderland, gentler northern slopes fading into tundra and the Talath Oiohelka, and the dragon-haunted basin of the Withered Heath between the eastern forks of the range.

rotation: System of low hills east of Mirkwood, worked by Dwarves for iron, coal and silver. Gallery mouths in the hillsides, smelter slag heaps and beneath it all a Dwarven city of workshops and subterranean markets of hard steel.

Gallery mouths in dark ore-bearing hillsides, slag heaps cooling in the rain and the constant smell of hot metal. The Dwarves have worked these hills for centuries; the landscape shows it in every face of exposed stone.

Dragon Grass grows in the hollows of the Withered Heath to the north — tall, dry and rattling in the wind, its hollow stalks eight feet high. Silver firs on the sheltered slopes; everything else is rock and ore and frost.

The Narrows between Mirkwood and the Grey Mountains: a strip of relatively sheltered valley where the young River Running runs clear over gravel and the forest thins enough to let in light. The hills press in on both sides.
Arctic summers and long dark winters on the northern slopes; the Narrows are milder but cold enough that the mines keep the workers alive better than the open air does in January.

Dwarves who have been here long enough that the hills are an extension of themselves. Outsiders are tolerated to the degree that they are useful; the Dwarven markets under the hills have their own economy that the surface barely touches.

land.name: Grey Mountains (Ered Mithrin)
land.biome_hint: high cold mountains with snowfields, glaciers, conifer slopes and sheer southern cliffs
land.description: A long mountain chain north of Mirkwood with peaks mostly around 5000 feet, Mount Gondmaeglom reaching 10,720 feet and more than 50 miles in diameter; southern faces rise abruptly in sheer cliffs over the Wilderland, while northern slopes grade into the Talath Oiohelka.[file:38]

land.name: The Narrows (Q. Arka)
land.biome_hint: cool temperate valley with river, fields, scattered woods and frequent snow
land.description: A thin strip of land between Mirkwood and the Grey Mountains where forest and mountains almost meet, centered on the broad, flat-bottomed valley of the young Forest River (Taurduin); relatively sheltered, arable and rich in wildlife despite a short growing season.[file:38]

land.name: Talath Oiohelka (Plain of Ever-ice)
land.biome_hint: arctic plain with permafrost, ice fissures, patterned ground and minimal vegetation
land.description: The broken, ice-covered plain north of the Grey Mountains, dotted with tortured hills and deep crevasses—remnants of the Iron Mountains—and permafrost polygons and patterned ground formed by freeze–thaw cycles.[file:38]

land.name: Withered Heath
land.biome_hint: cold, partially frozen basin with dragon-scarred ground, seasonal bogs and limited grass cover
land.description: A vast, desolate basin between the two eastern forks of the Grey Mountains, pitted and scarred by dragon battles, underlain by former swampland and now full of treacherous mud pockets and seasonal slush when snowmelt partially reverts it to swamp; primary breeding and lairing ground for the region’s dragons.[file:38]

land.name: Northern Waste (Forodwaith fringe)
land.biome_hint: rocky tundra with moss/lichen cover, sparse grasses and extreme weather
land.description: The tundra zone between the northern foothills and Talath Oiohelka, composed of barren rocky ground with mosses, lichens and hardy grasses, punctuated by ancient Morgothic Orc-hold ruins that offer rare shelter in an otherwise deadly land.[file:38]

land.name: Forest River (Taurduin) headwaters
land.biome_hint: steep mountain river gorge with waterfalls and conifer-lined banks
land.description: The beginnings of the Forest River issuing from under the mountains, cutting a deep rift and forming features such as Steel Fall, a several-hundred-foot cascading waterfall, before flowing into the Narrows.[file:38]

land.name: Mithlin forks and Langwell confluence
land.biome_hint: cold headwaters and confluences in mountainous, glacially carved terrain
land.description: The two forks of the Mithlin rise in the Grey Mountains and join the Langwell to form the upper Anduin, creating a critical hydrological link between the Ered Mithrin and the greater river system of Middle-earth.[file:38]

facts.notes: This object treats the Grey Mountains, Narrows, Northern Waste fringe and Withered Heath as a single climatic and ecological unit centered on the Ered Mithrin and its dragon-haunted basin; specific Dwarven holds (Silverplunge, Thunderclift, Norr-dum, Silverpit), Beorning manors, Ice-orc Kala Dulakurth and named dragon lairs such as Steel Fall or Anvilmount can be modeled as separate site objects where finer resolution is needed.[file:38]

people.military: 150 Professional Warriors, many mounted. 150-200 drilled militia troops. 300-500 raw levy, used only in emergencies and takes 2-5 weeks to raise.
people.description: The Grey Mountains region is sparsely populated but contested by Beornings in the Narrows, Dwarves of Durin’s folk in mining colonies, Ice-orcs in northern fortresses and outposts, and several Orc tribes in passes and foothills, with Dragons, Undead and agents of Angmar and Gundabad influencing politics and warfare.[file:38]

aspect.en: The Grey Mountains (Ered Mithrin) form a long, cold northern range between Mirkwood and the Forodwaith, with abrupt cliffs above the Wilderland, gentler northern slopes fading into tundra and the Talath Oiohelka, and the dragon-haunted basin of the Withered Heath between the eastern forks of the range.

rotation: The valley of the Lonely Mountain — green fields and a walled town rebuilt where a dragon's desolation once lay grey for miles. Erebor's peak stands over all, and the River Running comes down beside the gate.

Young pine and rowan clothe the slopes where the old burning was; the scars in the rock are still visible above the new green. Ravens keep their watch on Ravenhill as they did when the Mountain was a kingdom.
The road to the Front Gate runs beside the river under the Mountain's shadow; below, the valley opens to the plain where the grey ruins of the old town were a warning for an age.
A mountain valley of sharp seasons — deep snow in winter, green flood of growth in spring, and the cold shade of the peak even at midsummer.
Men of Dale and dwarves of the Mountain share the valley; the sound of hammers comes up from the forges under the hill, and the town prospers again under the King under the Mountain.
South and west the land was once burned bare; now the woods creep back year by year, and the memory of the fire is a grey line in the stone.

phrases: Dale under winter is a white valley beneath a white Mountain; the river runs dark between ice-rimmed banks, and the old desolation is buried clean.
Snow on Dale hides the old scars; the valley is a white sea around the grey island of the Mountain, and the raven-call is the only sound.
The cold of Dale is the Mountain's breath — it comes down off the high snows and pools in the valley, and the raven-guards huddle on their ridge.

aspect.en: Ronalindon is a serene coastal subregion of Harlindon situated along the shores of the Gulf of Lhûn and Belegaer. Famed for its peaceful forest glades, quiet river estuaries, and coastal mudflats, it represents a pristine maritime-woodland environment where Elves live in harmony with both the forest and the sea. Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Southern coast of the Gulf of Lhûn where oak and ash forests reach down to the water. Labyrinthine tidal estuaries, otters among the roots and Elves who build light boats to sail the calm gulf.

Southern Lindon coast where oak and ash reach the water of the Gulf of Lhûn. Labyrinthine tidal inlets where otters hunt and Elves who build light boats can disappear into the estuary system for days.

Dense coastal forest with a damp, ferny understorey; the tidal estuaries make the distinction between land and sea ambiguous the same way estuaries everywhere do. The Elves here have built with that ambiguity rather than against it.
The southern shore of the Gulf curves gently; the water is calm enough for small boats year-round and the inlet maze provides shelter even in the worst of the Atlantic storms.
Milder than northern Lindon, with the Gulf of Lhûn acting as a heat reservoir. Winters are damp rather than cold; summers pleasant without being warm. The prevailing mood is grey-green and quiet.

Sindar Elves who have been here since before the First Age ended and have had time to decide exactly how they want to live. Their interaction with outsiders is courteous and minimal; the estuary system is theirs.

land.name: Ronalindon Estuaries
land.biome_hint: coastal wetland and river estuaries with high humidity and poplars
land.description: Quiet river estuaries and tidal marshes emptying into the Gulf of Lhûn.

facts.notes: Ronalindon is a deeply spiritual and peaceful retreat for sea-yearning Elves before they depart from the Grey Havens. Eerily beautiful remnants of Beleriand, characterized by rugged coastal hills, fertile valleys, and evergreen forests. A light rain, drizzle, or ethereal fog falls on most days of the year, allowing mosses, ferns, firs, and spruce to thrive.

people.symbol: Círdan's Device: A White Pelannun on a Blue Field
people.military: 2,000 Warriors and Sailors (Forlindon: 800 Warriors/Sailors, 800 Levy. Harlindon: 1,200 Sailors/Warriors, 800 Militia).
people.description: A quiet, sparse population of Laiquendi and Falathrim Elves who lead simple, maritime-focused lives.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

aspect.en: Ered Luin, also known as the Blue Mountains, is an ancient mountain range separating Lindon from Eriador. Extending 590 miles from the Ice Bay of Forochel down to Orod Elu in the south, the range is formed of grey rock with a bluish tint caused by a high concentration of copper ores. The mountains are riddled with natural caverns, marble and limestone formations, and once held precious metals, though Dwarvish mining has left them depleted of gold except for minor remote veins. Geology consists of marble and limestone with folded sandstone and shale foothills. abundant copper, iron, and tin ores are actively mined by the dwarves (naugrim).

rotation: The Blue Mountains and green Lindon between them and the Sea — the last piece of drowned Beleriand, split by the Gulf of Lhûn where the water comes far inland.
Tall pine-woods and oakwoods on the seaward slopes, older than any other living woods in the west. The range itself is old and worn, its peaks low and blue in the sea-haze.
West of the gulf lie the Grey Havens and the white quays; the ships that leave them do not return. The road to the water is the oldest road still travelled.
Dwarf-halls and elven havens share the land — the mountains hold the mansions of old Nogrod's kin, and the coast keeps the last ports of the Eldar.
Sea-weather rules here — long grey rains, salt wind, snow that lies long on the high moors but rarely in the sheltered vales.
Everything in Lindon smells of the Sea; even the mountain streams run with a salt wind behind them, and the sunsets over the water are the last sight of the world.

land.name: Northern Ered Luin peaks
land.biome_hint: alpine peaks with year-round ice caps and glaciers
land.description: The taller northern section of the range, home to the peak of Lossotil (9,497 feet) and several glacial ice fields.

land.name: Southern Ered Luin peaks
land.biome_hint: sub-alpine peaks with seasonal winter snow
land.description: The lower southern section of the range, including Orod Elu (6,824 feet), which experiences seasonal winter snow cover.

facts.notes: Ered Luin stands as a vital mining zone and barrier separating Lindon from Eriador, with secret, rune-guarded passes. The Blue Mountains are ancient and run north-to-south, heavily composed of marble and limestone with massive natural caverns. Snowfields and icecaps are present year-round on the northern range, while pine trees disappear over 5,000 feet. Mineral copper deposits give the peaks their bluish tint.

people.symbol: A Hammer surmounted by Three Tongues of Flame
people.military: 490 Warriors. 2,100 Warrior Levy.
people.description: The Ered Luin is primarily inhabited by the Dwarves of Nogrod and Belegost's descendants, alongside scattered Elven wanderers and mountain Giants.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

facts.products: Finished goods, iron, tin, copper, lead.

phrases: Winter on the Blue Mountains is the Sea's winter — grey water, white ridges, and a wind that has come a thousand miles over the waves.
Rain on Lindon is the Sea sent over the mountains — long grey veils, dripping woods, and the white road to the Havens running wet.
The cold here is a salt cold off the Sea; it fills the gulf and climbs the blue slopes, and the ships at the Havens tug at their moorings in the ice-wind.

aspect.en: Lindon is the westernmost Elvish realm of Middle-earth, the remnant of Ossiriand that survived the War of Wrath. After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Inner northern hills of Harlindon where old oaks and birches reach gold in autumn and the Sindar Elves live in quiet contemplation. The sea is heard but not seen here, lending this land its gentle melancholy.

Inner hills of northern Harlindon with old oaks turning gold in autumn. The Sindar here live in quiet contemplation of a sea heard but not seen; the rolling of the water reaches them as sound without sight.

Oak and birch on the inner hillsides, with bracken in autumn and spring wildflowers in the clearings. The Elvish settlements are built low and integrated into the slope so that they read as landscape rather than architecture.

Rounded hills with the Ered Luin visible to the east and the Gulf of Lhûn to the west as a line of light between the hills. The distance from the sea is the defining quality here — present but not immediate.
Cooler and wetter than the southern Harlindon coast, with autumn arriving early enough to make the gold leaves genuinely dramatic. The Sindar who chose this location chose well.
Noldor and Sindar Elves who came here after the War of Wrath and have been here since, which means they've had time to become the landscape rather than just inhabiting it.

land.name: Forlindon (North Lindon)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate coastal and lowland zone with maritime influence transitioning to colder mountain foothills
land.description: The northern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, including coastal plains and the northern Blue Mountain foothills. Historically the primary home of the Noldor (Godhellim) in the realm, it contains harbors and settlements connected to Mithlond and is treated in the government section as a distinct administrative region.[file:99]

land.name: Harlindon (South Lindon)
land.biome_hint: mild, wet coastal strip with forests and rural Elven settlements around secondary harbors
land.description: The southern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, associated with Sindar and Laiquendi (Iathrim, Laegrim). It combines coastal stretches and forested lowlands, was once a fief under Celeborn, and is portrayed as more rural and woodland-oriented than Forlindon.[file:99]

land.name: Rhûnlindon (east-of-Lhûn / Blue Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cool to cold mountain zone with conifer forests, winter snow and extensive mining
land.description: The part of Lindon’s sphere east of the River Lhûn, including the eastern Blue Mountains with Dwarven halls and some Elven refuges. Population tables assign Rhûnlindon about 10% of Lindon’s population, with climate corresponding to the Ered Luin band (colder winters, moderate summers, 30–40 inches of precipitation).[^file99]

land.name: Mithlond (Grey Havens)
land.biome_hint: maritime urban enclave with sheltered harbor, mild wet climate and intensive shipbuilding
land.description: The principal harbor city at the head of the Gulf of Lhûn, seat of Círdan in the Third Age and the main port for Elves and Ring-bearers departing to Valinor. Population tables show Mithlond comprising 20–25% of Lindon’s inhabitants in the Third Age (and 9–10% in the Second Age), emphasizing its central role in Lindon’s demography and economy.[file:99]

land.name: Taeg Lindon routes and refuges
land.biome_hint: mixed grassland, forest and hill country between the Misty Mountains and the Ered Luin, with hidden Elven refuges
land.description: The 'Bounds of Lindon' section describes the Wandering Companies’ preferred route from Imladris to Mithlond: across Eregion, the Mitheithel ford south of Fennas Drúnin, the South Downs and Barrow-downs (with stops near Tom Bombadil’s house), then either through the Old Forest and Green Hills or along the Brandywine’s eastern shore before turning west to the Ered Luin. Along roughly 600 miles they maintain rustic camps and more elaborate permanent refuges (glades, caves, small houses) 20–30 miles apart, some shared with Rangers after the fall of Arthedain.[file:99]

facts.notes: This Lindon work is an unlicensed, non-commercial fan-made Realm (version 3.2, 2023) rather than an original ICE product, but it is structured like a MERP Realm and synthesizes Tolkien canon with MERP-style material. For your Middle-earth-on-Europe map, Lindon should be treated as one macro-region with internal subregions (Forlindon, Harlindon, Rhûnlindon) sharing a maritime temperate climate, and Mithlond explicitly marked as a major harbor node. Climate numbers (temperature ranges and precipitation) from the Traveller’s Guide can be mapped directly onto your climate system for coastal vs mountain bands, while the Wandering Companies’ route description provides a canonical overland corridor from Imladris to the Grey Havens for your path and distance calculations.[file:99] Eerily beautiful remnants of Beleriand, characterized by rugged coastal hills, fertile valleys, and evergreen forests. A light rain, drizzle, or ethereal fog falls on most days of the year, allowing mosses, ferns, firs, and spruce to thrive.
