people.military: 2,000 Warriors and Sailors (Forlindon: 800 Warriors/Sailors, 800 Levy. Harlindon: 1,200 Sailors/Warriors, 800 Militia).
people.description: Lindon’s population is overwhelmingly Elvish, composed of multiple lineages (Noldor, Sindar, Laiquendi, Nandor, Falathrim) under Gil-galad and later Círdan, with a significant Dwarven presence in the Blue Mountains and peripheral contact with Men and Hobbits via routes and harbors. The Traveller’s Guide provides detailed population tables showing long-term decline through the Third Age.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

aspect.en: The Belegaer, or Great Sea, is the vast ocean separating Middle-earth (Endor) from the Undying Lands of Aman in the far West. In the coastal domains of Lindon, Arnor, and Gondor, it comprises key areas such as the Gulf of Lhûn (Nen Lhûn) and the Bay of Belfalas (Nen Belfalas). The deep gulf of Nen Lhûn, formed in the cataclysms of the First Age, serves as the calm and misty harbor for the Elven ships sailing from Mithlond, rich in salmon, lobsters, and shellfish. Further south, the vast Bay of Belfalas rests on Endor's continental shelf, driven by the warm, counterclockwise Southron Stream which collides with the cold Great Stream off the Cape of Andrast, creating turbulent, dangerous waters home to sharks, grey sperm whales, and giant squids.

rotation: The Great Sea — grey and boundless water west of all lands, where the waves sigh and murmur against the shores of Middle-earth without ceasing.
Out of the Havens the white ships take the Straight Road west; for all else the sea is a wall of distance and a road without end.
Grey water, salt wind, and the wheeling of sea-birds. The light here is the light of the West — pale, clean, and very old.
Storm-wracked in winter, broad and glimmering in summer. The sea keeps its own season and its own law, and the shore is only where it begins.
Sea-birds beat upstream against the breeze where the great rivers come down; the sound of the surf is the oldest sound in the world.
Westward the water runs to the world's rim. Men may sail it and return; the Elves sail it and do not.

land.name: Gulf of Lhûn
land.biome_hint: deep gulf with rocky coastal cliffs and heavy fog
land.description: The deep, misty gulf cutting through the Blue Mountains.

land.name: Bay of Belfalas
land.biome_hint: warm bay with sandy beaches and seasonal hurricanes
land.description: The great warm-water bay washing the southern shores of Gondor.

facts.notes: A gateway to the Undying Lands, which can only be reached by Elven ships sailing along the Straight Road.

people.military: Elven guard ships, Gondor fleet squads, Corsair war-dromunds.
people.description: Traversed primarily by Elven ships sailing West, Gondorian merchants, and Haradrim/Corsair raiders.

phrases: Belegaer under winter is a vast grey engine — cold wind, marching waves, and the long dark of the Sea at the end of all lands.
Rain on the Sea is a grey union of sky and water; the horizon is lost, and the ship is a white mote in a weeping world.

aspect.en: Southern Mirkwood and Southern Rhovanion form a wild, embattled region stretching from the Old Forest Road down to the Dagorlad and the Emyn Muil, dominated by the dark forest around Dol Guldur, the horse-plains of Talath Harroch, and the Anduin vales and Brown Lands that lie between Mirkwood and Gondor. Geology consists of primarily sedimentary strata of limestone and shale, with significant granite projections such as the cinder cone of amon lanc and the mountains of mirkwood.

rotation: Southern Mirkwood — the dark wood grown darker since the Shadow came to Dol Guldur. Trees bent together into arches, a green dimness beneath, and paths that end where the forest wills.
The ground is carpeted in roots and fungi; the air is thick and still. Under the canopy the quiet is so deep that a footstep sounds like a drum.
The Elf-path is the one safe way — a narrow line of beaten earth that the forest tolerates. Off it, the trails lie, the streams are black, and sleep itself is dangerous.
About the naked hill where the Necromancer dwelt the trees grow twisted even for this wood; the forest remembers the darkness and leans toward its ruin.
In summer the heat under the canopy is still and rank; in winter the cold seeps up from the roots. The wood has its own weather and it is never kind.
Spiders and darker things hold the deep wood; the free folk keep to the path and the fringes, and the forest's heart belongs to no one who walks on two legs.

land.name: Angaladadh (Northwest quadrant)
land.biome_hint: dense temperate hardwood–evergreen forest with heavy undergrowth
land.description: The deep northern heart of Southern Mirkwood’s forest, north-west of Dol Guldur, where the canopy remains thick, the old rose-tree circles still stand and Elven influence is strongest.

land.name: Aur Esgalabar / Romeniaur (Northeast quadrant)
land.biome_hint: mosaic of forest edge, scrub and plains
land.description: The northeastern wedge where the forest thins and gives way to grassland and the East Bight, mixing woodland, scrub and open country.

land.name: Talath Harroch (The Plains)
land.biome_hint: cool temperate grassland and farmland with scattered homesteads
land.description: The broad plains southeast of Mirkwood, home to horse-herding Northmen, wild herds and culcarnix, with long snowy winters and violent spring rains.

land.name: Nan Lothanduin / Nan Anduin
land.biome_hint: broad river valley with alluvial fields, groves and settlements
land.description: The Anduin vales south of the Old Forest Road and opposite Dol Guldur, containing fertile pockets such as Tharlorien, the North and South Undeeps and Beijabar holdings.

land.name: Dol Guldur (Amon Lanc)
land.biome_hint: rocky volcanic hill with dead trees and corrupted scrub
land.description: A stark, 3649‑foot volcanic cone on the southern eaves of Mirkwood, crowned and ringed by fortress walls and towers, once called the Naked Hill and now the hill of sorcery under Sauron’s control.

land.name: Emyn Guldur (Hills of Sorcery)
land.biome_hint: rocky hills with dark forest patches, caves and cliffs
land.description: Rugged hills and broken country around Dol Guldur, full of caves and shelves where spiders and fell beasts lair, and criss-crossed by secret Orc-paths.

land.name: Old Forest Road (southern sector)
land.biome_hint: forest-margin road through mixed woodland and clearings
land.description: The east–west road along the northern edge of Southern Rhovanion, carrying refugees and trade and linking the western vales with the eastern plains and forest entries.

land.name: Road to the Morannon
land.biome_hint: long overland route across river-vales and dry hills
land.description: The main north–south route from Nan Anduin across the Brown Lands toward the Black Gate, used increasingly by Sauron’s forces shifting from Dol Guldur to Mordor.

land.name: North and South Undeep
land.biome_hint: wide, shallow river reaches with rocky beds and down-like hills
land.description: Shallow fords of the Anduin where the river spreads over rock shelves, forming strategic crossing-points guarded and contested by Gondor and its enemies.

land.name: Brown Lands
land.biome_hint: dry temperate steppe on old terraced hills
land.description: Bleak, brown hills east of the Anduin whose ridges were once raised and irrigated garden beds tended by the Entwives, now covered in short dry grass and scarred by frost and neglect.

facts.notes: This object treats Southern Mirkwood and Southern Rhovanion as a single strategic and ecological unit in T.A. 1640: the haunted southern forest around Dol Guldur, the Talath Harroch horse-plains, the Anduin vales and Brown Lands, and the human and inhuman powers contesting them; individual sites such as Woodmen-town, Rhosgobel, Thorontir and Dol Guldur’s detailed layouts can be represented as separate site objects if needed. The largest forest in western Endor, dominated by oaks, maples, elms, and conifers. It has fallen under a stagnant, heavy shadow since the Necromancer established Dol Guldur, making southern reaches twisted, dark, and home to giant spiders.

people.military: 650 Warriors, led by local chieftains.
people.description: Southern Rhovanion is a country under siege: Beijabar and Wood-men cling to the western eaves, horse-lords and Gramuz Northmen fight for survival on the Talath Harroch, Gondor projects power along the Anduin and into Dor Rhûnen, Easterling tribes press from the east, and above all Dol Guldur and its Necromancer darken the forest and shape the fate of all inhabitants after the Great Plague.

source.supplement: Southern Mirkwood – Haunt of the Necromancer

facts.products: Lumber, hides, nuts, carved wooden boxes.

phrases: Summer in Mirkwood is a stifling green dark; the heat stands still under the canopy and the forest breathes slowly in its sleep.
Rain on Mirkwood is a long black dripping; the eaves shed it for days and the paths run with dark water.
Mirkwood in winter is a black-and-white maze — bare black boughs, grey light, and the dim paths hidden under frost and dead leaves.

rotation: Gentle hills in the heart of Harlindon, known for the Elvish tradition of singing at dawn from hilltops facing the sea. Ancient oaks in open meadows and river-pebble paths between the mountains and the coast.

Gentle hills in central Harlindon with river-pebble paths between the mountains and the coast. The Elvish tradition of singing at dawn from hilltops facing the sea started here; the acoustics of the valley invite it.
Ancient oaks in open meadows, the understorey kept clear enough to walk through. The sense of an intentional landscape — not garden exactly, but managed, tended, thought about over long centuries.

A valley oriented directly toward the sea that catches the dawn light. In summer the mornings are quiet and mist-free enough to hear the water from the hilltops; in winter it takes longer for the light to reach the valley floor.
Mild and damp, with the Atlantic influence keeping the temperatures even year-round. A place of pleasant weather by the standards of northern Middle-earth, which is probably why the Elves chose it.

Sindar who live here because they chose this specific valley for specific reasons that have to do with sound and light and orientation to the sea. The choice is still visible in how they've arranged themselves in it.

rotation: Open plain of Harlindon swept by the gulf wind. Grass that bends in silver waves, heather in spring bloom and Elvish bonfires dotting the dark on gathering nights. Bright and open with a gentle underlying melancholy.
Open Harlindon plain where the gulf wind runs without obstruction. Grass that bends silver in the breeze, heather in full bloom by spring and Elvish bonfires on the headlands on gathering nights.

The most exposed part of Lindon — flat enough that the weather arrives visibly from the west. The Elves who live here have learned to read the cloud-shapes on the horizon and they are rarely caught by surprise.

Low ground between the Ered Luin and the coast, with no feature to break the wind or the sight-lines. In this flatness there is a particular quality of openness that some find liberating and others find lonely.
Relentless mild Atlantic weather — rarely extreme, rarely calm. The Elves who chose this landscape chose the wind as much as they chose the grass, and their architecture acknowledges both.
Gatherings under open sky when the season permits. A less-cloistered community than the wooded sub-regions; they chose the plain deliberately and live accordingly.

For your Middle-earth-on-Europe map, Lindon should be treated as one macro-region with internal subregions (Forlindon, Harlindon, Rhûnlindon) sharing a maritime temperate climate, and Mithlond explicitly marked as a major harbor node. Climate numbers (temperature ranges and precipitation) from the Traveller’s Guide can be mapped directly onto your climate system for coastal vs mountain bands, while the Wandering Companies’ route description provides a canonical overland corridor from Imladris to the Grey Havens for your path and distance calculations.[file:99] Eerily beautiful remnants of Beleriand, characterized by rugged coastal hills, fertile valleys, and evergreen forests. A light rain, drizzle, or ethereal fog falls on most days of the year, allowing mosses, ferns, firs, and spruce to thrive.

people.symbol: Círdan's Device: A White Pelannun on a Blue Field
people.military: 2,000 Warriors and Sailors (Forlindon: 800 Warriors/Sailors, 800 Levy. Harlindon: 1,200 Sailors/Warriors, 800 Militia).
people.description: Lindon’s population is overwhelmingly Elvish, composed of multiple lineages (Noldor, Sindar, Laiquendi, Nandor, Falathrim) under Gil-galad and later Círdan, with a significant Dwarven presence in the Blue Mountains and peripheral contact with Men and Hobbits via routes and harbors. The Traveller’s Guide provides detailed population tables showing long-term decline through the Third Age.

aspect.en: South Harlindon is a green, quiet coastal and forest region south of the Gulf of Lhûn. Historically a fief under Celeborn, Harlindon is characterized by lowlands cloaked in rich deciduous and coniferous forests and a long-term peaceful rural atmosphere. The eastern foothills are used by Dwarves for active coal and iron mines. Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Southernmost fringe of Lindon, where oak and conifer forests reach a rocky shoreline of tidal inlets. Dwarven mining roads in the eastern foothills and a small Sindar Elvish community living quietly by the sea.

Southernmost Lindon coast where oak forest reaches rocky sea-inlets and tidal pools. A small Sindar community lives quietly here at the edge of both land and Elvish presence, closest to the wider world.

Dense temperate forest with an aromatic understorey — bay and broom and something that has no name in Westron. The Dwarven mining roads from the eastern Ered Luin reach this coast and stop at the sea.
Tidal inlets and rock shelves along the coast, with the forest right to the edge in places. The transition from solid land to sea is abrupt here in a way it isn't further north on the Gulf.
Sheltered from the worst of the Atlantic weather by the Ered Luin to the northeast; milder than northern Lindon and wetter than the Gulf shore. A comfortable climate that doesn't announce itself.
Sindar who chose the end of the road — literally the last coastal settlement before Belegaer — and who have the quiet manner of people who have thought about the sea for a very long time.

land.name: Harlindon Forest Belts
land.biome_hint: warm-temperate coastal forest with oak, ash, poplar, and holly
land.description: The dense deciduous and evergreen woods covering the coastal lowlands of South Harlindon.

facts.notes: South Harlindon represents the rustic, woodland-oriented side of Lindon, in contrast to the high-craft ports of Forlindon. Eerily beautiful remnants of Beleriand, characterized by rugged coastal hills, fertile valleys, and evergreen forests. A light rain, drizzle, or ethereal fog falls on most days of the year, allowing mosses, ferns, firs, and spruce to thrive.

people.symbol: Círdan's Device: A White Pelannun on a Blue Field
people.military: 2,000 Warriors and Sailors (Forlindon: 800 Warriors/Sailors, 800 Levy. Harlindon: 1,200 Sailors/Warriors, 800 Militia).
people.description: Inhabitants are primarily Sindar and Laiquendi Elves who prefer a woodland life, along with some Dwarven coal miners in the east.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

aspect.en: Lindon is the westernmost Elvish realm of Middle-earth, the remnant of Ossiriand that survived the War of Wrath. After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Narrow valleys in Harlindon's northern foothills where short rivers run down from the Ered Luin to the Gulf. Alders and willows along salmon-rich streams; a place tied by tradition to the Nandor women who first settled Lindon.

Narrow valleys in northern Harlindon where short rivers run fast down from the Ered Luin to the Gulf. Alders and willows along salmon-rich streams, and the tradition that the Nandor women who first settled Lindon camped here.

The valleys are small and the rivers loud; the water is cold even in summer and the salmon runs in autumn are dense enough to attract bears from the mountains. The Elves fish with the patience of those who have time.

Rushing water and narrow light — the valleys orient north-south and catch the morning and evening sun but miss the midday. The effect is a landscape in which shadow and light alternate through the day.

Cool summers in the shadow of the mountains; cold winters when the snow fills the valley-floors. The streams keep running through winter because the gradient is steep enough to prevent complete freezing.
Nandor Elves with long roots in this specific landscape. The memory of the first settlement is alive here in a way it isn't in the more recently-built communities further south.

land.name: Forlindon (North Lindon)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate coastal and lowland zone with maritime influence transitioning to colder mountain foothills
land.description: The northern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, including coastal plains and the northern Blue Mountain foothills. Historically the primary home of the Noldor (Godhellim) in the realm, it contains harbors and settlements connected to Mithlond and is treated in the government section as a distinct administrative region.[file:99]

land.name: Harlindon (South Lindon)
land.biome_hint: mild, wet coastal strip with forests and rural Elven settlements around secondary harbors
land.description: The southern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, associated with Sindar and Laiquendi (Iathrim, Laegrim). It combines coastal stretches and forested lowlands, was once a fief under Celeborn, and is portrayed as more rural and woodland-oriented than Forlindon.[file:99]

land.name: Rhûnlindon (east-of-Lhûn / Blue Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cool to cold mountain zone with conifer forests, winter snow and extensive mining
land.description: The part of Lindon’s sphere east of the River Lhûn, including the eastern Blue Mountains with Dwarven halls and some Elven refuges. Population tables assign Rhûnlindon about 10% of Lindon’s population, with climate corresponding to the Ered Luin band (colder winters, moderate summers, 30–40 inches of precipitation).[^file99]

land.name: Mithlond (Grey Havens)
land.biome_hint: maritime urban enclave with sheltered harbor, mild wet climate and intensive shipbuilding
land.description: The principal harbor city at the head of the Gulf of Lhûn, seat of Círdan in the Third Age and the main port for Elves and Ring-bearers departing to Valinor. Population tables show Mithlond comprising 20–25% of Lindon’s inhabitants in the Third Age (and 9–10% in the Second Age), emphasizing its central role in Lindon’s demography and economy.[file:99]

land.name: Taeg Lindon routes and refuges
land.biome_hint: mixed grassland, forest and hill country between the Misty Mountains and the Ered Luin, with hidden Elven refuges
land.description: The 'Bounds of Lindon' section describes the Wandering Companies’ preferred route from Imladris to Mithlond: across Eregion, the Mitheithel ford south of Fennas Drúnin, the South Downs and Barrow-downs (with stops near Tom Bombadil’s house), then either through the Old Forest and Green Hills or along the Brandywine’s eastern shore before turning west to the Ered Luin. Along roughly 600 miles they maintain rustic camps and more elaborate permanent refuges (glades, caves, small houses) 20–30 miles apart, some shared with Rangers after the fall of Arthedain.[file:99]

aspect.en: The Ered Luin Vales encompass the central valleys, river passes, and sub-alpine basins of the Blue Mountains. This region is centered around the Nan-i-Naugrim (Dwarven Vale) and the headwaters of the River Annuduin, where the Dwarves established a complex network of fourteen holds, including Merlost, built on the ruins of ancient Belegost.

rotation: Sub-alpine valleys and gorges of the Ered Luin with fourteen Dwarven hall-fortresses, including Merlost over the ruins of Belegost. Firs on rock walls, snowmelt waterfalls and the constant ring of Dwarven picks.

Sub-alpine valleys and gorges of the Ered Luin with fourteen Dwarven hall-fortresses from Merlost southward. Firs on rock walls, snowmelt waterfalls audible from a mile and the ring of Dwarven picks carried on the wind.

The valleys between the mountain faces are genuinely sheltered — warmer and drier than the exposed ridgelines above, cold enough for good timber and the kind of silence that sits around heavy industry.

Merlost above the ruins of Belegost: a name that carries the weight of what was lost in the First Age. The new halls are solid and practical and the Dwarves who live in them have their own relationship with that history.

Short summers when the snowmelt waterfalls are at full volume; long winters when the snow fills the valley-floors and the only warmth is inside the mountain. The Dwarves prefer the inside; the valleys are for moving between.
Dwarven craftsmen and miners who have organised their entire lives around the mountain. Outsiders pass through on the east-west trade route; the Dwarves observe and occasionally engage.

land.name: Nan-i-Naugrim (Dwarven Vale)
land.biome_hint: sub-alpine valley with cold rivers and coniferous margins
land.description: The central valley of the Ered Luin, home to fourteen Dwarven holds situated along the headwaters of the River Annuduin.

facts.notes: The Dwarven Vale serves as a central hub of trade and industry in western Eriador, connecting Elven Lindon with the kingdoms of Men.

people.symbol: A Hammer surmounted by Three Tongues of Flame
people.military: 490 Warriors. 2,100 Warrior Levy.
people.description: The primary population of the vales is Dwarves of Durin's Folk and descendants of Belegost and Nogrod.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

facts.products: Finished goods, iron, tin, copper, lead.

aspect.en: The High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath, S. 'High-climbing Pass of the North') cuts through the central Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell and Eriador in the west to the upper Anduin Vales and Rhovanion in the east. It encompasses the Orcish stronghold of Goblin-gate, the eyrie of the Great Eagles, the Northman market-town of Maethelburg, the western foothills of Rhudaur, and the broad river plain of the Anduin. Geology consists of limestone and granite with massive igneous basalt intrusions. western foothills consist of red sandstone, while eastern valleys contain oily black shale; rich in copper, iron, silver, gold, and mithril.

rotation: The middle vale of the Great River — broad grey water running south between wooded banks, misty at dawn and hiding the far shore under curtains of rain.
Woods and willow-islands crowd the eastern shore; the west is open grassland rolling away under a wide sky. The river narrows and quickens where the channel steepens.
The River is the road here — boats go south with the current until the rapids of Sarn Gebir bar the way, where white water breaks on tooth-like rocks and the portage is steep and stony.
At dusk mist lies among the trees and along the pale margins of the water; stars come out over the stony hills, and the river carries small uncertain sounds through the dark.
Between the banks the world narrows to water and wind — rain that curtains the view, fog that hides the shores, and after the storm a hard bright sky.
Below the narrowing gorge the river opens again on still water and long fens; the reeds whisper in the grey light and small birds pipe among them.

land.name: Anduin Vales (eastern lowlands)
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with lush meadows, broadleaf groves, wetland margins and open farmland
land.description: The broad valley plain east of the Misty Mountains, gently sloping eastward and southward; easily traversed open terrain with grassy meadows, river marshes, elm and oak groves, and scattered Northman homesteads and trading towns. Maethelburg is the main settlement, a fortified hill-town at the confluence of the Anduin and Sirros (Foamflood). The Great River here is the main highway, plied by Northman cnearras (shallow-draught clinker-built craft) trading between Maethelburg and Gondor.[file:88]

land.name: Western Foothills of Rhudaur
land.biome_hint: cold Atlantic-type rugged moorland and forested ravines with bog, heather and ancient conifer cover
land.description: The rugged, forested foothills and moorland west of the Misty Mountains in the territory of Rhudaur; grim stony heights, deep ravines, ancient pine-shrouded valleys and heather-covered moorland, cut by treacherous bogs. Home to Hillmen clans and prowled by Stone-trolls and Orcs at night; nearly impassable without a guide except along the Great East Road (which ends at the Ford of Bruinen).[file:88]

land.name: High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath)
land.biome_hint: subarctic alpine pass with permanent snowcaps, glaciers, scree slopes and fierce storm exposure
land.description: A double-branched pass through the Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell to the Anduin: the lower branch (Pass of Imladris, c.3,500 ft) permits horses and wagons but is controlled by Goblin-gate at its summit; the upper mountain-path (over 5,000 ft) is passable only on foot or by mule/pony, steep and exposed to storms but less Orc-infested. Both branches are snow-blocked from Hithui to Gwirith. The pass is riddled with scree, avalanche risk, tumbling boulders and the constant threat of Giants above and Orcs below.[file:88]

land.name: Goblin-Gate (Goblin-town underground)
land.biome_hint: karst limestone cave system with ice caves (upper), inhabited city levels, fungi caves, and deep mine shafts
land.description: A vast network of natural limestone caverns expanded and connected by Orcish mining over millennia, stretching up to 40 miles between the Wolf Gate (main western entrance at the pass summit) and the Back Door (eastern exit to the Anduin slopes), with further passages to the Fungi Caves, Mine levels, and reputed deep shafts connecting to the Underdeeps of Moria. At T.A. 1640: the Great Goblin rules from the City Level; Gollum has not yet arrived (that happens c.T.A. 2470). Underground lakes, underground rivers, stalactites, ice caves (upper levels), massive fungi forests (lower levels) and deep mine shafts all present in the complex.[file:88]

land.name: Eagles' Eyrie (Amon Thyrir pinnacle)
land.biome_hint: bare alpine rock pinnacle above the tree line, surrounded by high-altitude thermals and glaciated peaks
land.description: A solitary rock pinnacle rising above the mountain crags east of the High Pass, inaccessible except by flight; crowned by the vast bowl-shaped nest (up to 40 ft diameter, several tons) of the Lord of the Eagles. The surrounding high peaks and thermal columns of warm rising air are the domain of a small population of Great Eagles, each controlling a territory of 200+ sq miles of mountain terrain.[file:88]

land.name: Giants' Isle (mountain vale)
land.biome_hint: remote high-altitude vale with rock, scree, glacial streams and no human habitation
land.description: A secluded area of high mountain vales where Stone Giants are concentrated; largely avoided by all other peoples. The Giants hurl boulders during thunderstorms and have occupied these heights since the First Age. No settlement is possible here.[file:88]

facts.notes: This module is centered on T.A. 1640 (primary time period), with additional adventures set in T.A. 2940 (time of The Hobbit, when Gollum is already in the caves and Thorin's company passes through) and F.A. 1. The fauna and flora data reflect the T.A. 1640 baseline. Goblin-gate's internal geography is partially procedurally generated (Random Features Table in the module) and not fully fixed on maps—only key route passages are mapped. The region connects westward to Rivendell/Eriador and eastward to northern Mirkwood via Maethelburg and the Old Ford, making it a critical chokepoint on the Misty Mountains.[file:88] The longest and highest mountain chain in the west, serving as a formidable glacial barrier between Eriador and Rhovanion. Heavy snows and glaciers cover peaks above 11,500 feet year-round. It is riddled with Orc-holds, Dwarven caverns, and the under-deeps.

people.military: 100 Beornings. 60 Burgwards of Maethelburg. 900 Militia (3-4 weeks to raise, organized by clan). 135 Eagles (allies).
people.description: The region is sparsely populated by several distinct peoples: Northmen (Nenedain) in the Anduin Vales, Beornings on the eastern bank, Hillmen in the rough hills of Rhudaur, and Orcs in the mountain strongholds, alongside rarer presences of Elves, Dwarves, Giants and Eagles.

facts.products: Grain, hides, cattle, honey, amber, tin.

phrases: The Vale of Anduin in winter is a grey country of mist and pale water; the river runs dark and the high banks stand cold and bare on either side.
Rain on the Anduin is a curtain drawn across the world; the far shore vanishes, and there is only the hiss of water falling on water.
A cold from the north rides the river-valley; it comes down the channel before dawn, and the mist along the banks is grey ice made air.

aspect.en: Ronen-in-Anduin is the eastern floodplains and low rolling hills bordering the Great River Anduin as it passes through the territory of Rhovanion. It represents a transition zone between the river valleys and the wide eastern steppes.

rotation: The south vale of Anduin — the long lake of Nen Hithoel under bare peaks, the dark gorge of the Argonath above it, and the thunder of Rauros at its foot.
The River opens from the narrows into still water ringed by wooded slopes; the green lawns of the old landing lie under the hills where the high seats of the watch once stood.
Eastward the land rises into the Emyn Muil — a knife-edged country of cliffs and gullies where the rock is broken and the going is slow and cruel.
Below the Falls the land falls away to fens and then the dead meres; the River's song here is all the sound there is, and it is loud.
The mists of the falls hang golden in the afternoon; the water's fury shakes the quiet air, and the spray rises like smoke from the deep channel.
A stern and splendid country — water, rock and height; the pillars of the kings stand in the narrows, and the River goes on south whether the land permits or not.

land.name: Anduin Margins
land.biome_hint: river floodplains merging into semi-arid grassy steppe
land.description: The low, rolling floodplains bordering the river.

facts.notes: Ronen-in-Anduin is highly vulnerable to raids from Easterlings crossing the River Running.

people.military: Local clan militia.
people.description: Inhabited by scattered Northmen herders and wandering Easterling scouts.

phrases: Rain over the long lake is a grey world of falling water and rising mist; the Falls thunder unseen behind the curtain.
The lake-country in winter is a stern land — dark water, white-crowned peaks about the falls, and the sound of Rauros rolling through the cold.
A keen cold comes down the ravines of the Emyn Muil; it carries the smell of the dead meres and leaves the stones ringing.

aspect.en: Southern Mirkwood and Southern Rhovanion form a wild, embattled region stretching from the Old Forest Road down to the Dagorlad and the Emyn Muil, dominated by the dark forest around Dol Guldur, the horse-plains of Talath Harroch, and the Anduin vales and Brown Lands that lie between Mirkwood and Gondor. Geology consists of primarily sedimentary strata of limestone and shale, with significant granite projections such as the cinder cone of amon lanc and the mountains of mirkwood.

rotation: The land of the Woodmen — the west-eaves of Mirkwood where free folk keep hidden halls in the oak-woods and hold the forest's shadow at bay.
Great oaks and elms over deep mast; the clearings are meadow and bee-pasture, and the air is warm with honey in summer.
The halls are broad wooden steads behind stockades — places of firelight, carved pillars and animal friends, hidden among the trees from the dark things of the Wood.
Deer-paths and secret ways; the Woodmen walk where others would be lost in an hour, and the forest's edge is theirs and no other's.
White autumn mist lies on the ground at dawn and the sun rises red to clear it; along the paths go grass, flowers, birds and red deer to the fords of Anduin.
A border-land — green and homely within, black and watchful at the eaves; the Woodmen live in the seam between the two and keep the knowledge of both.

land.name: Angaladadh (Northwest quadrant)
land.biome_hint: dense temperate hardwood–evergreen forest with heavy undergrowth
land.description: The deep northern heart of Southern Mirkwood’s forest, north-west of Dol Guldur, where the canopy remains thick, the old rose-tree circles still stand and Elven influence is strongest.

land.name: Aur Esgalabar / Romeniaur (Northeast quadrant)
land.biome_hint: mosaic of forest edge, scrub and plains
land.description: The northeastern wedge where the forest thins and gives way to grassland and the East Bight, mixing woodland, scrub and open country.

land.name: Talath Harroch (The Plains)
land.biome_hint: cool temperate grassland and farmland with scattered homesteads
land.description: The broad plains southeast of Mirkwood, home to horse-herding Northmen, wild herds and culcarnix, with long snowy winters and violent spring rains.

land.name: Nan Lothanduin / Nan Anduin
land.biome_hint: broad river valley with alluvial fields, groves and settlements
land.description: The Anduin vales south of the Old Forest Road and opposite Dol Guldur, containing fertile pockets such as Tharlorien, the North and South Undeeps and Beijabar holdings.

land.name: Dol Guldur (Amon Lanc)
land.biome_hint: rocky volcanic hill with dead trees and corrupted scrub
land.description: A stark, 3649‑foot volcanic cone on the southern eaves of Mirkwood, crowned and ringed by fortress walls and towers, once called the Naked Hill and now the hill of sorcery under Sauron’s control.

land.name: Emyn Guldur (Hills of Sorcery)
land.biome_hint: rocky hills with dark forest patches, caves and cliffs
land.description: Rugged hills and broken country around Dol Guldur, full of caves and shelves where spiders and fell beasts lair, and criss-crossed by secret Orc-paths.

land.name: Old Forest Road (southern sector)
land.biome_hint: forest-margin road through mixed woodland and clearings
land.description: The east–west road along the northern edge of Southern Rhovanion, carrying refugees and trade and linking the western vales with the eastern plains and forest entries.

land.name: Road to the Morannon
land.biome_hint: long overland route across river-vales and dry hills
land.description: The main north–south route from Nan Anduin across the Brown Lands toward the Black Gate, used increasingly by Sauron’s forces shifting from Dol Guldur to Mordor.

land.name: North and South Undeep
land.biome_hint: wide, shallow river reaches with rocky beds and down-like hills
land.description: Shallow fords of the Anduin where the river spreads over rock shelves, forming strategic crossing-points guarded and contested by Gondor and its enemies.

land.name: Brown Lands
land.biome_hint: dry temperate steppe on old terraced hills
land.description: Bleak, brown hills east of the Anduin whose ridges were once raised and irrigated garden beds tended by the Entwives, now covered in short dry grass and scarred by frost and neglect.

facts.notes: This object treats Southern Mirkwood and Southern Rhovanion as a single strategic and ecological unit in T.A. 1640: the haunted southern forest around Dol Guldur, the Talath Harroch horse-plains, the Anduin vales and Brown Lands, and the human and inhuman powers contesting them; individual sites such as Woodmen-town, Rhosgobel, Thorontir and Dol Guldur’s detailed layouts can be represented as separate site objects if needed. The largest forest in western Endor, dominated by oaks, maples, elms, and conifers. It has fallen under a stagnant, heavy shadow since the Necromancer established Dol Guldur, making southern reaches twisted, dark, and home to giant spiders.

people.military: 650 Warriors, led by local chieftains.
people.description: Southern Rhovanion is a country under siege: Beijabar and Wood-men cling to the western eaves, horse-lords and Gramuz Northmen fight for survival on the Talath Harroch, Gondor projects power along the Anduin and into Dor Rhûnen, Easterling tribes press from the east, and above all Dol Guldur and its Necromancer darken the forest and shape the fate of all inhabitants after the Great Plague.

source.supplement: Southern Mirkwood – Haunt of the Necromancer

facts.products: Lumber, hides, nuts, carved wooden boxes.

phrases: The Woodmen's country in winter is a white-drifted forest of black oaks; the halls are warm behind their stockades and the deer-yards are silent.
Summer in the Beornings' woodland is green gold — oak-shade, high meadows, and honey in the hollow trees.

aspect.en: Nan Anduin is the long, wide, and highly fertile alluvial valley through which the Great River Anduin flows between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood. It contains some of the richest soil in Middle-earth, supporting scattered communities of Beornings, Woodmen, and Northman pioneers.

rotation: The northern Vales of Anduin — the green land between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood's eaves, where the River runs broad and the Beornings keep their bee-pastures and their halls.
Great oaks and elms clothe the vales, deep in mast and honey; the meadows are loud with bees, and the Carrock — the great stone — stands mid-river where the eagles come.
The Gladden Fields spread quiet where the mountain-streams come down — a reedy fen that once saw a king lost and a doom begin.
Between the mountains and the Wood the vale is a green corridor — the Old Ford crosses the River where the stepping-stones break the current into fast bright channels.
The Beornings' country — wood-men and bee-keepers who hate goblins and guard the fords; their halls stand hidden in the oakwoods and their bread is famous.
Black winters and green abundant summers; the river swells with the mountain rain, and the fords are crossing or drowning by the sky's decision.

land.name: Anduin Floodplains
land.biome_hint: fertile alluvial plains with willow groves and wheat fields
land.description: The fertile, wide flat lands bordering the Great River.

facts.notes: The Anduin is the life-blood of Rhovanion, serving as a natural trade corridor and barrier.

people.military: 100 Beornings. 60 Burgwards of Maethelburg. 900 Militia (3-4 weeks to raise, organized by clan). 135 Eagles (allies).
people.description: Home to Beornings (Beijabar), Woodmen, and pastoral Northmen.

facts.products: Grain, hides, cattle, honey, amber, tin.

phrases: The Anduin vales under winter are a quiet land of black water and white hills; the fords freeze at their edges and the mountains close in.
Snow on the vales makes a clean and silent world — white meadows, black water, and the dark line of the forest under its burden.
Rain brings the mountain-streams down and the Anduin up; the fords deepen, the fens spread, and the valley fills with the sound of water.

aspect.en: The High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath, S. 'High-climbing Pass of the North') cuts through the central Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell and Eriador in the west to the upper Anduin Vales and Rhovanion in the east. It encompasses the Orcish stronghold of Goblin-gate, the eyrie of the Great Eagles, the Northman market-town of Maethelburg, the western foothills of Rhudaur, and the broad river plain of the Anduin. Geology consists of limestone and granite with massive igneous basalt intrusions. western foothills consist of red sandstone, while eastern valleys contain oily black shale; rich in copper, iron, silver, gold, and mithril.

rotation: The high spine of the world — three great peaks over the Dimrill Dale, Caradhras cruel and tallest, with snow above the cloud-line and storm for a gatekeeper.
Pine and bare rock on the lower slopes; above the tree-line are grey shoulders, hanging valleys, and ledge-paths where a storm can fill the night with thunder and falling ice.
The passes are the gates between east and west — the Redhorn Gate and the high, deceptive ways where the paths lie and the mountain decides who may cross.
Beneath the feet of the mountains run the deep ways of Moria; the stone is old and hollow, and the silence below is not empty.
At sunset the ridges cast long shadows down onto the lowlands; between the trees open glimpses of green plains that seem far below and far away.
The weather here is a will, not a climate — it closes the passes in snow, sends lightning through the hollows, and lets none pass unconsidered.

land.name: Anduin Vales (eastern lowlands)
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with lush meadows, broadleaf groves, wetland margins and open farmland
land.description: The broad valley plain east of the Misty Mountains, gently sloping eastward and southward; easily traversed open terrain with grassy meadows, river marshes, elm and oak groves, and scattered Northman homesteads and trading towns. Maethelburg is the main settlement, a fortified hill-town at the confluence of the Anduin and Sirros (Foamflood). The Great River here is the main highway, plied by Northman cnearras (shallow-draught clinker-built craft) trading between Maethelburg and Gondor.[file:88]

land.name: Western Foothills of Rhudaur
land.biome_hint: cold Atlantic-type rugged moorland and forested ravines with bog, heather and ancient conifer cover
land.description: The rugged, forested foothills and moorland west of the Misty Mountains in the territory of Rhudaur; grim stony heights, deep ravines, ancient pine-shrouded valleys and heather-covered moorland, cut by treacherous bogs. Home to Hillmen clans and prowled by Stone-trolls and Orcs at night; nearly impassable without a guide except along the Great East Road (which ends at the Ford of Bruinen).[file:88]

land.name: High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath)
land.biome_hint: subarctic alpine pass with permanent snowcaps, glaciers, scree slopes and fierce storm exposure
land.description: A double-branched pass through the Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell to the Anduin: the lower branch (Pass of Imladris, c.3,500 ft) permits horses and wagons but is controlled by Goblin-gate at its summit; the upper mountain-path (over 5,000 ft) is passable only on foot or by mule/pony, steep and exposed to storms but less Orc-infested. Both branches are snow-blocked from Hithui to Gwirith. The pass is riddled with scree, avalanche risk, tumbling boulders and the constant threat of Giants above and Orcs below.[file:88]

land.name: Goblin-Gate (Goblin-town underground)
land.biome_hint: karst limestone cave system with ice caves (upper), inhabited city levels, fungi caves, and deep mine shafts
land.description: A vast network of natural limestone caverns expanded and connected by Orcish mining over millennia, stretching up to 40 miles between the Wolf Gate (main western entrance at the pass summit) and the Back Door (eastern exit to the Anduin slopes), with further passages to the Fungi Caves, Mine levels, and reputed deep shafts connecting to the Underdeeps of Moria. At T.A. 1640: the Great Goblin rules from the City Level; Gollum has not yet arrived (that happens c.T.A. 2470). Underground lakes, underground rivers, stalactites, ice caves (upper levels), massive fungi forests (lower levels) and deep mine shafts all present in the complex.[file:88]

land.name: Eagles' Eyrie (Amon Thyrir pinnacle)
land.biome_hint: bare alpine rock pinnacle above the tree line, surrounded by high-altitude thermals and glaciated peaks
land.description: A solitary rock pinnacle rising above the mountain crags east of the High Pass, inaccessible except by flight; crowned by the vast bowl-shaped nest (up to 40 ft diameter, several tons) of the Lord of the Eagles. The surrounding high peaks and thermal columns of warm rising air are the domain of a small population of Great Eagles, each controlling a territory of 200+ sq miles of mountain terrain.[file:88]

land.name: Giants' Isle (mountain vale)
land.biome_hint: remote high-altitude vale with rock, scree, glacial streams and no human habitation
land.description: A secluded area of high mountain vales where Stone Giants are concentrated; largely avoided by all other peoples. The Giants hurl boulders during thunderstorms and have occupied these heights since the First Age. No settlement is possible here.[file:88]

facts.notes: This module is centered on T.A. 1640 (primary time period), with additional adventures set in T.A. 2940 (time of The Hobbit, when Gollum is already in the caves and Thorin's company passes through) and F.A. 1. The fauna and flora data reflect the T.A. 1640 baseline. Goblin-gate's internal geography is partially procedurally generated (Random Features Table in the module) and not fully fixed on maps—only key route passages are mapped. The region connects westward to Rivendell/Eriador and eastward to northern Mirkwood via Maethelburg and the Old Ford, making it a critical chokepoint on the Misty Mountains.[file:88] The longest and highest mountain chain in the west, serving as a formidable glacial barrier between Eriador and Rhovanion. Heavy snows and glaciers cover peaks above 11,500 feet year-round. It is riddled with Orc-holds, Dwarven caverns, and the under-deeps.

people.military: 100 Beornings. 60 Burgwards of Maethelburg. 900 Militia (3-4 weeks to raise, organized by clan). 135 Eagles (allies).
people.description: The region is sparsely populated by several distinct peoples: Northmen (Nenedain) in the Anduin Vales, Beornings on the eastern bank, Hillmen in the rough hills of Rhudaur, and Orcs in the mountain strongholds, alongside rarer presences of Elves, Dwarves, Giants and Eagles.

facts.products: Grain, hides, cattle, honey, amber, tin.

phrases: The Misty Mountains in winter are a white rampart across the world; the passes are sealed, and the peaks hold their storms like a grudge.
On the high passes the snow is a living thing — it drifts, it blinds, it buries; the mountains shut their gates and the wind walks abroad.
The cold of the high passes is thin, bright, and murderous; it numbs the hands on the rock and turns the breath to ice.

aspect.en: Northern Mirkwood is the northern half of the great forest once known as Greenwood the Great, stretching between the Anduin, the Grey Mountains, the Withered Heath and the upper River Running, and including Thranduil’s woodland realm, the Long Lake, the Lonely Mountain and the Iron Hills.

rotation: The Woodland Realm — the Elvenking's country in the north-eaves of Mirkwood, where the wood is greener and the dark has not so deep a hold.
Beech-woods over halls of living stone; the king's doors stand in a steep tree-covered slope above the Forest River, and the cave-halls go down to cold springs and deep cellars.
The Forest River is the realm's road — it runs dark and strong under the bridge, out of the wood to the Long Lake, carrying the barrels and the trade.
Feasts are held in the glades by torchlight; the smell of roasting meat and the sound of elven laughter drift through the trees and mislead the hungry.
Green summers and white winters; the rain on the eaves is soft, and the river runs fuller and darker for it. The wood is watched, and the deer-parks are guarded.
The wood-elves are unfriendly to strangers in the deep forest — less cruel than the southern wood, but their doors are shut to those they do not know.

land.name: Northern Mirkwood proper
land.biome_hint: large temperate conifer–broadleaf forest with hills, marshes and river-valleys
land.description: The northern half of Mirkwood, north of the Men-i-Naugrim and between the Anduin, the Grey Mountains, the Withered Heath and the upper River Running, including Thranduil’s realm and vast tracts of deep forest.

land.name: Ered Mithrin (Grey Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cold temperate to subarctic mountains with rock, snow and conifer bands
land.description: A long, jagged range north of Mirkwood with peaks over 6000 feet, snowfields in winter and numerous lairs of dragons, Great Eagles, giants and hardy mountain folk.

land.name: Withered Heath
land.biome_hint: cold, rocky heath with sparse vegetation and dragon-haunted cliffs
land.description: The desolate, frost-scarred upland east of the Grey Mountains and north of Erebor that has long served as the breeding ground and hunting territory of dragons.

land.name: Long Lake
land.biome_hint: cold temperate lake with marshy margins and nearby low hills
land.description: A long, narrow lake east of Mirkwood, essentially a glacial trench filled to the brim by the Forest River, feeding the River Running and supporting Lake-town and its trade.

land.name: Forest River (Taurduin)
land.biome_hint: mountain-fed river with gorges, marshes and mixed forest banks
land.description: River flowing from the Grey Mountains through the northern forest into Long Lake, cutting gorges with stone cliffs and shingle banks and forming the Long Marshes near its mouth.

land.name: Anduin (upper course)
land.biome_hint: large temperate river with floodplains, bluffs and mixed woodland
land.description: The upper Anduin flowing south along the western edge of Mirkwood, defining the forest’s western boundary and offering fertile vales for Northmen and Beijabar.

land.name: Long Marshes
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate marsh with reeds, shallow pools and islets
land.description: Expansive marshlands of brackish pools and islets along the lower Forest River near Long Lake, teeming with insects, birds, amphibians and small mammals.

land.name: Mountains of Mirkwood
land.biome_hint: low to mid-elevation karst hills with forested slopes and caves
land.description: Lower, older limestone mountains within the forest that extend to its eastern edge, riddled with caverns ideal for caches, lairs and hidden strongholds.

land.name: Rhovanion plains (northern fringe)
land.biome_hint: cool temperate steppe and farmland with scattered groves
land.description: The open grasslands and gentle hills east of the forest and south of the Iron Hills, used by Northmen as grazing land and farmland.

facts.notes: This object treats Northern Mirkwood as the combined forest, mountain and river system north of the Men-i-Naugrim in T.A. 1640, including Thranduil’s woodland realm, the Grey Mountains, Long Lake, Erebor’s immediate environs and the Iron Hills; specific cities such as Lake-town and Dale can be modeled as separate site objects.

people.symbol: Dark Green Beech Leaf on a Grass Green Field
people.military: 1,900 Elite Warriors and Rangers. 2,100 Warriors. 200 Raft-elf Warriors.
people.description: Northern Mirkwood in T.A. 1640 is a sparsely civilized frontier containing Thranduil’s Wood-elves, Dwarves of the Iron Hills and Erebor, multiple Northmen cultures in valleys and plains, and scattered Beijabar and other folk in the hills, all living under the growing long-range shadow of Dol Guldur and the aftermath of the Great Plague.

phrases: The Woodland Realm in winter is a green court gone white — bare beeches, the river dark and cold, and the warm halls hidden under the hill.
Summer under the Elvenking's eaves is a green and golden twilight — feasts in the glades, lanterns among the leaves, and the river running dark below.
Rain on the north-wood is soft and long; the beech-woods drip, the river rises, and the doors of the halls stand open to the wet dark.

aspect.en: The Tower Hills, or Emyn Beraid, are a range of green, rolling hills located west of the Shire. On their highest crests stand three ancient Elven-towers built by Gil-galad, where the Elendil Stone (palantír) was guarded for millennia.

rotation: The Tower Hills — green ridges west of the Shire where the white towers of Elostirion stand, the last work of the Elves on the hither shore.
Tall woods on the hill-flanks and the towers above them; the palantír of the west kept here once looked only toward the Sea.
The East Road ends here — it runs on to the Grey Havens and the last quay. There is no way beyond the towers but the water.
Sea-weather rules: salt wind, grey rain off the water, and clear days when the Sea itself is rumoured visible from the high stones.
A green and lonely borderland; the hobbits farm the eastern slopes and the Elves pass through westward, going to the ships and not returning.
The hills are the world's last green gesture before the grey water; every path through them ends at the Sea.

land.name: Emyn Beraid Crests
land.biome_hint: rolling green chalk downs with heather fields and birch groves
land.description: The high chalk ridges where the three ancient towers stand.

facts.notes: The Tower Hills are a tranquil, holy sanctuary where the Elves preserve ancient memories of the First Age.

people.symbol: Círdan's Device: A White Pelannun on a Blue Field
people.military: Elven archer squads.
people.description: Inhabited by high elves of Lindon and occasional Hobbit travelers.

source.supplement: Tolkien (LotR) with Lindon / Shire regional material

phrases: Rain over the Tower Hills comes off the Sea; it beats on the white towers and runs down the green slopes to the road that ends at the world's edge.
Winter on the Tower Hills is a green land gone grey at the edge of the Sea — bare woods, white towers, and the smell of the salt wind.

aspect.en: Rhudaur is the eastern successor state of Arnor, a rugged, sparsely settled land between the Ettenmoors, the Trollshaws and the Angle. It stretches from the Ettenmoors and Ettendales in the north down through the Pinefells and Trollshaws to the rolling lowlands between the rivers Mitheithel and Bruinen, forming a harsh frontier of jagged hills, evergreen forests, boggy vales and predator-haunted woodlands.

rotation: Western Rhudaur, where dry-stone farms and working mills survive as remnants of Dúnedain prosperity. Now held by Hillmen allied to the Witch-king; black-pine hills, cold torrents and hollows where darkness falls quickly.

Dark-pine hills and cold torrents where Dúnedain prosperity used to live. Hillmen allied to the Witch-king now hold the dry-stone farms; hollows where darkness falls fast and the paths lead where they are directed to lead.

Evergreen Pinefells on the ridges — dense, dark and sinister in the way ancient conifers get when nothing has cleared them for a century. The old Dúnedain farms in the valley-bottoms are occupied now by people with different loyalties.
Boulder-strewn fells on the high ground; better valley-floor farming below it. The geology hasn't changed; the population has changed twice, and the second change brought it into Angmar's orbit.
Cold and wet from the east wind that comes off the Misty Mountains without much warmth. The Pinefells catch the cloud and release it as slow drizzle; the valleys are permanently damp.

Hillmen under Angmar's direction, which means watchers on the roads and information flowing north. The valley-farms are productive; their produce feeds the Witch-king's army rather than Arnor's people.

land.name: Ettenmoors (Môr Ithvaen, 'Granite Sea')
land.biome_hint: cold, rocky highland with minimal soil, scattered hardy vegetation and extreme terrain
land.description: Northernmost highlands of Rhudaur, a landscape of large hills and boulder-strewn terrain created by the uplift of the Misty Mountains. Jagged, little-weathered fells hold very little topsoil; boulders from child-sized to villa-sized lie in 'crazy jumbles' through which passage is impossible for anything larger than a rabbit. The region is bleak, treacherous and ideal for Trolls and other large predators.[file:132]

land.name: Ettendales
land.biome_hint: cool, boggy hill region with springs, stagnant wetlands and patchy grass/heath
land.description: Hill country south of the Ettenmoors, with smaller hills and less granite. The Ettendales hold many springs feeding the Mitheithel but suffer from poor drainage; vales between hills contain stagnant bogs, especially during spring thaw. Despite their water resources, the bogs make travel dangerous and limit settlement.[file:132]

land.name: Pinefells / Coldfells
land.biome_hint: cool evergreen forested hills with well-drained soils and persistent cold winds
land.description: Highlands immediately south and east of the Ettendales, similar in structure but better drained and heavily wooded. Dominated by evergreen forests, the region is known as the Pinefells; others call them 'Coldfells' due to the legendary cool winds and waters. It forms a heavily forested, cold highland belt between the Ettendales and Trollshaws.[file:132]

land.name: Trollshaws
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate mosaic of wooded groves, brush and open grassland in broken hill terrain
land.description: Central Rhudaur between the Mitheithel and Bruinen, rugged hill country with woodland scattered across it. Trees form small dense patches separated by open ground; heavy brush along grove edges extends inward where canopy thins. Popular with wolves, it is also the winter ground for Rhudaur’s vast herds of losrandir and the favored haunt of Hill Trolls.[file:132]

land.name: Coed Drug ('Evilwood')
land.biome_hint: dark, old-growth forest with closed canopy, thick understorey and a supernatural atmosphere
land.description: The most significant forest in Rhudaur, growing on the southern side of the Trollshaws above the Great East Road. An ancient, dense dual stand of woods, it exudes unease and 'latent evil'. Home to Forest Trolls and huge wolves; its immense trees block most sunlight, leaving the interior perpetually dim. Some inner places are said never to be touched by sun or moonlight, and even Elves and Hillmen fear to enter.[file:132]

land.name: The Angle (lowlands between Mitheithel and Bruinen)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate grassland and light woodland with strong winds and limited fertile pockets along rivers
land.description: Rolling grassy hills south of the Coed Drug and between the rivers, broken by jagged fells and occasional stands of trees. Constant northeast winds and rain off the fells strip away topsoil, so agriculture is difficult except along relatively protected and fertile riverbanks. It forms Rhudaur’s main lowland and agricultural zone, albeit poor compared to the rest of Eriador.[file:132]

land.name: Oiolad ('Endless Plain' of the Eredoriath)
land.biome_hint: open grassland/plain adjoining Rhudaur, serving as raiding and travel corridor
land.description: Flat plain west of the Mitheithel beyond Rhudaur’s lowlands, used as raiding ground by the Rhudaurrim and Hillmen into more favored regions. While technically outside core Rhudaur, it is closely linked to its economy and warfare, providing a contrast to the rugged homeland fells.[file:132]

facts.notes: This object isolates Rhudaur as a region within Arnor: The Land, focusing on geographic subzones (Ettenmoors, Ettendales, Pinefells/Coldfells, Trollshaws, Coed Drug, Angle) and mapping the general Flora & Fauna of Eriador onto these specific landscapes. The key Rhudaur-specific ecological elements are the Pinefells evergreens, the Coed Drug ancient 'Evilwood', the losrandir herds and the concentration of Hill and Forest Trolls. Climate and hydrology are dominated by snow-fed highlands (Ettenmoors/Ettendales) and the swift Mitheithel, with constant winds limiting agriculture to narrow riverine bands.[file:132]

people.military: 4,500 Warriors and Eastern Mercenaries, usually grouped according to tribe.
people.population: 50,000: 35,000 Hillmen in thirteen tribes and 15,000 Dunlendings in eleven tribes.
people.description: Rhudaur’s population is sparse and concentrated in hill-country and strategic sites such as Cameth Brin and the Angle. Politically, it is the easternmost and least stable of Arnor’s successor realms, dominated by Hillmen and later influenced or controlled by Angmar. The Arnor book’s detailed cultural and political treatment is split across Arnor: The Land and Arnor: The People; here we focus on the geographic side, noting the Hillmen and Rhudaurrim as the characteristic inhabitants of this harsh landscape.

It stretches from the Ettenmoors and Ettendales in the north down through the Pinefells and Trollshaws to the rolling lowlands between the rivers Mitheithel and Bruinen, forming a harsh frontier of jagged hills, evergreen forests, boggy vales and predator-haunted woodlands.

rotation: The Angle enclosed between the Mitheithel and Bruinen, once the heart of Dúnedain Rhudaur. Deep fertile soil now largely abandoned, palisaded Hillmen villages on the hilltops and Dúnedain tower-ruins rising among the trees.

The Angle between the Mitheithel and Bruinen, once the fertile heart of Dúnedain Rhudaur. Deep soil now abandoned, Hillmen palisades on the hilltops and the old Dúnedain towers rising above their own ruins in the trees.

The soil here is some of the best in Rhudaur — silt from two rivers, deep and workable. The Hillmen farm it efficiently; the tower-ruins above them are a kind of complaint about who owns what and since when.
The rivers form a natural enclosure; the interior of the Angle is sheltered and relatively flat. Its agricultural value was why the Dúnedain valued it; it's why the Hillmen want it too.
Cool and wet enough for good grass; sheltered enough from the mountain winds to grow grain. The same qualities that made it Arnor's breadbasket make it worth holding now.
Hillmen who hold the land with Angmar's blessing and watch the fords of both rivers. The palisaded villages are defensive because they know what happened to the Dúnedain who were here before.

rotation: The Trollshaws — the woods and broken hills under the mountains' western feet, where the Road begins its climb and the trolls have their holes.
Thick beech-woods over stony ravines; the ground folds and drops, the streams come down loud and cold, and the caves in the rock are not all empty.
The Road through the shaws is a hard wet way — soaked camps, drowned fords, and the smell of woodsmoke that may not come from friends.
Old and uneasy country; the ruins on the heights were Rhudaur's, and the shade of that evil kingdom has never quite left the hills.
A land of dripping woods and sudden hollows; by night the fires that show among the trees should be passed by, not approached.
Rain here is long and cold and fires will not light; winter fills the ravines with snow and the ways are treacherous until spring.

An ancient, dense dual stand of woods, it exudes unease and 'latent evil'. Home to Forest Trolls and huge wolves; its immense trees block most sunlight, leaving the interior perpetually dim. Some inner places are said never to be touched by sun or moonlight, and even Elves and Hillmen fear to enter.[file:132]

land.name: The Angle (lowlands between Mitheithel and Bruinen)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate grassland and light woodland with strong winds and limited fertile pockets along rivers
land.description: Rolling grassy hills south of the Coed Drug and between the rivers, broken by jagged fells and occasional stands of trees. Constant northeast winds and rain off the fells strip away topsoil, so agriculture is difficult except along relatively protected and fertile riverbanks. It forms Rhudaur’s main lowland and agricultural zone, albeit poor compared to the rest of Eriador.[file:132]

land.name: Oiolad ('Endless Plain' of the Eredoriath)
land.biome_hint: open grassland/plain adjoining Rhudaur, serving as raiding and travel corridor
land.description: Flat plain west of the Mitheithel beyond Rhudaur’s lowlands, used as raiding ground by the Rhudaurrim and Hillmen into more favored regions. While technically outside core Rhudaur, it is closely linked to its economy and warfare, providing a contrast to the rugged homeland fells.[file:132]

facts.notes: This object isolates Rhudaur as a region within Arnor: The Land, focusing on geographic subzones (Ettenmoors, Ettendales, Pinefells/Coldfells, Trollshaws, Coed Drug, Angle) and mapping the general Flora & Fauna of Eriador onto these specific landscapes. The key Rhudaur-specific ecological elements are the Pinefells evergreens, the Coed Drug ancient 'Evilwood', the losrandir herds and the concentration of Hill and Forest Trolls. Climate and hydrology are dominated by snow-fed highlands (Ettenmoors/Ettendales) and the swift Mitheithel, with constant winds limiting agriculture to narrow riverine bands.[file:132]

people.military: 4,500 Warriors and Eastern Mercenaries, usually grouped according to tribe.
people.population: 50,000: 35,000 Hillmen in thirteen tribes and 15,000 Dunlendings in eleven tribes.
people.description: Rhudaur’s population is sparse and concentrated in hill-country and strategic sites such as Cameth Brin and the Angle. Politically, it is the easternmost and least stable of Arnor’s successor realms, dominated by Hillmen and later influenced or controlled by Angmar. The Arnor book’s detailed cultural and political treatment is split across Arnor: The Land and Arnor: The People; here we focus on the geographic side, noting the Hillmen and Rhudaurrim as the characteristic inhabitants of this harsh landscape.

phrases: The Trollshaws in rain are a sodden cheerless maze of hills — soaked woods, rising fords, and no dry ground under heaven.
Winter locks the Trollshaws fast — black rock, white ravines, and the growl of streams half-frozen in their beds.
The cold gathers in the folds of the Trollshaws and stays; the caves breathe it and the paths are fangs of ice.

aspect.en: Rhudaur is the eastern successor state of Arnor, a rugged, sparsely settled land between the Ettenmoors, the Trollshaws and the Angle. It stretches from the Ettenmoors and Ettendales in the north down through the Pinefells and Trollshaws to the rolling lowlands between the rivers Mitheithel and Bruinen, forming a harsh frontier of jagged hills, evergreen forests, boggy vales and predator-haunted woodlands.

rotation: Northern moorlands of Rhudaur, windy peat-bogs and heather hills claimed by Trolls and Orcs since the fall of the Dúnedain. Brown water, grey horizons and the snow-capped Misty Mountains visible only on rare clear days.

Windy peat-bogs and heather hills on Rhudaur's northern edge, Orc and Troll country since the Dúnedain abandoned it. Brown water, grey horizons and the snow-capped Misty Mountains on the rare days it clears.

Heather and coarse grass on well-drained ground; blanket bog where the drainage fails, which is most places. The moors are traversable but slow, and they have the character of land that discourages lingering.
No trees of any size — the altitude and the wind combine to prevent it. The Misty Mountains form the southern horizon; Angmar's territory begins somewhere to the north with no visible marker.
Cold, wet and windy year-round. The altitude keeps the temperature down; the Atlantic weather keeps the moisture up. In winter the bog freezes in the night-frosts and partially thaws in the day.

Trolls and Orcs who have found the emptiness useful. No one patrols here; nothing maintains a claim. The moors belong to whoever is walking them at any given moment, which is usually something unpleasant.

land.name: Ettenmoors (Môr Ithvaen, 'Granite Sea')
land.biome_hint: cold, rocky highland with minimal soil, scattered hardy vegetation and extreme terrain
land.description: Northernmost highlands of Rhudaur, a landscape of large hills and boulder-strewn terrain created by the uplift of the Misty Mountains. Jagged, little-weathered fells hold very little topsoil; boulders from child-sized to villa-sized lie in 'crazy jumbles' through which passage is impossible for anything larger than a rabbit. The region is bleak, treacherous and ideal for Trolls and other large predators.[file:132]

land.name: Ettendales
land.biome_hint: cool, boggy hill region with springs, stagnant wetlands and patchy grass/heath
land.description: Hill country south of the Ettenmoors, with smaller hills and less granite. The Ettendales hold many springs feeding the Mitheithel but suffer from poor drainage; vales between hills contain stagnant bogs, especially during spring thaw. Despite their water resources, the bogs make travel dangerous and limit settlement.[file:132]

land.name: Pinefells / Coldfells
land.biome_hint: cool evergreen forested hills with well-drained soils and persistent cold winds
land.description: Highlands immediately south and east of the Ettendales, similar in structure but better drained and heavily wooded. Dominated by evergreen forests, the region is known as the Pinefells; others call them 'Coldfells' due to the legendary cool winds and waters. It forms a heavily forested, cold highland belt between the Ettendales and Trollshaws.[file:132]

land.name: Trollshaws
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate mosaic of wooded groves, brush and open grassland in broken hill terrain
land.description: Central Rhudaur between the Mitheithel and Bruinen, rugged hill country with woodland scattered across it. Trees form small dense patches separated by open ground; heavy brush along grove edges extends inward where canopy thins. Popular with wolves, it is also the winter ground for Rhudaur’s vast herds of losrandir and the favored haunt of Hill Trolls.[file:132]

land.name: Coed Drug ('Evilwood')
land.biome_hint: dark, old-growth forest with closed canopy, thick understorey and a supernatural atmosphere
land.description: The most significant forest in Rhudaur, growing on the southern side of the Trollshaws above the Great East Road. An ancient, dense dual stand of woods, it exudes unease and 'latent evil'. Home to Forest Trolls and huge wolves; its immense trees block most sunlight, leaving the interior perpetually dim. Some inner places are said never to be touched by sun or moonlight, and even Elves and Hillmen fear to enter.[file:132]

It forms Rhudaur’s main lowland and agricultural zone, albeit poor compared to the rest of Eriador.[file:132]
