aspect.en: The High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath, S. 'High-climbing Pass of the North') cuts through the central Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell and Eriador in the west to the upper Anduin Vales and Rhovanion in the east. It encompasses the Orcish stronghold of Goblin-gate, the eyrie of the Great Eagles, the Northman market-town of Maethelburg, the western foothills of Rhudaur, and the broad river plain of the Anduin. Geology consists of limestone and granite with massive igneous basalt intrusions. western foothills consist of red sandstone, while eastern valleys contain oily black shale; rich in copper, iron, silver, gold, and mithril.

rotation: Northern foothills of the Misty Mountains where bare rock and north wind admit neither comfort nor shelter. Mountain Orcs, wolves and Eagles are the chief inhabitants; the trails to the High Pass begin among this bare stone.

Northern foothills of the Misty Mountains where bare rock and north wind admit nothing gentle. Mountain Orcs, wolves and Great Eagles divide the altitude between them; the trails to the High Pass begin here.
Sparse alpine grass on the lower slopes, bare rock above. The treeline is lower here than anywhere on the range because the north wind comes off the Ettenmoors without warming.
The approach to the High Pass begins in these foothills, which means everything here is transitional — lower than the pass but already cold, exposed, and fundamentally unwelcoming.
Wind-scoured and cold, with snow possible in any month and reliable from autumn to late spring. The brief summer is more of a pause than a season.

Mountain Orcs using the cave-systems as bases; Great Eagles nesting on the highest crags; wolves that cross the pass in winter when the lower hunting is poor. No one here is particularly interested in human affairs.

land.name: Anduin Vales (eastern lowlands)
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with lush meadows, broadleaf groves, wetland margins and open farmland
land.description: The broad valley plain east of the Misty Mountains, gently sloping eastward and southward; easily traversed open terrain with grassy meadows, river marshes, elm and oak groves, and scattered Northman homesteads and trading towns. Maethelburg is the main settlement, a fortified hill-town at the confluence of the Anduin and Sirros (Foamflood). The Great River here is the main highway, plied by Northman cnearras (shallow-draught clinker-built craft) trading between Maethelburg and Gondor.[file:88]

land.name: Western Foothills of Rhudaur
land.biome_hint: cold Atlantic-type rugged moorland and forested ravines with bog, heather and ancient conifer cover
land.description: The rugged, forested foothills and moorland west of the Misty Mountains in the territory of Rhudaur; grim stony heights, deep ravines, ancient pine-shrouded valleys and heather-covered moorland, cut by treacherous bogs. Home to Hillmen clans and prowled by Stone-trolls and Orcs at night; nearly impassable without a guide except along the Great East Road (which ends at the Ford of Bruinen).[file:88]

land.name: High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath)
land.biome_hint: subarctic alpine pass with permanent snowcaps, glaciers, scree slopes and fierce storm exposure
land.description: A double-branched pass through the Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell to the Anduin: the lower branch (Pass of Imladris, c.3,500 ft) permits horses and wagons but is controlled by Goblin-gate at its summit; the upper mountain-path (over 5,000 ft) is passable only on foot or by mule/pony, steep and exposed to storms but less Orc-infested. Both branches are snow-blocked from Hithui to Gwirith. The pass is riddled with scree, avalanche risk, tumbling boulders and the constant threat of Giants above and Orcs below.[file:88]

land.name: Goblin-Gate (Goblin-town underground)
land.biome_hint: karst limestone cave system with ice caves (upper), inhabited city levels, fungi caves, and deep mine shafts
land.description: A vast network of natural limestone caverns expanded and connected by Orcish mining over millennia, stretching up to 40 miles between the Wolf Gate (main western entrance at the pass summit) and the Back Door (eastern exit to the Anduin slopes), with further passages to the Fungi Caves, Mine levels, and reputed deep shafts connecting to the Underdeeps of Moria. At T.A. 1640: the Great Goblin rules from the City Level; Gollum has not yet arrived (that happens c.T.A. 2470). Underground lakes, underground rivers, stalactites, ice caves (upper levels), massive fungi forests (lower levels) and deep mine shafts all present in the complex.[file:88]

land.name: Eagles' Eyrie (Amon Thyrir pinnacle)
land.biome_hint: bare alpine rock pinnacle above the tree line, surrounded by high-altitude thermals and glaciated peaks
land.description: A solitary rock pinnacle rising above the mountain crags east of the High Pass, inaccessible except by flight; crowned by the vast bowl-shaped nest (up to 40 ft diameter, several tons) of the Lord of the Eagles. The surrounding high peaks and thermal columns of warm rising air are the domain of a small population of Great Eagles, each controlling a territory of 200+ sq miles of mountain terrain.[file:88]

land.name: Giants' Isle (mountain vale)
land.biome_hint: remote high-altitude vale with rock, scree, glacial streams and no human habitation
land.description: A secluded area of high mountain vales where Stone Giants are concentrated; largely avoided by all other peoples. The Giants hurl boulders during thunderstorms and have occupied these heights since the First Age. No settlement is possible here.[file:88]

facts.notes: This module is centered on T.A. 1640 (primary time period), with additional adventures set in T.A. 2940 (time of The Hobbit, when Gollum is already in the caves and Thorin's company passes through) and F.A. 1. The fauna and flora data reflect the T.A. 1640 baseline. Goblin-gate's internal geography is partially procedurally generated (Random Features Table in the module) and not fully fixed on maps—only key route passages are mapped. The region connects westward to Rivendell/Eriador and eastward to northern Mirkwood via Maethelburg and the Old Ford, making it a critical chokepoint on the Misty Mountains.[file:88] The longest and highest mountain chain in the west, serving as a formidable glacial barrier between Eriador and Rhovanion. Heavy snows and glaciers cover peaks above 11,500 feet year-round. It is riddled with Orc-holds, Dwarven caverns, and the under-deeps.

people.military: 100 Beornings. 60 Burgwards of Maethelburg. 900 Militia (3-4 weeks to raise, organized by clan). 135 Eagles (allies).
people.description: The region is sparsely populated by several distinct peoples: Northmen (Nenedain) in the Anduin Vales, Beornings on the eastern bank, Hillmen in the rough hills of Rhudaur, and Orcs in the mountain strongholds, alongside rarer presences of Elves, Dwarves, Giants and Eagles.

facts.products: Grain, hides, cattle, honey, amber, tin.

aspect.en: Angmar is a cold, militarized realm north of Arnor, ruled by the Witch-king of the Nazgûl; it exists primarily as a war machine, built on harsh land, hardened frontier peasants, and armies of men, orcs, and monsters. Geology consists of deeply eroded limestone that robs the surface soil of water, with igneous and metamorphic outcrops near the mountains. carn dûm is built on a massive block of dull red granite.

rotation: The Witch-king's war realm of grey walls, muddy camps and enforced misery. Carn Dûm sits on dark red granite among mountains that cage everyone within. Cold, Orcs and fear are the three pillars of Angmar.

The Witch-king's domain: dark granite mountains, muddy camps and a cold that has moral weight. Carn Dûm sits on red rock above everything; the mountains form a wall that keeps both weather and people inside.

Despite Angmar's grimness, the Dúnedain who fight here know every herb that grows in the frozen margins — aloe in sheltered courtyards, athelas where the rock-springs emerge. Survival knowledge dressed as botany.

Carn Dûm on the heights; fortified villages below it; patrol roads connecting everything. The landscape has been organized for warfare and nothing else; every feature serves a military purpose or is ignored.

Arctic cold from the Forodwaith to the north, channelled and concentrated by the mountain walls. Mean temperatures that kill the careless; blizzards that move in within hours. The cold is not a backdrop — it is a weapon.

Orcs, fear and subjugated human peasants doing the farming that keeps the armies fed. The ordinary life of Angmar runs on the same machinery as any other kingdom; it is just organized around malice instead of anything else.

land.name: Angmar (general region)
land.biome_hint: cold frontier land with tundra, rocky hills, and scattered forests
land.description: Harsh territory north of Arnor with poor soils, severe climate, and primarily military function; described as land where only hardened peasants can survive and where warfare is an accepted part of life.

land.name: Fortified frontier villages
land.biome_hint: small agricultural pockets in cold, windswept valleys and slopes
land.description: Small walled communities tied as fiefs to one of three frontier castles; each village must patrol its surroundings daily, escort supply trains, and supply soldiers for campaigns.

land.name: Agricultural fields of Angmar
land.biome_hint: marginal agriculture on cold plateaus and valley bottoms
land.description: Small fields bounded by low stone walls to break the wind; rye, barley, oats, potatoes, cabbage, turnips, and beets form the basic crops, supplemented by peas, beans, occasional eggs, and hardy apple trees.

land.name: Border castles of Angmar
land.biome_hint: stone strongholds on hills or rocky spurs in severe climate
land.description: Three major castles guard the borders, collect tribute, coordinate conscription and supplies, and rule the villages; examples include Morkai and Eldanar, with multi-level donjons and complex defenses.

land.name: Carn Dûm
land.biome_hint: mountain fortress in subarctic conditions, with steep access routes
land.description: Capital fortress-city of Angmar in the northern mountains, with extensive outer and inner defenses; principal political, military, and logistical center of the Witch-king.

land.name: No Man’s Land of Angmar
land.biome_hint: broken, cold uplands and ravines designed for defense-in-depth
land.description: Border buffer zone marked by towers, small keeps like Cargash Keep, and minor castles like Eldanar, serving as a defensive cushion and theatre for raids and skirmishes.

land.name: Streams and rivers of Angmar
land.biome_hint: cold streams in narrow valleys with sparse but important riparian vegetation
land.description: Network of cold streams with shaded banks where mosses like Attanar and other herbs grow; provide fish for bears and villagers as a key food source.

facts.notes: This object treats Angmar as a political and geographic region in the mid-Third Age at the height of the Witch-king’s power; subregions such as Carn Dûm or specific castles can be split into separate site objects for higher resolution. A rocky, barren, and bleak highland plateau with frozen soil, little water, and severe wood shortages. Populated by Orcs, Trolls, and dark-hearted Men who serve the Iron Crown of Carn Dûm.

people.description: Angmar’s population mixes free and enslaved men with strong contingents of professional soldiers and ex-soldiers from warrior cultures such as Rhudaur, Rûn, and the Estarav of the Anduin, supported by orcs, trolls, and other creatures in the Witch-king’s service.

aspect.en: Ered Luin, also known as the Blue Mountains, is an ancient mountain range separating Lindon from Eriador. Extending 590 miles from the Ice Bay of Forochel down to Orod Elu in the south, the range is formed of grey rock with a bluish tint caused by a high concentration of copper ores. The mountains are riddled with natural caverns, marble and limestone formations, and once held precious metals, though Dwarvish mining has left them depleted of gold except for minor remote veins. Geology consists of marble and limestone with folded sandstone and shale foothills. abundant copper, iron, and tin ores are actively mined by the dwarves (naugrim).

rotation: The Blue Mountains and green Lindon between them and the Sea — the last piece of drowned Beleriand, split by the Gulf of Lhûn where the water comes far inland.
Tall pine-woods and oakwoods on the seaward slopes, older than any other living woods in the west. The range itself is old and worn, its peaks low and blue in the sea-haze.
West of the gulf lie the Grey Havens and the white quays; the ships that leave them do not return. The road to the water is the oldest road still travelled.
Dwarf-halls and elven havens share the land — the mountains hold the mansions of old Nogrod's kin, and the coast keeps the last ports of the Eldar.
Sea-weather rules here — long grey rains, salt wind, snow that lies long on the high moors but rarely in the sheltered vales.
Everything in Lindon smells of the Sea; even the mountain streams run with a salt wind behind them, and the sunsets over the water are the last sight of the world.

land.name: Northern Ered Luin peaks
land.biome_hint: alpine peaks with year-round ice caps and glaciers
land.description: The taller northern section of the range, home to the peak of Lossotil (9,497 feet) and several glacial ice fields.

land.name: Southern Ered Luin peaks
land.biome_hint: sub-alpine peaks with seasonal winter snow
land.description: The lower southern section of the range, including Orod Elu (6,824 feet), which experiences seasonal winter snow cover.

facts.notes: Ered Luin stands as a vital mining zone and barrier separating Lindon from Eriador, with secret, rune-guarded passes. The Blue Mountains are ancient and run north-to-south, heavily composed of marble and limestone with massive natural caverns. Snowfields and icecaps are present year-round on the northern range, while pine trees disappear over 5,000 feet. Mineral copper deposits give the peaks their bluish tint.

people.symbol: A Hammer surmounted by Three Tongues of Flame
people.military: 490 Warriors. 2,100 Warrior Levy.
people.description: The Ered Luin is primarily inhabited by the Dwarves of Nogrod and Belegost's descendants, alongside scattered Elven wanderers and mountain Giants.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

facts.products: Finished goods, iron, tin, copper, lead.

phrases: Winter on the Blue Mountains is the Sea's winter — grey water, white ridges, and a wind that has come a thousand miles over the waves.
Rain on Lindon is the Sea sent over the mountains — long grey veils, dripping woods, and the white road to the Havens running wet.
The cold here is a salt cold off the Sea; it fills the gulf and climbs the blue slopes, and the ships at the Havens tug at their moorings in the ice-wind.

aspect.en: Numeriador is the cold, rugged, and wind-swept northern plateau of Eriador, lying north of the Hills of Evendim. It is a sparsely populated, rolling wilderness of grasses and stunted shrubs, once part of the kingdom of Arnor.

rotation: Cold, wind-swept plateau north of the Hills of Evendim, the edge of the inhabited world before Forochel. Thin soil over rock, juniper scrub, scarce shepherds and wolves that grow bolder every winter.

Cold wind-swept plateau at the edge of the inhabited world, just north of the Hills of Evendim. Thin soil over granite, juniper and heather as far as the eye carries, and wolves that grow bolder through winter.

Dwarf-willow and wild rye in the hollows; hardy moss on the exposed rock; the occasional juniper bush that has made itself indistinguishable from the surrounding stone. The vegetation is honest about how little encourages it.
Granite plateau with the Ered Luin visible to the west and Forochel beginning somewhere to the north without a clear border. The land becomes bleaker in a gradient that has no visible bottom.
Short cold summers, long dark winters. The growing season is barely sufficient for what grows here naturally; nothing was ever farmed on this plateau and nothing ever will be.
Scattered shepherds who follow their flocks between the marginal pastures and retreat to lower ground in winter. Wandering Dúnedain Rangers who use the emptiness as cover. Wolves.

land.name: Numeriador Steppes
land.biome_hint: semi-arid cold steppe with sparse thorny scrub and high exposure
land.description: The open, flat, and cold grasslands extending north toward Forochel.

facts.notes: Numeriador acts as a vast, lawless buffer zone between Arnor and the frozen north.

people.military: None.
people.description: Sparsely populated by wandering hillmen and isolated shepherds.

aspect.en: Lindon is the westernmost Elvish realm of Middle-earth, the remnant of Ossiriand that survived the War of Wrath. After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Northernmost sub-region of Forlindon, the most rain-swept and mist-prone part of Lindon. Moss-bogs, heath and silver birches in sheltered valleys; rounded hills of intense green grass and a watchful silence facing the wild north.

Northern Forlindon, the most rain-swept part of Lindon. Moss-bogs and silver birch in sheltered valleys; rounded green hills of intense colour that come from permanent moisture and the particular quality of northern light.

Heath and sedge-bog on the exposed ground; birch and alder in the valley-bottoms where the drainage improves. The constant drizzle keeps everything intensely green in a way the southern Lindon regions don't quite achieve.

The northernmost inhabited part of Lindon, with the coast immediately to the west and the Ered Luin to the east. The hills are rounded and old, their harshness smoothed by a geological time that precedes the Elves.
Cold, wet and grey for most of the year, with the Atlantic feeding moisture into the coast from the west and the mountains catching the clouds from the east. Summer is real but brief and mild.
The quietest part of a quiet land. Elves who live here chose the rain and the silence and have made something of both.

land.name: Forlindon (North Lindon)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate coastal and lowland zone with maritime influence transitioning to colder mountain foothills
land.description: The northern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, including coastal plains and the northern Blue Mountain foothills. Historically the primary home of the Noldor (Godhellim) in the realm, it contains harbors and settlements connected to Mithlond and is treated in the government section as a distinct administrative region.[file:99]

land.name: Harlindon (South Lindon)
land.biome_hint: mild, wet coastal strip with forests and rural Elven settlements around secondary harbors
land.description: The southern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, associated with Sindar and Laiquendi (Iathrim, Laegrim). It combines coastal stretches and forested lowlands, was once a fief under Celeborn, and is portrayed as more rural and woodland-oriented than Forlindon.[file:99]

land.name: Rhûnlindon (east-of-Lhûn / Blue Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cool to cold mountain zone with conifer forests, winter snow and extensive mining
land.description: The part of Lindon’s sphere east of the River Lhûn, including the eastern Blue Mountains with Dwarven halls and some Elven refuges. Population tables assign Rhûnlindon about 10% of Lindon’s population, with climate corresponding to the Ered Luin band (colder winters, moderate summers, 30–40 inches of precipitation).[^file99]

land.name: Mithlond (Grey Havens)
land.biome_hint: maritime urban enclave with sheltered harbor, mild wet climate and intensive shipbuilding
land.description: The principal harbor city at the head of the Gulf of Lhûn, seat of Círdan in the Third Age and the main port for Elves and Ring-bearers departing to Valinor. Population tables show Mithlond comprising 20–25% of Lindon’s inhabitants in the Third Age (and 9–10% in the Second Age), emphasizing its central role in Lindon’s demography and economy.[file:99]

land.name: Taeg Lindon routes and refuges
land.biome_hint: mixed grassland, forest and hill country between the Misty Mountains and the Ered Luin, with hidden Elven refuges
land.description: The 'Bounds of Lindon' section describes the Wandering Companies’ preferred route from Imladris to Mithlond: across Eregion, the Mitheithel ford south of Fennas Drúnin, the South Downs and Barrow-downs (with stops near Tom Bombadil’s house), then either through the Old Forest and Green Hills or along the Brandywine’s eastern shore before turning west to the Ered Luin. Along roughly 600 miles they maintain rustic camps and more elaborate permanent refuges (glades, caves, small houses) 20–30 miles apart, some shared with Rangers after the fall of Arthedain.[file:99]

facts.notes: This Lindon work is an unlicensed, non-commercial fan-made Realm (version 3.2, 2023) rather than an original ICE product, but it is structured like a MERP Realm and synthesizes Tolkien canon with MERP-style material. For your Middle-earth-on-Europe map, Lindon should be treated as one macro-region with internal subregions (Forlindon, Harlindon, Rhûnlindon) sharing a maritime temperate climate, and Mithlond explicitly marked as a major harbor node. aspect.en: Parth Celebrant, the Field of Celebrant, is a wide, rolling grassy plain nestled between the Great River Anduin and the Limlight. It is famous as the historical battleground where Eorl the Young led the Éothéod to save the armies of Gondor, leading to the gift of Rohan.

rotation: The Field of Celebrant — open grassland and groves between the River and the mountains' feet, where the North Kingdom was broken and the Eorlingas came down out of the north.
Thick turf over old graves; the mounds under the grass mark where a battle was lost and then miraculously won. The grass is a little greener on the field of the ride.
Oak and beech clothe the lower slopes; the high ground is bare down and sheep-walk under a wide sky, with the mountains standing close and white to the north.
The old road-line is still legible under the turf — a pale green scar running north, where the forts of the fallen kingdom kept their last watch.
A clean cold wind comes off the mountains and crosses the open field; the larks are up in summer and the grass lies flat under the winter rain.
A fair field with a sad memory; the River runs at its feet and the mountains stand at its back, and the world between them is green and empty.

land.name: Celebrant Plain
land.biome_hint: rolling grasslands and alluvial fields with high exposure
land.description: The historic, rolling battlefield between the rivers.

facts.notes: Parth Celebrant remains a highly revered historic site, commemorating the ancient alliance between Rohan and Gondor.

people.symbol: White Horse on a Green Field
people.military: Mounted Eoreds (patrols).
people.population: Sparsely populated (military outposts and nomadic herders).
people.description: Inhabited by Rohirrim horsemen and patrols from Gondor/Rohan.

source.supplement: Rohan: The Land of the Horse-Lords

phrases: The Field of Celebrant lies open to the winter wind; the old defeat is only a greener line in the dead grass, and the mountains are white and near.
In summer the field is a green and golden sea; the larks are up, and the old scars are hidden in flower and leaf.
The cold rides down off the mountains and across the open field; there is no shelter on the grass, and the sky is pale iron.

aspect.en: En Udanoriath, meaning the 'No-Man's-Land' or the 'Dwelling-less Waste', is a bleak, barren, and wind-scarred frontier zone located between the southern border of Angmar and the northern boundaries of Arthedain (near the North Downs). This cold highland waste is a desolate, rocky steppe plagued by bitter northern winds and constant military skirmishes. It serves as a buffer and raiding corridor where the Witch-king's patrols clash with Arnor's remnants, overseen by spy-towers like Mindil Cargash.

rotation: Barren steppe buffer zone between Angmar and the North Downs of Arthedain, the Witch-king's raiding corridor. Rocky and wind-scoured, with spy-towers disguised as ruins; in winter the blizzard kills in the open within hours.

Barren steppe buffer zone between Angmar and the North Downs, the Witch-king's raiding corridor. Rocky, wind-scoured, with spy-towers disguised as ruins; the blizzard can kill in the open within hours in winter.

Minimal tundra vegetation — moss, stunted grass, the occasional hardy scrub in a wind-shadow. The land offers nothing except transit; it has been used for transit since Angmar found it useful as a corridor.

Flat ground between two higher territories with no natural feature to encourage stopping. The ruined towers along the edge could be old Dúnedain watchtowers or Angmar's eyes dressed in old stone; in practice the distinction is academic.

The worst of the cold channels through here between the northern wastes and Arthedain. Wind chill rather than ambient temperature is the danger; the wind off the Forodwaith comes through without obstacle.
Nobody lives here by choice. Angmar's patrols move through; Ranger scouts move through. The steppe is defined entirely by what it connects.

land.name: En Udanoriath Frontier
land.biome_hint: cold, dry highland plateau with shattered boulders and howling winds
land.description: The desolate, rocky plateau between Angmar and Arthedain.

facts.notes: A highly dangerous warfront where any travelers are viewed as spies and hunted down.

people.military: Sauron's orc warbands, warg-riders, Ranger scouts.
people.description: Entirely devoid of permanent settlements; traversed only by soldiers, orc warbands, and Dunlending mercenaries.

aspect.en: Lindon is the westernmost Elvish realm of Middle-earth, the remnant of Ossiriand that survived the War of Wrath. After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Inner Forlindon along the Linduin, a land of constant drizzle and moss-green on every surface. Damp heather hills, pool-fed waterfalls in side valleys and Elvish homes built to face the sound of water. The quiet, rainy heart of Lindon.

Inner Forlindon along the Linduin river, where moss covers every surface and the constant drizzle is simply the weather. Damp heather hills, pool-fed waterfalls in side valleys and Elvish homes oriented toward the sound of water.

The Linduin runs through the centre of it, small but persistent. Its tributaries feed the bog-pools and the bog-pools feed the atmosphere. Everything here is damp to the touch; the moss is measured in inches rather than millimetres.

The valley opens east-west and the rain comes in from the Atlantic and stays. The hills funnel it down; the bog holds it. The result is a permanent dampness that the Elves here have made central to their aesthetic.

Mild winters, cool summers, persistent drizzle. No extremes; just the slow accumulation of moisture through every season. The plants that thrive here are the plants that have made peace with never being dry.

Sindar who chose this valley for its particular quality of sound — rain on moss, water on stone, the Linduin on its gravel-bed. They've lived inside that sound long enough to find silence uncomfortable.

land.name: Forlindon (North Lindon)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate coastal and lowland zone with maritime influence transitioning to colder mountain foothills
land.description: The northern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, including coastal plains and the northern Blue Mountain foothills. Historically the primary home of the Noldor (Godhellim) in the realm, it contains harbors and settlements connected to Mithlond and is treated in the government section as a distinct administrative region.[file:99]

land.name: Harlindon (South Lindon)
land.biome_hint: mild, wet coastal strip with forests and rural Elven settlements around secondary harbors
land.description: The southern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, associated with Sindar and Laiquendi (Iathrim, Laegrim). It combines coastal stretches and forested lowlands, was once a fief under Celeborn, and is portrayed as more rural and woodland-oriented than Forlindon.[file:99]

land.name: Rhûnlindon (east-of-Lhûn / Blue Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cool to cold mountain zone with conifer forests, winter snow and extensive mining
land.description: The part of Lindon’s sphere east of the River Lhûn, including the eastern Blue Mountains with Dwarven halls and some Elven refuges. Population tables assign Rhûnlindon about 10% of Lindon’s population, with climate corresponding to the Ered Luin band (colder winters, moderate summers, 30–40 inches of precipitation).[^file99]

land.name: Mithlond (Grey Havens)
land.biome_hint: maritime urban enclave with sheltered harbor, mild wet climate and intensive shipbuilding
land.description: The principal harbor city at the head of the Gulf of Lhûn, seat of Círdan in the Third Age and the main port for Elves and Ring-bearers departing to Valinor. Population tables show Mithlond comprising 20–25% of Lindon’s inhabitants in the Third Age (and 9–10% in the Second Age), emphasizing its central role in Lindon’s demography and economy.[file:99]

land.name: Taeg Lindon routes and refuges
land.biome_hint: mixed grassland, forest and hill country between the Misty Mountains and the Ered Luin, with hidden Elven refuges
land.description: The 'Bounds of Lindon' section describes the Wandering Companies’ preferred route from Imladris to Mithlond: across Eregion, the Mitheithel ford south of Fennas Drúnin, the South Downs and Barrow-downs (with stops near Tom Bombadil’s house), then either through the Old Forest and Green Hills or along the Brandywine’s eastern shore before turning west to the Ered Luin. Along roughly 600 miles they maintain rustic camps and more elaborate permanent refuges (glades, caves, small houses) 20–30 miles apart, some shared with Rangers after the fall of Arthedain.[file:99]

rotation: The most storm-exposed coast of Forlindon, ironically named the Land of the Bright Sun. Thirty-metre cliff-waves in winter, tree-bending westerlies, but in calm the sea turns to living silver and the clifftops to emerald. A land of extremes.

The most storm-exposed coast of Forlindon, ironically named the Land of the Bright Sun. Thirty-metre cliff-waves in the worst of the Atlantic winter; tree-bending westerlies; but in calm the sea turns to living silver.
Heath and gorse on the clifftops, wind-pruned and horizontal in growth habit. The trees gave up on the exposed ground a long time ago; only in the sheltered lee-valleys do they stand upright.
Vertical dark cliffs dropping into green-blue water, with sea-spray reaching the clifftops on rough days. The violence and the beauty operate on exactly the same principle: scale and indifference.

The most dramatic weather in Lindon, concentrated on a coast that faces into the Atlantic storms without any mitigation. The calm days that give the region its ironic name are real; they're also outnumbered.

The Elves who live here came because of the extremity, not in spite of it. They find something valuable in the contrast between the winter storms and the days when the sea goes still and bright. The name isn't entirely sarcastic.

rotation: The most settled sub-region of Forlindon, mild and green thanks to the Gulf of Lhûn. Oak forests and clover meadows, the oldest and best-preserved Elvish settlements in northern Lindon and the road to the port of Forlond.

Southernmost Forlindon, mild and green thanks to the Gulf. The oldest Elvish settlements in northern Lindon sit among oak forest and clover meadow; the road to Forlond passes through here and the port gives it a connection the other sub-regions lack.
Oak forest with a relatively open understorey; clover in the meadows between the trees. The most cultivated part of Lindon outside the immediate surrounds of Mithlond itself.
The Gulf of Lhûn buffers the worst of the Atlantic weather; the Ered Luin to the east blocks the continental cold. The result is a climate that is genuinely mild rather than merely not-extreme.
The longest growing season in Lindon. Mild winters that rarely freeze; summers warm enough to be pleasant. The Elves here have had time to establish an aesthetic and they've done so.
The oldest Elvish community in northern Lindon, connected to the wider world through Forlond's port. They have watched ships come and go for a long time; it has not made them incurious.

aspect.en: Talath Muil ('Drear Plain') is the rugged highland plain forming the northwestern marches of Arthedain, dividing northern Arthedain from the Wash Tundra and the Vale of the Lhûn. It is a windswept, largely treeless upland of low grass and open grassland, dotted with large wildflower meadows and small copses of ash and birch. To the east it abuts the rocky western edges of the northern Hills of Evendim, whose rough ground is difficult to traverse even on foot, and whose rocky hills gradually mellow into grass-covered downs and finally spill northeast into the dry plateau of the Rammas Forod.

rotation: High windswept plateau on the northwest marches of Arthedain, with short grass, wildflower meadows and ash groves bent eastward by the constant west wind. Wide and silent; the Ered Luin visible on clear days to the south.
High windswept plateau on the northwest marches of Arthedain, with the west wind bending every ash and birch permanently eastward. Wide and silent, with the Ered Luin a line on the southern horizon.
Low grasses and wildflowers in brief spring bloom; gorse and heather through the rest of the year. Small copses of wind-bent ash in the depressions where the soil is deep enough to support them.
Flat and open in a way that few places in Arthedain are. The view in all directions is clear; the exposure to the west wind is total. A landscape that keeps no secrets about itself.

The wind arrives from the Atlantic with nothing to slow it between the coast and the plateau. Cold and persistent; the warmth of summer barely dents it. The wildflowers of spring are the plateau's only real concession to gentleness.

Shepherds and the occasional Dúnedain patrol. Nobody lives here in winter if they can avoid it; the summer grazing is good enough to bring people back. The plateau has the patient character of land that has been used but never loved.

land.name: Talath Muil upland (Drear Plain)
land.biome_hint: cold, windswept upland grassland with low vegetation and frequent fog/drizzle
land.description: The core rugged highland plain forming the northwestern marches of Arthedain, an open, windswept grassland with low vegetation and occasional wildflower meadows, shunned even by the hardy Lossoth.[file:179]

land.name: Rocky western edges of the northern Evendim Hills
land.biome_hint: rocky upland fringe with thin soils, scrub and grass patches, used as lairs by hostile creatures
land.description: A rough, rocky zone where Talath Muil meets the western faces of the northern Hills of Evendim. Difficult to traverse, it offers hiding places for Orcs, Trolls and bandits, but winter cold can make it deadly.[file:179]

land.name: Grass-covered downs (eastern transition)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate downs with grasses and scattered shrubs, less severe than the drear plain
land.description: As the northern Evendim hills spread eastward from Talath Muil, they become less rocky and barren, melding into a low line of grass-covered downs that link the upland to the more hospitable Emyn Uial/Twilight Hills and central Arthedain.[file:179]

land.name: Rammas Forod plateau edge
land.biome_hint: cold, dry plateau edge with sparse grasses and low shrubs, leading towards tundra
land.description: The northeastern spillover of the hills onto the great dry plateau of Rammas Forod, marking the transition from Talath Muil’s drear uplands into a broader dry steppe plateau bordering the Wash Tundra and far north.[file:179][file:132]

facts.notes: Talath Muil, as framed here, is a cold, foggy, windswept upland between Arthedain and the far northern tundra, ecologically distinct from the more populated Evendim Hills and Emyn Uial. For your map and climate model (Third Age, pre-War of the Ring), treat it as a marginal, low-productivity biome with strong wind exposure, constant damp, and limited human presence, but with important military and ecological links to the Hills of Evendim, Rammas Forod and the Wash Tundra.[file:179][file:132]

people.description: Talath Muil sits at the far edge of Arthedain’s settled world. It has no dense population; its human presence consists of frontier shepherds, border watchposts and moving armies during the wars against Angmar. Even hardy Lossoth avoid this 'drear plain.'

source.supplement: Arnor: The Land (compilation from Rangers of the North / Angmar-related material)

aspect.en: The Rammas Forod (Sindarin 'Great Wall of the North'; Adûnaic Ramênytunêny, actually 'South-wall') is a low chain of hills dividing the down-lands of northern Arthedain from the watershed of the Wash Tundra. To the west it widens into the Talath Muil, while to the east its hills thin out and merge into the Everlasting Plain. Born as debris from the collapse of the Iron Mountains in the War of Wrath, the ridge has shed rock and soil into the valleys on either side, allowing modest forests to grow along its flanks. Clear air and narrow defiles offer room for small farms and gardens, and for a time the Rammas served as a religious retreat for the Faithful of Arnor.

rotation: Natural limestone escarpment crossing northern Arthedain, the kingdom's first geological line of defence. Blackthorn and hawthorn on its slopes, few watched passes and the sensation of crossing a threshold into colder country.

Limestone escarpment crossing northern Arthedain, the kingdom's first geological boundary. Blackthorn and hawthorn on the slopes, with few passes watched and the threshold feeling of crossing from one kind of country into a colder one.

The escarpment supports a sudden burst of spring vegetation on its south face — blackthorn, hawthorn, wildflowers in the limestone crevices. The north face is bare and the wind off it is a different quality of cold.
A natural wall of pale limestone with a sharp break in topography. South of it, the cultivated land of Arthedain; north of it, the increasingly empty and cold ground toward the northern frontiers.

The south face catches sun and shelter; the north face catches everything that comes down from Forochel. The difference in microclimate between the two sides of the escarpment is visible in what grows.

Watched passes rather than continuous wall; a patrol-point rather than a fortification. The Dúnedain who monitor the crossings know which passes are used and by whom, and that knowledge is the defence.

land.name: Main Rammas ridge
land.biome_hint: cold, semi-arid ridge and plateau with short-season grasses, spring blooms and expansive views
land.description: The primary low hill line that separates northern Arthedain’s down-lands from the Wash Tundra watershed. Formed from the wreckage of the Iron Mountains, it acts as a natural 'great wall' with slopes that drop into sediment-filled valleys hosting small forests and farms.

land.name: Western widening into Talath Muil
land.biome_hint: transition from dry ridge to colder, windier upland grassland tied to Talath Muil
land.description: To the west, the ridge broadens and grades into the Talath Muil, the drear, windswept upland plain that connects the Rammas to the Evendim Hills and the valley of the Lhûn.

land.name: Eastern fade into the Everlasting Plain
land.biome_hint: cold, dry plain edge extending the steppe-like regime beyond the ridge
land.description: To the east, the hills diminish and gradually blend into the Everlasting Plain, a wide interior expanse that carries the Rammas’s steppe-like character out onto a broader, lower plateau with even fewer structural breaks.

land.name: Valleys and defiles with forests and farms
land.biome_hint: relatively greener microclimates embedded in an otherwise dry upland, with small woods and intensive plots
land.description: On both sides of the ridge, erosion has created valleys and narrow defiles where transported soil accumulates. These niches support small forests and patches of farmland or gardens and host religious houses, isolated farmsteads and Lumënyihmënyt camps.

facts.notes: In your climate and biome model, Rammas Forod should be treated as a cold, semi-arid plateau and ridge system under strong rain shadow, with a very short green season, long dry periods and snowy, windy winters. It is also a key military and cultural frontier between Arthedain and Angmar and a corridor where garrisons, religious communities and Lumënyihmënyt hunters overlap, all in the Third Age before the War of the Ring.

people.description: In the late Third Age before the War of the Ring, the Rammas Forod functions as both a fortified frontier between Arthedain and Angmar and a zone of religious retreat. Permanent population is sparse, concentrated in strongpoints, tiny farmsteads in sheltered defiles and seasonal hunter camps along the northern edge.

source.supplement: Arnor: The Land (with material from Rangers of the North / Northern Waste / Angmar)

aspect.en: The Evendim Hills (Sindarin Emyn Uial, 'Hills of Twilight') are the upland region around the valley of the Cornalas and the northern shore of Lake Evendim (Nenuial) in western Arthedain. For one season they are pale brown under constant cool mists cupped in the valley, for another they lie soft and white under snow, and in the Awakening and the Poem the valley becomes a shifting tapestry of lush greens. Though unproductive by southern standards—steep hillsides strain shepherds’ knees and narrow vales have thin soil—the hills have long been the heart of Arthedain, their rippling waters and mists inspiring poets and musicians.

rotation: Hills encircling Lake Nenuial in western Arthedain, with the marble ruins of Annúminas on the southern shore. Silver mist on full-moon nights wrapping the ruins in ghostly light; great beauty and greater melancholy.

Hills around Lake Nenuial, with the marble ruins of Annúminas on the southern shore. The lake is large enough to generate its own mist; on full-moon nights the ruins emerge from it and submerge again as the light shifts.

Gorse and heather on the exposed upper slopes; the lakeside has been allowed to naturalise into meadow and alder-wood over the generations since Annúminas was abandoned. The ruins make sense as part of the landscape now.

Lake Nenuial fills a glacial basin with no obvious outflow; the Nenuial has its own weather, its own mist, its own quality of reflection. The hills around it are incidental to the lake's dominant presence.
Cool and damp, moderated by the lake. The hills get more snow than the lakeside; the lake rarely freezes completely. Annúminas stands in water-mist through most of the year.

Almost no one lives here permanently except the rangers who visit the ruins and the lake-fishermen who work the Nenuial from small boats. The beauty is real and the melancholy is real and neither cancels the other.

land.name: Cornalas valley
land.biome_hint: cool, mist-filled upland valley with bogs, terraced fields and mixed shrub/grass cover
land.description: A central valley of the Evendim Hills where cool mists are 'cupped in the valley like wine in a goblet,' muting sounds and painting the landscape pale brown in one season, white in another and lush green in the Awakening and the Poem. Boggy ground and terraced fields coexist here under constant damp.[file:179]

land.name: Twilight Hills (Emyn Uial) proper
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate upland hills with mixed managed and wild vegetation, high rainfall and strong seasonality
land.description: Steep hills with narrow vales and thin soils, surrounded by stone-walled fields and terraces, planted groves and ubiquitous gorse, heather and grass. The hills give an impression of wildness despite human works; steadings are typically a half-day’s march apart.[file:179]

land.name: Roads and terraces network
land.biome_hint: human-modified upland landscape with intensive small-scale agriculture and infrastructure
land.description: Hardpacked earth roads on flat ground and stone-shouldered, paved roads on steep sections tie the hills together, allowing travellers to 'always arrive where they are headed.' Terraces and retaining walls support fields, but frost-heaves and erosion constantly push rocks up and wash soil away.[file:179]

facts.notes: For your climate and biome system, treat the Evendim Hills (Emyn Uial) as a cool, maritime upland with high rainfall, heavy seasonal mist and snow, and a strong human imprint through terraces and roads, yet always on the edge of rewilding by gorse, heather and grass. In the pre–War of the Ring Third Age, they are still inhabited and functioning as a heartland of Arthedain, though already feeling the strain of colder winters and creeping decline.[file:179]

people.description: The Evendim Hills (Emyn Uial) are home primarily to the Commons of Arthedain—the hillfolk of the Twilight Hills—with stern but just Dúnedain lords. Their culture is shaped by hard labour, cool damp climate and relative peace under Arthadan rule. Later, wars and the Banes of Angmar depopulate the hills, but in your period they remain a living, if harsh, homeland.

source.supplement: Arnor: The Land (compilation from Rangers of the North, Lost Realm of Cardolan, etc.)

aspect.en: Fornost Erain, the 'Norbury of the Kings', was once the grand, fortified northern capital of the kingdom of Arthedain, located at the northern end of the North Downs. Now a silent, massive ruin known as Deadmen's Dike, it is haunted by ghosts, wraiths, and the memories of the fallen Dúnedain. The ruins are characterized by crumbling stone ramparts, collapsed halls, and overgrown ditches.

rotation: Fortified capital of Arthedain on the North Downs, still the heart of the last Dúnedain kingdom of the north. Grey walls, maintained ramparts, the Royal Court and the Seers; but more empty houses with each generation and Angmar darkening the north.

Arthedain's grey-walled capital on the North Downs, still functioning but emptying slowly. Maintained ramparts, a working court and the northern palantír in the tower; more empty houses each generation as the population contract continues.

The town is built into the Down itself; the walls and the natural rock-face are difficult to separate at a distance. What was once a city now fits within a smaller perimeter that the garrison can actually defend.
The North Downs here are chalk and flint, with the escarpment dropping north toward the empty ground. Fornost sits at the highest defensible point; below it, the ground is farmed by whoever is left.
Cold winters and grey springs that define northern Arthedain. The Down keeps the worst wind off the town; the town generates its own heat from density that it is slowly losing.
Dúnedain who have decided to stay. Not from optimism — they know the numbers — but from the particular stubbornness of people who will not be the ones to lower the last flag.

land.name: Deadmen's Dike
land.biome_hint: fortified ruins atop wind-swept downs with high exposure
land.description: The massive defensive earthworks and stone foundations of the ruined city.

facts.notes: Fornost remains a place of dread, avoided by locals due to rumors of active dark spirits.

people.military: Occasional Ranger patrols.
people.description: Deserted by civilized folk; only rangers and occasional tomb-robbers pass through.

facts.products: None (relics and ancient treasures of Arnor).

aspect.en: The Old Forest is an ancient, sentient, and deeply shadowed woodland bordering the eastern Shire. Known for its hostile, moving trees and gnarled roots, it is ruled by the mysterious Old Man Willow and protected by Tom Bombadil.

rotation: The Old Forest — a remnant of the woods that once covered the world, grown dark and queer with age. The trees are awake and they remember injuries.
Oak and ash stand so close that daylight fails; the air is still, the quiet is watchful, and a shout comes back muffled without an echo.
The paths are the Forest's and not the traveller's — they shift, they fade, they lead down to the willow-dells where the stream murmurs over wild herbs.
Fog fills the valley at dawn like a sea; from the high edge the whole wood is a grey ocean of mist broken into billows, with the smell of rain coming in.
After rain the wood steams under a heavy blue sky; water drips for hours from the thatch of leaves and the thatch of the whole forest.
Nothing in the Forest is hostile by accident; the willows hate, the paths mislead, and the trees lean and watch. The way through is courtesy and patience.

land.name: Withywindle Valley
land.biome_hint: dense primeval forest with gnarled roots, stagnant bogs, and moving trees
land.description: The dark, deep river valley at the heart of the forest, where Old Man Willow lies.

facts.notes: The Old Forest is incredibly dangerous; pathways shift, and the trees actively conspire against travelers.

people.military: The forest itself is its own defense.
people.description: Uninhabited by mortals; Hobbits fear to enter, and only Tom Bombadil dwells on its borders.

source.supplement: Tolkien (LotR) with Shire / Eriador regional material

phrases: In winter the Old Forest is grey and bare but no less watchful; the willows sleep lightly, and the paths belong to them alone.
The Old Forest under rain is a green darkness full of small sounds — drip and trickle and the creak of wet wood.
Nothing hurries; the rain is the Forest's own.

aspect.en: Arthedain is the northern Dúnedain kingdom in Eriador, cradled between the Blue Mountains and the Misty Mountains and bounded by the rivers Lhûn and Baranduin, a cool, sparsely populated realm of rocky hills, downs, marshes, and the Shire, ruled from Fornost as the last Númenórean realm in the North in T.A. 1640.

rotation: Chalk hills of southern Cardolan, once the granary of the southern Arnor kingdom. Dúnedain towers on the crests, wild pasture where wheat fields once grew and nomadic shepherds in a land that history has forgotten.

Chalk hills of southern Cardolan, once the grain country of Arnor's southern kingdom. Dúnedain towers standing on the crests above wild pasture that has replaced the wheat; nomadic shepherds in a land that history has finished with.

The native forest was felled centuries ago and never replanted; the chalk now carries open pasture and the occasional bramble thicket where the seeds found purchase. The land is recovering toward something, slowly.
Rolling chalk downs with the towers on the heights — visible from miles away, too thin to garrison, too significant to demolish. The paths below them are still used because paths on chalk endure.

Southern Cardolan's climate is milder than the north — shorter winters, earlier springs, the southern influence of Belegaer moderating both extremes. The grass grows well; the towers stand in weather that could be worse.
Shepherds who have no particular connection to the Dúnedain history beneath their feet. They use the tower-ruins as shelter when the weather closes in.

land.name: Forochel and the Icy North
land.biome_hint: arctic coastal tundra and sea-ice
land.description: The far northern portion of Arthedain reaches toward the Ice-bay of Forochel and the Forodwaith, a realm of ice-plains, tundra and bitter cold, inhabited mainly by the Lossoth and visited by Dúnedain only in times of dire need.[file:25]

land.name: North Downs
land.biome_hint: rocky downs with thin soils and open grass-heath
land.description: High rolling hills east of Lake Evendim, forming rocky ridges that march across northeastern Arthedain like massive natural altars; they shelter and overlook Fornost and serve as a defensive barrier toward Angmar.[file:25]

land.name: Lake Nenuial (Lake Evendim)
land.biome_hint: cool upland lake with stony shores and reeds
land.description: A large blue lake in north-central Arthedain, sheltered on three sides by the Hills of Evendim, with the ruined first capital of Annúminas on its southern shore.[file:25]

land.name: Annúminas
land.biome_hint: ruins on windy lake-hills
land.description: Elendil’s original capital of Arnor on the southern shore of Lake Evendim, once a glittering Númenórean city and now a crumbling ruin of marble and stone razed in T.A. 1409.[file:25]

land.name: Fornost Erain
land.biome_hint: fortified hill-city in rocky uplands
land.description: The Northern Fortress of the Kings, built on the southern slopes of the North Downs, ringed by dikes and walls, now the capital of Arthedain and seat of its Royal Court and Seers in T.A. 1640.[file:25]

land.name: Baranduin / Brandywine River
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with mixed woodland and farmland
land.description: A swift yet meandering river flowing over 500 miles from Lake Evendim to the Sea south of Harlindon, forming a major barrier and artery, with key crossings at the Brandywine Bridge and Sarn Ford and providing the Shire with water and fertile valley lands.[file:25]

land.name: Southern Arthedain and the Shire
land.biome_hint: temperate lowland farmland and hedged hills
land.description: The fertile southern part of the kingdom, once neglected by Dúnedain concerned with war, now intensively farmed and settled by hobbits of the Shire, with rolling hills, rich fields and the Green Hill Country.[file:25]

land.name: Weather Hills and Amon Sûl
land.biome_hint: treeless limestone ridges and exposed summits
land.description: Barren rocky ridges in the southeast forming a natural wall along the border, culminating at Weathertop (Amon Sûl), a thousand-foot hill that once bore the chief northern palantír tower and still dominates the Great East Road.[file:25]

land.name: Midgewater Marshes
land.biome_hint: cool, insect-ridden freshwater bog
land.description: Buzzing bogs below the Weather Hills, carved in glacial times and now collecting stagnant water in treacherous pools swarming with midges, making overland travel slow and unpleasant.[file:25]

land.name: White Downs, Far Downs and Tower Hills
land.biome_hint: chalk downs with short turf and coastal influence
land.description: Chalk cliffs and downs in the west of the Shire leading up to the Emyn Beraid (Tower Hills), where three ancient white towers overlook the estuary of the Lhûn and house a westward-looking palantír.[file:25]

land.name: Bree-land and the Greenway
land.biome_hint: temperate hill-country with fields and woodland patches
land.description: Region around Bree-hill where the Great East Road crosses the old North–South road (Greenway); Bree is surrounded by ditches, dikes and hedges rather than walls, and serves as a weathered but still significant stop for travelers and traders.[file:25]

facts.notes: This Arthedain object is meant to capture the realm as described around T.A. 1640 in Rangers of the North, with climate and landforms usable as a base layer for pathfinding, biome assignment and climate modeling; more focused regions like Angmar, Cardolan and Rhudaur are handled in their own supplements.[file:25]

people.military: Royal Forces: 540 Men at Arms. 370 Cavalry. 1,000 Rangers. Noble Forces: 2,150 Men at Arms. 620 Cavalry. 3,000 Levy.
people.population: 50,000 Dúnedain (not including the Shire and Bree-land).
people.description: Arthedain’s population is dominated by the high Men of the Dúnedain, with important minorities including the hobbits of the Shire, the Lossoth of Forochel, rivermen on the northern waters, Bree-landers at the crossroads, and scattered Northmen and Dunlendish groups on the borders.

aspect.en: Dor Rhunen, the 'Land of the East,' comprises the semi-arid, vast southern plains and rolling grasslands surrounding the southern shores of the Sea of Rhûn. Extending southwest toward the desolate Battle Plain of Dagorlad and bordered to the south by the ash-choked fences of Mordor, this is a harsh, wind-swept buffer territory. It is heavily influenced by the cultures of Rohan and the Wold to the west, but dominated by exceptionally brutal nomadic Easterling tribes, such as the Variags, Nuriags, and Asdriags, who frequently raid the trade caravans.

rotation: Vast semi-arid steppes south of the Sea of Rhûn, swept by Easterling nomadic tribes of brutal reputation. The Dagorlad closes the south and the shadow of Mordor haunts the southwest horizon. A land without law or mercy.

Short-grass steppe and scrub desert running south toward the shadow of Dagorlad. Easterling tribes cross it in columns that raise dust visible for a day's ride; no one lingers here who doesn't have to.

Feathergrass and rough sedge bend low in the east wind, the only vegetation on the flat where the soil grows thin and the rock shows through. Water is the only reason anyone stops anywhere in this landscape.

The horizon is always the same distance away. The plateau drops toward the Dagorlad in the south with no visible transition — the land simply gets harder and emptier and more hostile without explanation.
Summers are burning and dry; winters short enough to be cruel. The Easterlings who cross this land in any season do so fast, with enough water calculated to the last skin.

Nomadic raiders and traders who belong to no kingdom. Their allegiances shift with the wind and whoever can make the better offer. Mordor's shadow on the southwest horizon has shaped their entire politics.

land.name: Southern Dor Rhunen Grasslands
land.biome_hint: semi-arid dry grasslands with sparse thorny scrub and high exposure
land.description: The dry, vast plains transitioning into the desolation of Dagorlad to the west and Mordor to the south.

facts.notes: Dor Rhunen serves as a dangerous, lawless transition zone connecting the western lands of Rhovanion with the eastern expanses of Khand.

people.description: A highly volatile frontier populated by warlike nomadic horsemen, brutal Easterling tribes, and occasional raiding Orc bands.

aspect.en: Cardolan, the Land of Red Hills, is the southern successor-kingdom of Arnor between the Baranduin and the Gwathló–Mitheithel, a windswept land of treeless plains, red downs, marshy river basins and the barrow‑haunted hills whose shattered Dúnedain realm never fully recovered from war, civil strife and plague.

rotation: Marshy coastal strip where the Baranduin and Gwathló meet Belegaer in a labyrinth of marshes and shifting sandbars. Migratory birds in their thousands in autumn, tidal fords only the Gwathuirim know and land that changes with every tide.

Coastal marshland where the Baranduin and Gwathló combine their flood-plains before meeting the sea. Shifting sandbars, tidal fords only the Gwathuirim can read, and the smell of estuary mud at every tide.

Migratory birds in their thousands in autumn — godwits and knots and grey plovers in flocks that darken the sky above the sandbars. The estuaries are rich; the birds find them before the Gwathuirim have finished counting the numbers.

The land here is genuinely uncertain about what it is. Tidal flats at high water; mud-and-reed banks at low water; the channels shift with the spring floods and the autumn storms. Nothing stays where it was.
Mild maritime climate controlled entirely by the sea. The wind off Belegaer is constant; the rain follows the tide more than the season. Frost is rare; genuinely warm days are rarer.

Gwathuirim who know which channels can be forded at which tides, which fords shift, which ones are permanent. That knowledge is their only navigational advantage in a landscape that resists outsiders.

land.name: Cardolan proper
land.biome_hint: treeless temperate plains with river basins and red downs
land.description: All lands between Baranduin and Gwathló–Mitheithel as far north as the Great East Road, roughly six hundred miles by one hundred and fifty, divided by the Old North Road into Minhiriath (Region of the Streams) and Mintyrnath (Region of the Downs). [file:31]

land.name: Minhiriath
land.biome_hint: semi‑arid temperate plain with many streams and floodplain pockets
land.description: The southwestern half of Cardolan, a nearly featureless, gently seaward‑sloping plain cut by countless small rivers and streams toward Baranduin, Gwathló and the sea, with generally poor soils suited mainly to sheep, except along streams and in the richly silted Gwathló basin.[file:31]

land.name: Mintyrnath
land.biome_hint: windswept hills and downs with thin turf and scattered woods
land.description: The northeastern half, a complex of red downs, highlands and basins including the Pinnath Ceren, Barrow‑downs, South Downs, Girithlin highlands and parts of the Gwathló basin; windswept, infertile ridges alternate with richer floodplains.[file:31]

land.name: Barrow-downs (Tyrn Gorthad) and South Downs
land.biome_hint: open chalk and limestone ridges with short turf and barrow mounds
land.description: A line of ridges running northeast with steep southwestern faces and long gentle slopes, largely treeless and infertile, famed for ancient Adan passage‑graves, royal barrows and later the Wight‑haunted mounds of Cardolan’s princes.[file:31]

land.name: Old Forest (Taur Iaur)
land.biome_hint: dense temperate old‑growth forest with hostile, uneven ground
land.description: Dark, dangerous woodland west of the Barrow‑downs between them and Baranduin, where resentful ancient trees remain from the primordial forest and house Tom Bombadil’s domain; little inhabited and largely unexplored by Cardolani.[file:31]

land.name: Pinnath Ceren and Girithlin highlands
land.biome_hint: rocky red and white ridges, thin soils, cool and windy
land.description: Red‑tinted ridges atop a small plateau and the higher Girithlin highlands, rich in iron ores and marble, historically centers of resistance and mining, but exposed to erosion and only marginally fertile beyond scattered farming pockets.[file:31]

land.name: Gwathló basin and Nîn‑in‑Eilph
land.biome_hint: rich alluvial farmland and extensive freshwater marshes
land.description: The wide, flood‑prone basin of the Gwathló, narrow near the sea but spreading to almost eighty miles near Tharbad, with extremely fertile silted farmlands on the floodplain and the four‑hundred‑square‑mile Swanfleet Marshes of alkali bogs and swans where Mitheithel and Glanduin join.[file:31]

land.name: Rast Vorn and Eryn Vorn
land.biome_hint: coastal dark forest on broken, foggy, reef‑strewn shores
land.description: A dark, mostly unexplored peninsula south of the Baranduin’s mouth with treacherous shoal‑ridden, fog‑shrouded coasts and the ancient Dark Woods inhabited by Beffraen; considered one of the most dangerous coasts known to Dúnadan mariners.[file:31]

land.name: Tharbad and environs
land.biome_hint: urban island in broad, seasonally flooded river marsh
land.description: The great river‑port city raised above surrounding fenland at the Gwathló crossing, protected by immense dikes and causeways and straddling the river with wondrous bridges; later reduced by siege, plague and flood to a decaying but still strategic free city in the marshes.[file:31]

facts.notes: This Cardolan object treats the realm at its mid‑Third Age extent around T.A. 1640 as a single climatic and cultural region node, combining Minhiriath and Mintyrnath into one macro‑region for your model; more detailed political units like Saralainn, Tharbad, individual principalities or the Warlord’s domain can be spun out later as separate objects if finer resolution is needed.[file:31]

people.military: Each Prince and Lord commands about 100 warriors in a personal retinue and can raise 200-800 levy troops in 2-3 weeks. Most often, however, the Lords rely upon mercenary bands and the Dunnish tribes in the region for military muscle. Gondor and Arthedain also maintain garrisons in Cardolan to ensure the safety of the trade routes.
people.population: 48,000 Cardolani (not including populations of Saralainn or the Cantons).
people.description: Cardolan’s population mixes Dúnedain princes and warriors, Eriadoran Northmen, Dunlendings, Beffraen and later southern refugees; after the Kingdom’s fall the land fragments into rival principalities, mercenary companies, peasant rebels, Gondorian garrisons and eventually bandit‑ridden ruins under the shadow of Angmar.

aspect.en: Arthedain is the northern Dúnedain kingdom in Eriador, cradled between the Blue Mountains and the Misty Mountains and bounded by the rivers Lhûn and Baranduin, a cool, sparsely populated realm of rocky hills, downs, marshes, and the Shire, ruled from Fornost as the last Númenórean realm in the North in T.A. 1640.

rotation: The Weather Hills — a long line of bare ridges south of the East Road, where the watch-towers of fallen Arthedain stand ringed and ruined on the heights.
Weathertop is the crown of the line — bare and windy, with the whole world spread below; the old fortress of Amon Sûl held the chief of the northern seeing-stones.
Scrub and stunted trees between barren reaches; the paths are faint and the thickets are tangled, and kingsfoil grows where a wise eye knows to look.
Rain sweeps the hills in fine soaking veils off the west; the ridges run with water and the stone is black and streaming, and after rain the air is washed and the sky is pale.
A cold, watching country — the ruins see a long way and the land sees back; travellers keep to the Road and the hollows, and do not camp on the heights.
East and south the marsh-pools and the thickets run on toward the wild; the hills are the last wall of the settled world before the Road goes into the Lone-lands.

land.biome_hint: arctic coastal tundra and sea-ice
land.description: The far northern portion of Arthedain reaches toward the Ice-bay of Forochel and the Forodwaith, a realm of ice-plains, tundra and bitter cold, inhabited mainly by the Lossoth and visited by Dúnedain only in times of dire need.[file:25]

land.description: A large blue lake in north-central Arthedain, sheltered on three sides by the Hills of Evendim, with the ruined first capital of Annúminas on its southern shore.[file:25]

land.description: Elendil’s original capital of Arnor on the southern shore of Lake Evendim, once a glittering Númenórean city and now a crumbling ruin of marble and stone razed in T.A. 1409.[file:25]

land.biome_hint: fortified hill-city in rocky uplands
land.description: The Northern Fortress of the Kings, built on the southern slopes of the North Downs, ringed by dikes and walls, now the capital of Arthedain and seat of its Royal Court and Seers in T.A. 1640.[file:25]

land.name: Baranduin / Brandywine River
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with mixed woodland and farmland
land.description: A swift yet meandering river flowing over 500 miles from Lake Evendim to the Sea south of Harlindon, forming a major barrier and artery, with key crossings at the Brandywine Bridge and Sarn Ford and providing the Shire with water and fertile valley lands.[file:25]

land.biome_hint: temperate lowland farmland and hedged hills
land.description: The fertile southern part of the kingdom, once neglected by Dúnedain concerned with war, now intensively farmed and settled by hobbits of the Shire, with rolling hills, rich fields and the Green Hill Country.[file:25]

land.biome_hint: treeless limestone ridges and exposed summits
land.description: Barren rocky ridges in the southeast forming a natural wall along the border, culminating at Weathertop (Amon Sûl), a thousand-foot hill that once bore the chief northern palantír tower and still dominates the Great East Road.[file:25]

land.biome_hint: cool, insect-ridden freshwater bog
land.description: Buzzing bogs below the Weather Hills, carved in glacial times and now collecting stagnant water in treacherous pools swarming with midges, making overland travel slow and unpleasant.[file:25]

land.name: White Downs, Far Downs and Tower Hills
land.biome_hint: chalk downs with short turf and coastal influence
land.description: Chalk cliffs and downs in the west of the Shire leading up to the Emyn Beraid (Tower Hills), where three ancient white towers overlook the estuary of the Lhûn and house a westward-looking palantír.[file:25]

land.name: Bree-land and the Greenway
land.biome_hint: temperate hill-country with fields and woodland patches
land.description: Region around Bree-hill where the Great East Road crosses the old North–South road (Greenway); Bree is surrounded by ditches, dikes and hedges rather than walls, and serves as a weathered but still significant stop for travelers and traders.[file:25]

people.description: Arthedain’s population is dominated by the high Men of the Dúnedain, with important minorities including the hobbits of the Shire, the Lossoth of Forochel, rivermen on the northern waters, Bree-landers at the crossroads, and scattered Northmen and Dunlendish groups on the borders.

phrases: The Weather Hills in rain are a sodden secret country — grey ridges in streaming mist, with water running in every crevice of the old stones.
Winter lays the hills bare — iron grass, black thorn, and the empty crowns of the watch-towers against a colourless sky.
A searching cold owns these hills; it pours down the lee slopes at night and pools in the hollows till dawn.

aspect.en: Rohan is a beautiful territory and one of the jewels of the Gondorian crown, a wide land of rolling pastures and coombes dominated by the towering peaks of the White Mountains, home of the semi‑nomadic Horse‑lords who became the Rohirrim after T.A. 2510.

rotation: The Riddermark — a sea of grass between the Entwash and the White Mountains, where the wind never rests and the horse-lords' green ways run under a huge sky.
Green foothills climb to the white southern wall; Edoras stands on its hill in the vale of Harrowdale, and the Golden Hall shines when the sun is on it.
The mountains behind the Mark hold the deep refuges — the gorge of Harrowdale, the high green Firienfeld, and the Dwimorberg's dark door where the Paths of the Dead begin.
Streams thread the dales — the Snowbourn loud over its stones, the Entwash slow and green along the edge of Fangorn, and the Isen running cold out of the Gap.
Hot summers of high grass and hard winters of sere plain; the wind comes off the northern snows without a hill to stop it, and the rain sweeps the open Mark in grey veils.
Horse-country through and through — the mounds of the kings stand green on the road to Edoras, and the heralds' horns echo off the mountain wall at dawn.

land.name: The Riddermark (Rohan proper)
land.biome_hint: broad temperate grasslands with high plains, coombes, and mountain foothills
land.description: The Green Province of Calenardhon after T.A. 2510, granted to the Othod by Steward Cirion; bounded roughly by the Anduin on the east, the Isen on the west, the White Mountains on the south, and Fangorn and the Limlight on the north.

land.name: The Wold
land.biome_hint: windy chalk downs suited to sheep pasture
land.description: Steeply folded, semi‑arid downs forming the northeastern part of Rohan; green but treeless hills of short, springy grass and heather, with porous chalky rock where rain drains off quickly.

land.name: East Emnet and West Emnet
land.biome_hint: deep fertile grasslands ideal for horse herds
land.description: Vast carpets of tall grass forming the central plains; East Emnet stretches between the Wold and the Entwash, West Emnet between Fangorn, the Misty Mountains, and the Deeping Stream.

land.name: Eastfold and Westfold
land.biome_hint: rolling foothill pastures with coombes and stream‑cut valleys
land.description: Rich, well‑watered pastures along the northern flanks of the White Mountains, cut by streams from the high valleys; Westfold holds the Deeping Coomb and Hornburg, Eastfold contains Harrowdale and the Snowbourne.

land.name: Westmarch
land.biome_hint: windswept frontier grassland with high rainfall and superb grazing
land.description: Westernmost area of Rohan, lying west and south of the Gap between the Angren (Isen) and Adorn; lightly settled, often threatened by Dunlendings, with the best grass and finest horses in the realm.

land.name: Gap of Rohan
land.biome_hint: broad, windy mountain gap with river valleys
land.description: Forty‑mile‑wide strategic pass between the southern Misty Mountains and the northwestern White Mountains, only about 3,700 feet high at its center, providing a grassy doorway between Eriador and lands east and south.

land.name: White Mountains (Ered Nimrais edge)
land.biome_hint: alpine mountains with snowfields, cliffs, caves, and conifer woods on lower slopes
land.description: Snow‑covered limestone and marble range rising steeply from Rohan’s meadows, with jagged peaks like the Thrihyrne, Starkhorn, Irensaga, and Dwimorberg; carved by glaciers into alpine valleys such as the Deeping Coomb and Harrowdale.

land.name: Major rivers of Rohan
land.biome_hint: cold snow‑fed rivers, fens in the Entwash delta, and trout streams in mountain valleys
land.description: The Isen and Adorn feed the Westmarch; the Entwash rises in Fangorn and winds through the heart of Rohan before breaking into a fen‑filled delta at its mouths; the Snowbourne rises in the White Mountains at Harrowdale; the Limlight separates the East Emnet from Lórien.

facts.notes: This region object focuses on Rohan in the Rohirric Age (T.A. 2510 onward), but the same land supports earlier Othod settlements; sub‑sites like Edoras, Helm’s Deep, and Dunharrow can be handled as separate site objects tied to this region.

people.description: The Horse‑lords are a wandering people whose history passes through three main stages—othraim in southern Rhovanion, othod in the vales of the Anduin, and Rohirrim in Rohan—remaining semi‑nomadic and horse‑centered but evolving from scattered clans to a unified kingdom at the heart of western trade and war.

phrases: Rohan in high summer is a green sea of grass and wind; the larks are up, the horses are sleek, and the mountains stand blue and far.
Cold on the Mark is a wind-cold, endless and searching; it has the whole width of the plain to gather in, and it comes like a spear.
The Mark under winter is a sea of grey grass under a white wall; the wind is the lord of it, and the land rings hollow under the hooves.

rotation: The Wold — the high empty grasslands of the north Mark, rolling uplands where the herds graze far from any hall and the sky is the largest thing in the world.
Lonelier than the fields of the south — thorn-brakes and birch on the slopes, and the dark eaves of Fangorn closing the eastern horizon like a wall.
No roads, only grass-tracks; the Riders' ways run north over the downs to the Entwash fords, and the going is all open sky and long wind.
The northern herds winter here and the wolf and the winter are both hungry; the Wold is the Mark's far edge and feels it.
Mist comes up off the Entwash valley at dusk and the forest to the east is a black line under the stars; the nights here are enormous.
A country for riders and weather — cold, wind, and the smell of distance; there is no shelter on the Wold, only the sky.
