phrases: The Wold in winter is the loneliest part of the Mark — white downs, black thorn-brakes, and the far dark of Fangorn like a wall between worlds.
Cold on the Wold is a northern cold; it comes down the vale of the Anduin and across the empty downs, and there is no hill to hide behind.

aspect.en: Lindon is the westernmost Elvish realm of Middle-earth, the remnant of Ossiriand that survived the War of Wrath. After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Northern promontory of Forlindon pointing into Belegaer. Dark fractured cliffs battered by the sea, tall heather and peat bog inland, and seabird colonies on every ledge. On clear days Tol Fuin is visible to the northwest.

Northern Forlindon's cliff promontory, with fractured basalt dropping into heavy seas and seabird colonies on every ledge. On clear days Tol Fuin is visible to the northwest as a dark smear on the horizon.

Tall heather and peat bog inland; the exposed rock supports nothing larger. The clifftops are genuinely dangerous in high wind; the seabirds breed here because nothing else can reach the nesting-ledges.

The northernmost point of Lindon juts into Belegaer. The sea here is cold and often rough; the cape breaks the Atlantic swell into something more immediate and violent. It is the weather-edge of a weather-prone coast.
Cold, wet and wind-battered year-round. The brief northern summer is pleasant on the inland heath; the clifftops are never quite not dangerous.
Seabirds, seals in the coves, and the occasional Elvish lookout who comes to watch Tol Fuin. The cape does not encourage settlement.

land.name: Forlindon (North Lindon)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate coastal and lowland zone with maritime influence transitioning to colder mountain foothills
land.description: The northern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, including coastal plains and the northern Blue Mountain foothills. Historically the primary home of the Noldor (Godhellim) in the realm, it contains harbors and settlements connected to Mithlond and is treated in the government section as a distinct administrative region.[file:99]

land.name: Harlindon (South Lindon)
land.biome_hint: mild, wet coastal strip with forests and rural Elven settlements around secondary harbors
land.description: The southern part of Lindon west of the Gulf of Lhûn, associated with Sindar and Laiquendi (Iathrim, Laegrim). It combines coastal stretches and forested lowlands, was once a fief under Celeborn, and is portrayed as more rural and woodland-oriented than Forlindon.[file:99]

land.name: Rhûnlindon (east-of-Lhûn / Blue Mountains)
land.biome_hint: cool to cold mountain zone with conifer forests, winter snow and extensive mining
land.description: The part of Lindon’s sphere east of the River Lhûn, including the eastern Blue Mountains with Dwarven halls and some Elven refuges. Population tables assign Rhûnlindon about 10% of Lindon’s population, with climate corresponding to the Ered Luin band (colder winters, moderate summers, 30–40 inches of precipitation).[^file99]

land.name: Mithlond (Grey Havens)
land.biome_hint: maritime urban enclave with sheltered harbor, mild wet climate and intensive shipbuilding
land.description: The principal harbor city at the head of the Gulf of Lhûn, seat of Círdan in the Third Age and the main port for Elves and Ring-bearers departing to Valinor. Population tables show Mithlond comprising 20–25% of Lindon’s inhabitants in the Third Age (and 9–10% in the Second Age), emphasizing its central role in Lindon’s demography and economy.[file:99]

land.name: Taeg Lindon routes and refuges
land.biome_hint: mixed grassland, forest and hill country between the Misty Mountains and the Ered Luin, with hidden Elven refuges
land.description: The 'Bounds of Lindon' section describes the Wandering Companies’ preferred route from Imladris to Mithlond: across Eregion, the Mitheithel ford south of Fennas Drúnin, the South Downs and Barrow-downs (with stops near Tom Bombadil’s house), then either through the Old Forest and Green Hills or along the Brandywine’s eastern shore before turning west to the Ered Luin. Along roughly 600 miles they maintain rustic camps and more elaborate permanent refuges (glades, caves, small houses) 20–30 miles apart, some shared with Rangers after the fall of Arthedain.[file:99]

facts.notes: This Lindon work is an unlicensed, non-commercial fan-made Realm (version 3.2, 2023) rather than an original ICE product, but it is structured like a MERP Realm and synthesizes Tolkien canon with MERP-style material. For your Middle-earth-on-Europe map, Lindon should be treated as one macro-region with internal subregions (Forlindon, Harlindon, Rhûnlindon) sharing a maritime temperate climate, and Mithlond explicitly marked as a major harbor node. Climate numbers (temperature ranges and precipitation) from the Traveller’s Guide can be mapped directly onto your climate system for coastal vs mountain bands, while the Wandering Companies’ route description provides a canonical overland corridor from Imladris to the Grey Havens for your path and distance calculations.[file:99] Eerily beautiful remnants of Beleriand, characterized by rugged coastal hills, fertile valleys, and evergreen forests. A light rain, drizzle, or ethereal fog falls on most days of the year, allowing mosses, ferns, firs, and spruce to thrive.

people.symbol: Círdan's Device: A White Pelannun on a Blue Field
people.military: 2,000 Warriors and Sailors (Forlindon: 800 Warriors/Sailors, 800 Levy. Harlindon: 1,200 Sailors/Warriors, 800 Militia).
people.description: Lindon’s population is overwhelmingly Elvish, composed of multiple lineages (Noldor, Sindar, Laiquendi, Nandor, Falathrim) under Gil-galad and later Círdan, with a significant Dwarven presence in the Blue Mountains and peripheral contact with Men and Hobbits via routes and harbors. The Traveller’s Guide provides detailed population tables showing long-term decline through the Third Age.

source.supplement: Lindon: The Kingdom of the Elves (fan-made Realm #3003)

After the breaking and flooding of Beleriand, the Great Sea breached the Blue Mountains to form the Gulf of Lhûn, dividing Lindon into Forlindon (North Lindon) and Harlindon (South Lindon), with the River Lhûn as the eastern border against Arnor. Throughout the Second and early Third Age it is the principal Elven coastal realm and home of the Grey Havens (Mithlond). Geology consists of folded sedimentary rock (slate and sandstone) with rich iron lodes and abundant coal deposits in forlindon.

rotation: Southern Forlindon along the lower Linduin, the last sub-region to be named by the Elves. Dense alders, spring-flooded meadows with frogs and storks and the wide slow green river that speaks only of time, not history.

Southern Forlindon along the lower Linduin, where the river grows slow and green before meeting the Gulf. Dense alder groves, spring floods leaving stork-haunted meadows and a wide quiet water that speaks of time rather than history.
Alder and willow on the flood-margin; tall reeds in the backwaters; frogs and storks and the particular kind of silence that comes from a slow river in warm air. The last named sub-region of Lindon.

The Linduin broadens and slows here as it approaches the Gulf; the floodplain spreads accordingly. In spring it floods silently and completely; in summer it is a green waterway between meadows of exceptional richness.
The mildest climate in northern Lindon, sheltered from the Atlantic by the hills to the north and warmed by the Gulf of Lhûn to the south. Spring arrives earliest here and summer stays longest.

Sindar Elves who chose the river over the sea or the forest. Their settlements are low and riparian, built for proximity to the Linduin; the sound of moving water defines the place as much as the Elves do.

aspect.en: Mount Gundabad is the northernmost and one of the highest peaks of the Misty Mountains, a triple‑spired volcanic giant honeycombed into a vast Orc‑city and forge complex, capital of the Orcs of the Mountains and a key client realm of Angmar.

rotation: Gundabad, the triple-spired volcanic capital of the Mountain Orcs, with hundreds of underground levels of forges and armories. Black rock, dirty snow and smelter smoke rising from chimneys cut into the living stone.

Gundabad on its volcanic triple-peak, the Mountain Orc capital with hundreds of underground levels of forge and armory. Black rock, dirty snow and smelter smoke rising from chimneys cut into the living stone.

The surface around the mountain has been stripped bare by centuries of Orc occupation — no trees, scrub reduced to whatever can survive in the shadow of constant smoke. The rock is soot-stained for miles.

The mountain itself is visually distinctive: three peaks and the particular darkness of the rock under a permanent layer of smoke and ash. It is visible from a long distance in clear weather and rarely seen in clear weather.

Perpetually cold and darkened by smoke. The wind here carries ash and the smell of metal. What passes for summer at Gundabad is a brief reduction in severity rather than an actual change in character.

Mountain Orcs and their forges. The organisation here is military-industrial: everything exists to produce weapons and soldiers. The mountain has been producing both for longer than the Dúnedain kingdom lasted.

land.name: Mount Gundabad (triple‑spired peak)
land.biome_hint: barren volcanic peak with sheer rock faces, minimal vegetation, and extensive underground tunnels
land.description: Northernmost peak of the Misty Mountains, its central Great Spire rising to about 12,985 feet and flanked by the Twisted Spire and Cloven Spire; its south face bears the carved visage of an open‑jawed fire drake that forms an infamous entrance.

land.name: Twisted Spire and Cloven Spire
land.biome_hint: extreme high‑altitude rock spires subject to storms and lightning
land.description: Sub‑cones of the original volcano; the Twisted Spire bends and turns back on itself like a crooked wizard’s cap, and the Cloven Spire is split from its summit for some two thousand feet as if hewn by a mighty axe.

land.name: Gundalok Shelf
land.biome_hint: stony, well‑watered but thin‑soiled upland with limited vegetation
land.description: Plateau southeast of Mount Gundabad between the arms of the Misty Mountains and Ered Mithrin; rises about 400 feet above the Anduin Vales, with narrow, easily defended trails leading up from the lowlands.

land.name: River Langwell and falls
land.biome_hint: cold, fast mountain river and waterfall carved into plateau edge
land.description: Headwater of the Anduin traversing the Gundalok Shelf from the Misty Mountains; runs east to the shelf’s edge and then plunges over in a spectacular foaming cascade.

land.name: Oglorb Glacier and Lake Hyord
land.biome_hint: glacial ice and a cold, metallic‑tasting mountain lake in a tundra fringe
land.description: The Oglorb Glacier descends for twenty leagues from a northern spur of the Misty Mountains, melting just north of Mount Gundabad to form the chill waters of Lake Hyord, a deep lake five to ten or more miles across that protects Gundabad’s northern flank.

land.name: Den Loke (north–south corridor)
land.biome_hint: high, cold corridor between mountain chains with rocky ridges and sparse scrub
land.description: Easily traversed corridor between the Misty Mountains and Ered Mithrin dominated by Mount Gundabad, serving as the main passage between the Forodwaith and Rhovanion/Anduin Vales.

land.name: Angirith (western route)
land.biome_hint: rocky, storm‑prone high pass linking Gundabad to Angmar
land.description: Rugged route cutting through the northern Misty Mountains westward toward the Angmar Vale, with Mount Gundabad commanding its eastern end.

facts.notes: This object focuses on the Gundabad region at T.A. 1640, when it stands as an unconquered Orc capital and key armory for Angmar; later events like the War of the Dwarves and Orcs and the Battle of Five Armies can be modeled as time‑variant overlays.

people.description: Mount Gundabad is overwhelmingly an Orc realm, ruled by a Goblin‑king recognized as overlord of the Orcs of the Mountains under the distant suzerainty of the Witch‑king of Angmar; it also holds numerous slaves from surrounding lands.

aspect.en: Talath Uichel, the Plain of Everlasting Cold, is the vast tundra interior east of Forochel, structured into green belts and herding grounds, while beyond its northern edge lies the Landless Land, the polar ice-cap desert at the very end of Middle-earth.

rotation: Polar tundra east of Forochel, with impossibly brief summers of flowers and caribou herds and endless brutal winters under metres of snow. Beyond its northern edge lies the Landless Land, where the known world ends.

Polar tundra east of Forochel, where summer means six weeks of flowers and caribou and winter means darkness under metres of snow. Beyond the northern edge is the Landless Land, where the known world ends and something else begins.
In summer: low tundra flowers of extraordinary colour compressed into their brief season, caribou herds moving across the permafrost, the occasional Arctic fox. In winter: none of this is visible.
Permafrost below the surface layer; the ground never fully thaws. What grows here has made its accommodation with that fact. The flowers bloom in compressed urgency and the grasses dry fast.
The most extreme climate of the inhabited world: temperatures that kill quickly, brief summer that barely compensates. The Lossoth who survive here are as hard as the conditions require.

Lossoth who know the permafrost and the caribou migrations and the difference between the storms that can be sat out and the ones that can't. A people defined entirely by the environment they live in.

land.name: Talath Uichel (Plain of Everlasting Cold)
land.biome_hint: vast sub-arctic tundra with permafrost, bogs, heaths and large herbivore herds
land.description: The core tundra plain formed from the shattered bedrock of the Iron Mountains, structured into the Wash Tundra near Eriador, the central Herd Tundra ‘Land of Good Hunting’ and the northern Lakeland of rivers and lakes near the Forsaken Sea.[file:39]

land.name: Wash Tundra
land.biome_hint: mixed forest–tundra mosaic with rivers, bogs and relatively rich game
land.description: The southern green belt bordering Eriador, with more forest, wetlands and human contact than other parts of Talath Uichel, serving as staging ground for traders and frontier folk.[file:39]

land.name: Herd Tundra (Hyvämetsästykseen Maa)
land.biome_hint: open grass–lichen tundra with permafrost, seasonal waterlogging and massive herd migrations
land.description: The central, long plain reaching from Forochel’s shores to the watershed of Angmar, drained by the Everhir and Lhîchir, and underlain by frozen soil without underground drainage, riddled with bogs and shallow streams.[file:39]

land.name: Lakeland
land.biome_hint: tundra with dense lake and wetland networks, conifer stands and heavy insect/fowl activity in summer
land.description: The northern green belt near the Forsaken Sea and southeast of the Bleak Mountains, rich in lakes, fens and forests that support diverse wildlife and Ystvät Talven settlements.[file:39]

land.name: Eriadorian Frontier (Rammas Forod, Northern Marches)
land.biome_hint: cold steppe and forested hills transitioning into tundra and hosting mixed Eriador–Forodwaith flora and fauna
land.description: The jumbled hills and scarped downs where the old Iron Mountains descended into Eriador, later softened by soil, forests and herds; now a hard frontier zone with abandoned Angmar-haunted valleys and hardy Rivermen using northbound canoe routes.[file:39]

land.name: Landless Land (polar ice-cap)
land.biome_hint: true polar desert with thick sea-ice, minimal life, extreme cold and unique psychological/visibility hazards
land.description: The polar ice-cap covering Ekkaia’s waters, with permanent and multi-year pack-ice that thickens and thins seasonally; average monthly temperatures stay below freezing, snowfall is scant and distinctive light–dark cycles dominate the year.[file:39]

land.name: Bleak Mountains and Stone Tundra
land.biome_hint: elevated, rock-dominated cold deserts with thin vegetation and extreme exposure
land.description: Raised and fractured when the Stone Tundra sank at Angband’s fall, these ranges and plateaus form harsh, wind-scoured highlands between Talath Uichel and the Landless Land, shelters for Snow Trolls and other monsters.[file:39]

land.name: Fire Tundra and Morgoth’s Well
land.biome_hint: local warm enclave with unusual plant communities amid otherwise frigid tundra
land.description: A geothermal anomaly within Talath Uichel where hot springs, geysers and volcanic remnants create warm ground and exotic vegetation around the crater of Morgoth’s Well.[file:39]

facts.notes: Use this region for large-scale herd migrations, overland routes, Angmar–Arthedain maneuvering and polar expeditions; coastal and marine gameplay, iceberg travel and bay whaling belong primarily to the Forochel region.[file:39]

people.description: Talath Uichel and the Landless Land are the main domains of the Ystvät Talven tundra folk, Snow-elves in their icy city, Angmar’s sled-hordes and scattered frontier groups from Eriador; very few others can endure the conditions.[file:39]

aspect.en: The High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath, S. 'High-climbing Pass of the North') cuts through the central Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell and Eriador in the west to the upper Anduin Vales and Rhovanion in the east. It encompasses the Orcish stronghold of Goblin-gate, the eyrie of the Great Eagles, the Northman market-town of Maethelburg, the western foothills of Rhudaur, and the broad river plain of the Anduin. Geology consists of limestone and granite with massive igneous basalt intrusions. western foothills consist of red sandstone, while eastern valleys contain oily black shale; rich in copper, iron, silver, gold, and mithril.

rotation: The northern Misty Mountains — the high grey wall between Eriador and the vales of Anduin, where the High Pass climbs by hidden doors and the goblins hold the dark ways.
Pine and scree below, bare rock and permanent snow above; the eagles keep their eyries on the high shoulders and see all that moves below.
The High Pass is the way over — a path of ledges and caves where a dry shelter in a storm may be a door into the goblin-dark.
From the heights the view is a map of the world — oak and elm woods, broad grasslands, and the River winding below around a great standing stone.
Wolves and worse hold the passes by night; the eagles come to them by day, and the wind off the heights carries cries that are not all birds.
A range of storms and shut winters — the passes close under snow from autumn to spring, and the caves in the rocks are never empty for long.

land.name: Anduin Vales (eastern lowlands)
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with lush meadows, broadleaf groves, wetland margins and open farmland
land.description: The broad valley plain east of the Misty Mountains, gently sloping eastward and southward; easily traversed open terrain with grassy meadows, river marshes, elm and oak groves, and scattered Northman homesteads and trading towns. Maethelburg is the main settlement, a fortified hill-town at the confluence of the Anduin and Sirros (Foamflood). The Great River here is the main highway, plied by Northman cnearras (shallow-draught clinker-built craft) trading between Maethelburg and Gondor.[file:88]

land.name: Western Foothills of Rhudaur
land.biome_hint: cold Atlantic-type rugged moorland and forested ravines with bog, heather and ancient conifer cover
land.description: The rugged, forested foothills and moorland west of the Misty Mountains in the territory of Rhudaur; grim stony heights, deep ravines, ancient pine-shrouded valleys and heather-covered moorland, cut by treacherous bogs. Home to Hillmen clans and prowled by Stone-trolls and Orcs at night; nearly impassable without a guide except along the Great East Road (which ends at the Ford of Bruinen).[file:88]

land.name: High Pass (Cirith Forn en Andrath)
land.biome_hint: subarctic alpine pass with permanent snowcaps, glaciers, scree slopes and fierce storm exposure
land.description: A double-branched pass through the Misty Mountains connecting Rivendell to the Anduin: the lower branch (Pass of Imladris, c.3,500 ft) permits horses and wagons but is controlled by Goblin-gate at its summit; the upper mountain-path (over 5,000 ft) is passable only on foot or by mule/pony, steep and exposed to storms but less Orc-infested. Both branches are snow-blocked from Hithui to Gwirith. The pass is riddled with scree, avalanche risk, tumbling boulders and the constant threat of Giants above and Orcs below.[file:88]

land.name: Goblin-Gate (Goblin-town underground)
land.biome_hint: karst limestone cave system with ice caves (upper), inhabited city levels, fungi caves, and deep mine shafts
land.description: A vast network of natural limestone caverns expanded and connected by Orcish mining over millennia, stretching up to 40 miles between the Wolf Gate (main western entrance at the pass summit) and the Back Door (eastern exit to the Anduin slopes), with further passages to the Fungi Caves, Mine levels, and reputed deep shafts connecting to the Underdeeps of Moria. At T.A. 1640: the Great Goblin rules from the City Level; Gollum has not yet arrived (that happens c.T.A. 2470). Underground lakes, underground rivers, stalactites, ice caves (upper levels), massive fungi forests (lower levels) and deep mine shafts all present in the complex.[file:88]

land.name: Eagles' Eyrie (Amon Thyrir pinnacle)
land.biome_hint: bare alpine rock pinnacle above the tree line, surrounded by high-altitude thermals and glaciated peaks
land.description: A solitary rock pinnacle rising above the mountain crags east of the High Pass, inaccessible except by flight; crowned by the vast bowl-shaped nest (up to 40 ft diameter, several tons) of the Lord of the Eagles. The surrounding high peaks and thermal columns of warm rising air are the domain of a small population of Great Eagles, each controlling a territory of 200+ sq miles of mountain terrain.[file:88]

land.name: Giants' Isle (mountain vale)
land.biome_hint: remote high-altitude vale with rock, scree, glacial streams and no human habitation
land.description: A secluded area of high mountain vales where Stone Giants are concentrated; largely avoided by all other peoples. The Giants hurl boulders during thunderstorms and have occupied these heights since the First Age. No settlement is possible here.[file:88]

facts.notes: This module is centered on T.A. 1640 (primary time period), with additional adventures set in T.A. 2940 (time of The Hobbit, when Gollum is already in the caves and Thorin's company passes through) and F.A. 1. The fauna and flora data reflect the T.A. 1640 baseline. Goblin-gate's internal geography is partially procedurally generated (Random Features Table in the module) and not fully fixed on maps—only key route passages are mapped. The region connects westward to Rivendell/Eriador and eastward to northern Mirkwood via Maethelburg and the Old Ford, making it a critical chokepoint on the Misty Mountains.[file:88] The longest and highest mountain chain in the west, serving as a formidable glacial barrier between Eriador and Rhovanion. Heavy snows and glaciers cover peaks above 11,500 feet year-round. It is riddled with Orc-holds, Dwarven caverns, and the under-deeps.

people.military: 100 Beornings. 60 Burgwards of Maethelburg. 900 Militia (3-4 weeks to raise, organized by clan). 135 Eagles (allies).
people.description: The region is sparsely populated by several distinct peoples: Northmen (Nenedain) in the Anduin Vales, Beornings on the eastern bank, Hillmen in the rough hills of Rhudaur, and Orcs in the mountain strongholds, alongside rarer presences of Elves, Dwarves, Giants and Eagles.

facts.products: Grain, hides, cattle, honey, amber, tin.

phrases: Winter in the northern mountains is a season of white walls and shut passes; the goblins come and go under the snow, and the eagles watch.
Snow lies on the northern Misty Mountains from autumn to spring; the peaks are ramparts of it, and the high paths are trenches through it.
The cold in these heights is of the old, hard kind — it lives in the stone of the passes and waits for the traveller at every cave-mouth.

rotation: Desolate moorland of northwestern Eriador, the combined result of Angmar's wars, the Great Plague and abandonment. Heather over old farmsteads, peat-brown rivers and wandering Dúnedain Rangers as the only witnesses.

Desolate moorland in northwestern Eriador, the combined result of Angmar's wars and the Great Plague and the simple mathematics of abandonment. Heather over old farmsteads and Dúnedain Rangers as the only witnesses.

Heather and bracken growing through what were farmsteads fifty years ago. The outlines of field-boundaries are still there; the buildings have mostly fallen into themselves. It's archaeology pretending to be landscape.
A vast emptiness that was once the most populous part of the north. The roads are still there — the Dúnedain maintained them — but they connect ruins to ruins and the traffic is sparse.
Cold, wet and grey for most of the year, with the north wind coming down from Forochel without much interruption. The moorland feels more like weather than like land.

Dúnedain Rangers who know every barrow-mound and ruin and ford in this emptiness. They travel it in pairs and return with information about what is moving. It is their land in the sense that no one else claims it.

aspect.en: Anórien is the northern fief of Gondor that occupies the strip of land between the northern slopes and valleys of the White Mountains and the west bank of the Anduin, opposite northern Ithilien. Established towards the end of the Second Age along with Ithilien and Lebennin as part of Gondor’s Anduin heartland, it later remains the only Gondorian fief north of the White Mountains when Calenardhon is ceded to the Éothéod to become Rohan. The region is defined by mountain-fed valleys, tall grasslands and scattered woods, pierced by the Great West Road and guarded by beacon-peaks and the Drúadan Forest.

rotation: The green province north of the White Mountains — the Pelennor's fenced fields and orchards running up to the City walls, with the beacon-hills marching east along the mountain feet.
Tended woods of beech and fir on the foothills; beyond them the dark pines of Drúadan keep their own counsel. Every height carries a beacon against a day of need.
The Great West Road runs straight through the townlands to the fords of the Isen. Farms, dykes and orchards crowd close here; this is the garden and granary of the City.
Warm summers, hard bright winters off the mountains. The wind that comes down at evening smells of high snow even when the fields are in flower.
Country-folk of the Mark's kin and the City both — farmers and herdsmen who keep the beacons and the roads, and look south to the white wall that walls the world.
The Rammas wall rings the fields; outside it the land climbs in long green slopes to the hills where the signal-fires wait, unlit but ready.

land.name: Anórien proper (valleys and grasslands)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate grassland and mixed farmland with scattered woodland and a strong mountain influence
land.description: The main strip of Anórien between the northern White Mountain valleys and the Anduin: a narrow belt of tall grasslands, fields and scattered woods, with the Great West Road running east–west as the principal artery.[web:238][web:242]

land.name: Beacon peaks of the White Mountains
land.biome_hint: rocky upland with thin soils, grass and scrub, snow in winter and extensive views
land.description: The chain of peaks and shoulders north of the main White Mountain crest that host Gondor’s beacons (Amon Dîn, Eilenach, Nardol, etc.), rising above Anórien and sending warning fires towards Rohan.[web:234][web:242] These heights are rocky, colder and more sparsely vegetated than the valleys below, but they anchor the region’s identity and communications.

land.name: Drúadan Forest
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate mixed forest with dense undergrowth and minimal clearance
land.description: A dense, ancient woodland on the lower northern slopes of the White Mountains within or adjacent to Anórien, home of the Drúedain, characterised by heavy canopy, thick undergrowth and relatively little Gondorian exploitation.[web:234][web:243]

land.name: Anduin margin opposite northern Ithilien
land.biome_hint: temperate riverbank with narrow belts of moist-soil vegetation and adjacent farmland
land.description: The low river-edge lands and bluffs along the west bank of the Anduin opposite northern Ithilien, including the approaches to Cair Andros and downstream crossings; this forms Anórien’s eastern limit and a transit interface between river traffic and land routes.[web:234][web:240]

facts.notes: For mapping, treat Anórien as a narrow Anduin-valley and mountain-foot fief: cooler and more sparsely settled than Lebennin, with tall grasslands and scattered farms in the central strip, beacon peaks and the Drúadan Forest along the White Mountains, and the Anduin margin linking it to northern Ithilien and Cair Andros.[file:216][web:234][web:238][web:243]

people.description: Anórien’s human landscape in the late Third Age is shaped by its status as a strategic corridor rather than a dense core province: Dúnedain and mixed-descendant farmers in scattered villages and steadings, Drúedain clans in the Drúadan Forest, and military traffic along the Great West Road and beacon line.

source.supplement: Tolkien (LotR) with Gondor regional material (Sea-Lords of Gondor / Minas Tirith)

phrases: Winter in Anorien is a country of white heights and green vales; the beacons stand ready on cold bare hills and the wind off the mountains is clean and sharp.
Anorien in summer is the green lap of the realm — the Pelennor deep in grass and grain, the hills in flower, and the White Mountains blue in the warm air.
Rain over Anorien is a gentle grey curtain on the townlands; the fields drink, the orchards shine, and the White Mountains are a rumour in the mist.

aspect.en: Eregion is a Noldorin-founded realm on the western side of the Misty Mountains, centered on the great city of Ost-in-Edhil and famed for its jewel-smiths, close friendship with Khazad-dûm, and the forging of the Rings of Power.

rotation: Hollin — the empty land of the holly-trees west of Moria, where the Noldor once had their fairest realm in exile and only the hollies and the stones remember it.
Low ridges of broken stone crowned with dark holly; the three peaks of Moria close the eastern sky, and the old Elven road still runs beneath the heather toward the shut doors.
The streams are dry or diminished — the Sirannon's course is a thread of red-stained stones, and where its water was dammed long ago the land was changed and never healed.
A clean cold country under a wide sky; the wind comes off the mountains keen and clear, and the silence has an edge of watchfulness.
Nothing remains of Ost-in-Edhil but shapeless mounds and the buried lines of old walls; travellers camp here now where the jewel-smiths once worked.
At dawn in winter the hollies are crowned with light and red berries, and the snowy peaks stand ahead like the doors of the world — it is the most beautiful hour in a sad land.

land.name: Eregion proper
land.biome_hint: temperate rolling uplands with rivers, cultivated fields, and scattered woodland
land.description: All lands north of the river Glanduin and south of the Mitheithel/Bruinen, with Ost-in-Edhil on its southern edge and most Elven settlements north of the Glanduin.

land.name: Ost-in-Edhil
land.biome_hint: walled stone city on a river bluff with ornamental gardens
land.description: The great Noldorin fortress-city built on a granite bluff above the Glanduin, planned on an intricate triangular grid and resembling a gigantic stone ship facing west over Lake Estelin, with multiple districts at different elevations.

land.name: Estelin
land.biome_hint: temperate river-lake on a broadening of the Glanduin
land.description: Small lake west of Ost-in-Edhil formed by a natural rock dam later enhanced by Noldorin engineers; serves as a placid foreground to the city’s ‘ship’ prow.

land.name: Glanduin
land.biome_hint: temperate river with alternating rapids and slow reaches
land.description: Main river flowing below Ost-in-Edhil’s bluff, varying between swift and foaming and wide and sluggish, carrying trade and water past the city.

land.name: Sirannon
land.biome_hint: mountain-fed river descending through foothills
land.description: Tributary joining the Glanduin just upriver from the city; its valley and the narrow water tunnels provide access toward Khazad-dûm and to the Mirdainthron’s water entry.

land.name: Lantalaith
land.biome_hint: small fast-flowing hill stream
land.description: Small, swift river called “tumbling laughter” that drains the hills north of Ost-in-Edhil and guards the northwest edge of the city bluff.

land.name: Triangle between Sirannon and Glanduin
land.biome_hint: open pasture and scrub in a river angle
land.description: Sparsely inhabited wedge of land between the two rivers, used mainly by rustic Silvan shepherds rather than Noldorin estates.

land.name: Fields and estates north of Ost-in-Edhil
land.biome_hint: intensively cultivated temperate uplands
land.description: Rolling hills covered in triangular plots of wheat, barley, vineyards, and pasture land, punctuated by Noldorin country houses belonging to prominent families.

land.name: Tharbad Road and western approach
land.biome_hint: riverbank road along rocky slopes
land.description: Paved road running east from the west along the Glanduin’s steep bank, marked thirty miles from the city by twin holly-pillared obelisks welcoming kindred to ‘The Fortress of the Eldar’.

land.name: Ost-in-Edhil districts
land.biome_hint: stone terraces with mixed ornamental vegetation at several elevations
land.description: Tiered districts of the city (Tirannon, Ardhlarem, Medhlarem, Monde, Pennahithri, Gaiadhurm, High Citadel, Tirmmen) forming a multi-level urban layout with noble residences, commercial areas, harbors, misty terraces, wooded quarters, and a military citadel.

facts.notes: This object treats Eregion as the larger political and geographic region surrounding Ost-in-Edhil in the Second Age. Lórien, specific city sites, and Khazad-dûm are to be modeled as separate region or site objects.

people.description: Eregion is a Noldorin-founded realm ruled initially by Galadriel and Celeborn, with Celebrimbor and the Gwaith-i-Mírdain dominating its crafts and politics. The population includes Noldor, Sindar, and Silvan Elves, with close ties to the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm and scattered rustic Silvan shepherds in the less-settled triangle between the Sirannon and the Glanduin.

source.supplement: Lórien & The Halls of the Elven Smiths

phrases: Eregion in winter is Hollin naked — holly dark against the snow, red berries like drops of blood, and the mountain wall closing the east.
Snow lies long in Eregion; it fills the hollows of the old road and crowns every ridge, and the high peaks burn white against the sky.
The cold of Eregion is a mountain cold, thin and bright; it comes down off the snows and the empty land rings with it.

aspect.en: Moria, or Khazad-dûm, is the ancient and legendary underground Dwarf-city of the House of Durin, carved deep beneath the Misty Mountains. Now a vast, dark abyss occupied by Orcs, Cave-Trolls, and the shadow of the Balrog.

rotation: The land about Moria's gates — barren foothills of red stone where the hollies stand last and the dry watercourse of the Sirannon runs down to a dark and watchful mere.
Above the hidden doors the three peaks tower — Caradhras, Celebdil, Fanuidhol. The Dimrill Dale below them is silent around the still black water of Mirrormere.
The old road climbs to cliffs and shut doors; the Stair beside the falls is worn by feet that vanished an age ago. The country is the shell of a kingdom.
Beneath the hills the deep halls go down past light and knowledge — vast pillared dark where drums sound and the water is cold enough to freeze the heart.
A high cold land; snow lies long in the Dale, and the peaks keep their storms like a grudge. The wind off Caradhras has malice in it.
Nothing is here that is not stone, silence, or shadow; yet the stars in Mirrormere are the fairest sight in a land of ruins, and the Dale is holy ground to the dwarves.

land.name: Deeps of Moria
land.biome_hint: subterranean mine-shafts and stone bridges over deep abysses
land.description: The bottomless mines and subterranean pits where mithril is found.

facts.notes: Moria is a place of absolute darkness, feared by Elves and Men alike.

people.symbol: Durin's Folk: Seven Stars in a Triangular Formation
people.military: Mansion Watch and Weapon Host.
people.description: Currently occupied by the Orc-hordes of the Misty Mountains and a few isolated dwarven parties.

facts.products: Precious metals, gems, finished products, Mithril.

phrases: Moria's gates in winter face a white and hollow land; the Dimrill Dale is drifted deep, and the old road is a rumour under the snow.
Snow falls on Moria's hidden doors as it fell when the doors were open; the mountain keeps its secrets equally under white or stone.
The cold about the West-gate is the cold of deep places — it seeps up out of the earth as much as it blows down from the peaks.

aspect.en: Dunland is the rugged foothill and plateau country south of the Glanduin, east of the Gwathló and north of the Isen, a land of highlands and plains ruled by fractious Dunlending clans who herd, raid and scheme along the vital Old South Road and the Isen Gap.

rotation: The country between the Gap of Rohan and the ring of Isengard — green hills and long empty downs, poorer since the forests were felled for the traitor's fires.
The hill-folk keep to their own speech and their old wrongs; their hidden steads are on the high ground, and the eyes on the ridges miss nothing.
The North-South Road runs through it past Isengard; the ring-wall and the black tower stand in the valley's end under the mountain wall, and the place smells of smoke and iron.
Stump-fields and bitter brakes where woods once stood; the surviving groves are few and guarded. The land itself seems to remember being green.
West the Misty Mountains wall the sky, and the gorges of the Isen cut down through them — a loud river in a narrow bed, crossed at the fords where battles were fought.
Bare winters, wet autumns, and a wind that comes out of the Gap with ice in it; Dunland is a hard country that has been made harder.

land.name: Dunland Highlands
land.biome_hint: cool hills and ridges with mixed forest and pasture
land.description: Eastern highland zone backed by the southern Misty Mountains, with hills and ridges up to about twelve hundred feet, running in orderly lines and breaking westward into mesa‑like hills with flat tops and steep sides.[file:32]

land.name: Dunland Plains and Gwathló basin edge
land.biome_hint: temperate grasslands with scattered trees and marsh fringes
land.description: Western plateaus and low rolling hills that step down over fifty miles into the flat plains of the wide Gwathló basin, mostly grassy and nearly treeless except near settlements and stream corridors.[file:32]

land.name: Old South Road (Tiar Hariar)
land.biome_hint: engineered road across plateau edge and river valleys
land.description: The major highway skirting Dunland’s southern border, running east–west along the plateau edge from Tharbad toward the Isen Gap, carrying trade and travelers through Larach Duhnnan and clan territories.[file:32]

land.name: Larach Duhnnan
land.biome_hint: market town in upland valley with river and road access
land.description: Largest town of Dunland, built on a plateau overlooking the Dunstrem and the Old South Road, surrounded by an embankment with clan Feargan’s fortified hold on a raised hill; serves as main trade hub and neutral meeting‑ground for multiple clans.[file:32]

land.name: Caerdh Wood
land.biome_hint: cool mixed old forest in foothill basin
land.description: One of only two true forests in Dunland, a remnant of the primordial woods, considered mysterious and possibly haunted; hosts Daen Coentis temple‑observatories and three Drúedain villages.[file:32]

land.name: New Maresh marshes
land.biome_hint: freshwater marsh with raised hillocks and slow streams
land.description: Marshy area draining into the Dunstrem near its junction with the Gwathló, with hills rising above the wetlands to hold Stoor burrows and channels navigated by small boats among patches of quicksand.[file:32]

land.name: Temple of Justice valley
land.biome_hint: forested valley with religious complex and defensive works
land.description: A long dead‑end wooded valley about twenty‑five miles east‑south‑east of Cillien where the dark granite Temple of Justice stands on a low hill, with a stream and bridge at its mouth and steep walls guarded by lookout posts.[file:32]

facts.notes: Keep this Dunland object strictly for the foothills, plateaus, plains and valleys north of the Old South Road and below the alpine zone; the Southern Misty Mountains object above covers the high peaks and explicitly mountain-only flora, fauna and powers.[file:32]

people.military: Each Chief keeps from 100-400 Warriors as a permanent retinue. Each Clan can also raise 1,400-3,200 Warriors given 1-4 weeks. Tribes favor light armor and carry spears and melee weapons predominately.
people.description: Dunland is dominated by Dunlendings—Daen Lintis highlanders descended from the Daen Coentis—living in extended family bands within clans, but also includes Dúnedain estates, Stoors, Drúedain in Caerdh Wood, organized traders, bards, healers and a powerful Dark‑influenced Temple hierarchy.

source.supplement: Dunland and the Southern Misty Mountains

phrases: Dunland in winter is a stern and empty country — brown hills, thin smoke, and the white wall of the mountains closing the west.
Rain over Dunland is a grey ocean of water sweeping the downs; the Isen roars, the fords drown, and the hills stand black and dripping.
The cold comes out of the Gap with the west wind; it is the mountains' breath on Dunland's bare hills, and it spares no one.

aspect.en: The Cape and Bay of Forochel are a rough, cold and storm-wracked peninsula and bay thrusting into Belegaer and the Encircling Sea, the last remnant of lands once lying beyond the Iron Mountains, scarred by Morgoth’s malice but rich in marine life, whaling, furs and treacherous ice. Geology consists of barren shelf of granite worn smooth by the passage of great ice sheets, with little accessible mineral wealth.

rotation: Arctic peninsula of bare glacier-smoothed granite where the Lossoth hunt seals on winter ice and summer icebergs drift in dark green waters. Austere tundra beauty of coloured mosses, alpine flowers and arctic seabirds.

Arctic peninsula of bare glacier-smoothed granite, where the Lossoth track seals on winter ice and summer icebergs drift past in dark green water. Brief flowers in the tundra and Arctic seabirds on the cliffs.

Stunted conifers and birch in the sheltered southern valleys; tundra grasses and lichens on the exposed ground; rare medicinal herbs that the Lossoth have been gathering long enough to name. The flora is sparse and specific.

Granite polished by glaciers into rounded forms; the fjords cutting deep into the rock; the vast bay of the Ice Bay visible from the heights. A landscape made entirely by ice and water and the absence of heat.

The coldest inhabited land in Middle-earth. The southern valleys are bearable in summer; the interior is brutal in winter. The ice-fishing tradition requires going onto the frozen bay in temperatures that kill the careless.
Lossoth who hunt sea-mammals and gather roots and have a complete material culture adapted to arctic conditions. Their knowledge of the terrain and ice is the most specialised in the north.

land.name: Cape of Forochel
land.biome_hint: sub-arctic maritime peninsula with cliffs, tundra, glaciers and storm-exposed coasts
land.description: The glaciated peninsula jutting into Belegaer and Ekkaia, once part of Morgoth’s northern realm beyond the Iron Mountains, now a jagged landscape of cliffs, inlets and ice-scoured rock.[file:39]

land.name: Bay of Forochel
land.biome_hint: cold sea with seasonal pack-ice, rich marine megafauna and highly variable weather
land.description: An immense, ice-prone bay whose currents concentrate marine life but whose storms and shifting pack-ice routinely wreck ships and bergs.[file:39]

land.name: Ered Muil and Ered Rhívamar
land.biome_hint: cold mountains with mixed conifer valleys, bare ridges and avalanche-prone slopes
land.description: Forlorn mountain ranges dividing Forochel from the rest of Forodwaith and providing some of its more sheltered valleys, forests and predator habitats.[file:39]

land.name: Evermist valley
land.biome_hint: local micro-climate with denser forest, herbs and running water amid an otherwise harsh region
land.description: A hidden, relatively mild valley on the cape maintained by Elvish and spiritual power as a refuge and sanctuary, with richer vegetation than the surrounding land.[file:39]

facts.notes: Use this region for coastal, maritime and whaling routes, iceberg travel and interactions with Lossoth sea-hunters, Snow-elves and southern whalers; inland tundra and the broader herd-migration ecology are handled under Talath Uichel.[file:39] Bleak, barren arctic wastes where only the Lossoth live in snow-houses, hunting seals and whales. No trees grow in Forochel; only stubbly grasses and scrawny shrubs exist to feed the herds of Losrandir.

people.description: Forochel is the heartland of the Ystvät Talven sea-hunters and tundra folk, but also hosts Snow-elves, Noldorin mystics at Evermist and southern whaling expeditions, all under the distant shadow of Angmar.[file:39]

aspect.en: Mordor, the Black Land, is the volcanic plateau realm of the Dark Lord Sauron, walled in on three sides by the formidable mountain chains of Ephel Dúath and Ered Lithui. The plateau is arid, rugged, and heavily Orc-infested, serving as a fortress-kingdom of evil. Bedrock consists of black volcanic basalt giving the region its characteristic black, scorched appearance.

rotation: The Black Land — a volcanic plateau walled on three sides by the Ephel Dúath and the Ered Lithui, where the mountain Orodruin burns and the sky is a roof of ash and smoke.
Gorgoroth is barren by design — black basalt, slag-pits, and fumes; the armies that dwell here march on broad straight roads through a land that grows nothing.
The Morgai is the inner wall — a maze of ravines, scree and jagged ridges where the last bitter growth gives way to bare stone, and every path is watched.
Ash-clouded darkness blots the sky; time is hard to read under the gloom, and the air is bitter, drying, and thirsty as dust.
Across the plain the Mountain of Fire burns in its depths — rivers of flame flare in it and stain the darkness red; when it wakes, the earth shakes and the sky rains fire and black water.
Nothing here is clean — earth, air and water are all accursed; the pools are few and bitter, and the wind that blows is the breath of furnaces.

land.name: Gorgoroth Plain
land.biome_hint: scorched volcanic plateau with basalt rock faces and ash-clouds
land.description: A bare, wind-swept plain of black basalt and active volcanic vents.

facts.notes: Mordor remains an impenetrable natural fortress, viewed with terror by all Free Peoples.

people.military: Durthang: 200 Gondorian Soldiers. Cirith Ungol: 100 Gondorian Soldiers. Cirith Gorgor: 300 Gondorian Soldiers. Conquered Host: 11,000 Orc Warriors. 2,170 Uruk-hai. 750 Warg-riders. 100 Trolls.
people.description: Warlike populations of Orcs, Trolls, Half-Orcs, and dark Men loyal to Sauron.

phrases: Cold in Mordor is a knife in a sheath of fumes — it waits in the ravines and the shadows of the walls, and at night the plain gives up its heat and freezes.
Winter turns Gorgoroth from furnace to forge-cold; the ash is bound by black frost, and the red sky hangs low over the frozen pits.
Heat rules the plateau — the air is a kiln-breath through the fumes, the stone burns the foot, and the only water is warm and bitter.

aspect.en: Forithilien, or North Ithilien, is the northern part of Gondor’s eastern Anduin province between the Great River and the Ephel Dúath, stretching from the Dead Marshes and Nindalf southward to the valley of the Ithilduin (later Morgulduin). It is the section of Ithilien most clearly shown in The Lord of the Rings, where Frodo, Sam and Gollum travel towards Cirith Ungol and where Faramir’s rangers maintain secret refuges like Henneth Annûn. In Gondor’s strength it is famed as a fair, fertile land of climbing woods, swift streams and rich gardens; by the late Third Age it is largely depopulated and serves as a hidden war-ground between Gondor’s rangers and the forces moving out of Mordor.

rotation: Northern Ithilien at the edge of the Shadow — the Morgul Vale cuts the hills, its stream polluted and its air oppressive, and the dead city stands at its mouth.
The land was once the garden of Gondor; now the pale luminous meadows of the vale steam with deadly vapour, and the water sounds cold and cruel in the dark.
The wraith-road and the Harad Road meet at the Cross-roads; a broken statue of a king sits crowned with white flowers, a small defiance of green in the grey land.
Sheer stairs climb the vale's western wall — the Straight and the Winding Stairs, cut between rock faces and riddled with the crevices of forgotten winters.
The woods grow paler and more silent as the vale nears; beyond the eastern rim the sky is stained red, and it is hard to tell dawn from the fires of Mordor.
Rangers still move in the northern hills, and the green things of Ithilien fight a slow war against the valley's poison — a fair land in the Shadow's hand, but not yet dead.

land.name: North Ithilien wooded hill-belt
land.biome_hint: warm-temperate wooded hills with mixed broadleaf and conifer trees, many herbs and flowers, and frequent small streams
land.description: The main band of climbing woods and hills between the Anduin valley floor and the lower slopes of the Ephel Dúath, forming the landscape through which Frodo, Sam and Gollum travel and where most of Faramir’s ranger activity occurs.[web:221][web:226]

land.name: Ravines and waterfall basins (Henneth Annûn-type sites)
land.biome_hint: cool, moist microclimates with shade-tolerant plants, mosses and ferns within an otherwise warm region
land.description: Steep-sided ravines and cliff basins where swift streams drop from the slopes into sheltered bowls; these host waterfalls like Henneth Annûn and provide ideal locations for hidden refuges, with dense vegetation and complex microclimates.[web:221][web:226]

land.name: Anduin-margin terraces and clearings
land.biome_hint: fertile, well-watered ground with a mix of wild herbs, former garden species and meadow plants
land.description: Terraces and clearings along the westward edge of North Ithilien overlooking or near the Anduin, where earlier Gondorian settlement had fields, gardens and small harbours, now mostly overgrown but still forming more open, fertile patches within the general woodland.[web:221][web:224]

facts.notes: For your map and biome system, treat Forithilien as Tolkien’s primary Ithilien zone: a north-central, warm-temperate Anduin–Ephel Dúath belt with exceptional plant richness, many small streams and ravines, and a human geography dominated in the late Third Age by rangers and war traffic rather than settled towns.[web:221][web:224][web:225][web:226][web:228]

people.description: In Forithilien’s late Third Age state, permanent civilian settlement has largely withdrawn across the Anduin, but its land still bears the imprint of Gondor’s earlier occupation and its present use as a hidden war-front. The primary human presence is Faramir’s rangers, operating from secret refuges among the woods and cliffs, with enemy movements from Mordor crossing the region along roads and tracks.

source.supplement: Tolkien (LotR) with Ithilien / Gondor regional material

phrases: Northern Ithilien in winter is a pale country at the edge of the Shadow — frost on the broken towers, ice in the Morgul's steam, and the red sky beyond the pass.
A cold that is not all of winter hangs about the Vale; it breathes off the poisoned stream and climbs the stairs on silent feet.

aspect.en: Nurn is the more fertile, semi-arid southern province of Mordor surrounding the highly saline Lake Nurnen. Enriched by volcanic soils and watered by mountain streams, Nurn serves as the slave-worked breadbasket feeding the massive armies of Sauron.

rotation: The only productive farmland in Mordor, surrounding the saline Lake Nurnen. Slave-worked fields of sorghum and barley under Orc overseers; grey-green lake water, salt-white shores and a horizon that always smells of ash.

The farming province of Mordor around saline Lake Nurnen, worked by slave labour under Orc overseers. Grey-green water, salt-white shores and the smell of ash on every wind that comes over the Ered Lithui.

Volcanic enrichment makes the soil productive despite the aridity; slave-worked fields of grain and sorghum produce the food that the armies need. The productivity is real; the system that produces it is not.

The lake sits in a depression below the plateau level; it has no outlet and the salt concentration rises year by year. The shore is white; the water is bitter. Fish of a particular salt-adapted kind survive in it.

The single region of Mordor where conditions permit agriculture. It's warmer than the plateau; the lake provides moisture that the rest of Mordor lacks; the volcanic soil does the rest. The combination is almost reasonable.
Slaves from across the south and east working the fields they don't own. Orc guards maintaining order for the armies that eat the harvest. The logistics of feeding an empire are not romantic.

land.name: Plains of Nurnen
land.biome_hint: semi-arid volcanic plains with intensive grain farming
land.description: Fertile volcanic plains irrigated by rivers coming off the Ephel Dúath.

facts.notes: Lake Nurnen is a bitter, saline, and chemical-heavy inland sea with no natural outlet.

people.description: Populated by tens of thousands of slaves and their Orc taskmasters.

aspect.en: Drúwaith Iaur, or Old Púkel-land, is an extremely remote, isolated, and obscure territory in northwestern Gondor, bordering Andrast to the west and the Westmarch to the east. Once claimed and nominally administered by Gondor, the region fell into extreme desertion and depopulation following the Great Plague of T.A. 1636. By T.A. 1640, no Dúnedain remain, leaving the wild, rugged, and uncultivated terrain to be ruled at a clan level by scattered tribes of Dunmen (Dunir) and native Drúedain (Wild Men).

rotation: Remote northwestern Gondor, abandoned by the Dúnedain after the Great Plague. Wild Drúedain and Dunir clans rule rocky hills and ravines of short violent waterfalls, invisible to and uncaring of any outside authority.

Northwestern Gondor abandoned after the Great Plague, reclaimed by wild heath and the Drúedain and Dunir clans who were always more at home here than the Gondorians. Rocky ravines and short waterfalls; authority of no kind.

Unmanaged coastal heathland on the exposed ground; mossy forest pockets in the ravines; rough marsh in the valley bottoms. The land is recovering from cultivation with the enthusiasm of landscape that was never fully domesticated.

The headlands here are dramatic — short cliffs and surge channels cut into the rock. The coast is not navigable for most of the year; the ravines are not traversable without local knowledge. Both features are defensive.
Atlantic climate that was always too wet and too exposed for comfortable Gondorian settlement. The Drúedain, who came from different expectations, find it perfectly suited.

Drúedain who were here before Gondor came and are still here now that Gondor is gone. The land fits them in a way it never quite fit the Dúnedain; their relationship to it is comfortable in the manner of long occupancy.

land.name: Old Púkel-land wilderness
land.biome_hint: wet maritime hills and uncultivated grasslands with dense mossy valleys
land.description: The rugged, roadless, and disorienting hills and valleys making up the core territory of Druwaith Laur.

facts.notes: Drúwaith Iaur remains an unadministered 'domain of Wild Men' on Gondor's western border, viewed with anxiety by the settlers of the Westmarch.

people.description: Entirely depopulated of Gondorian settlers; inhabited solely by native Drúedain and rustic Dunlending clans.

aspect.en: Southern Gondor comprises the fertile river valleys, coastal plains, highland vales and mountain flanks between the White Mountains (Ered Nimrais) and the Bay of Belfalas, encompassing the provinces of Lebennin, Belfalas/Dor-en-Ernil, Lamedon, Anfalas and the Pinnath Gelin—the heartland of Númenórean civilization in Middle-earth.

rotation: Sub-region in the upper Morthond valleys, defined by its rock fords: easy summer crossings over bright water, dangerous winter traps of ice and flood. Pine and mountain birch, Gondorian miners and alpine herders in the high vales.

Upper Morthond valleys defined by rock fords — easy enough in summer, lethal traps of ice and flood in winter. Pine and mountain birch on the valley sides, Gondorian miners at the ore-faces and alpine herders moving between the high pastures.

Stone pines on the lower mountain slopes mix into mast-pines and then pure conifer above a certain altitude. Lebethron grows in the highest valleys — dark and dense, prized for its workability and its particular smell.

The Morthond runs fast and clear between limestone walls; in winter the fords freeze from the edges inward and the stones below the ice are audible at night. The sound is beautiful and the crossing is not.

Sub-Mediterranean mountain climate: warm and dry in summer when the valley traps heat between the valley-walls; cold and snow-bound in winter when the passes close. Brief dramatic springs when the snowmelt turns the fords white.

Gondorian miners who know the ore-veins and alpine herders who know the high pastures and both of whom know the ford-timings better than any map records. The knowledge is local and doesn't travel well.

land.name: Lebennin (Land of Five Rivers)
land.biome_hint: temperate fertile lowlands with mixed agriculture, river floodplains, boggy bottomland and mountain-fringe conifer forests
land.description: The heartland of Southern Gondor, a fertile central plain watered by the Gilnduin, Celos, Serni, Erui and their tributaries; the most populous and productive province, dominated by farmland with boggy bottomlands near the rivers and conifer-covered mountain valleys to the north.[file:73]

land.name: Dor-en-Ernil / Belfalas
land.biome_hint: rocky Mediterranean-type coast with mountain mineral wealth, pine forests and maritime influence
land.description: The rocky peninsula and coastal province of the Prince of Belfalas, containing the Ered Torthonion and the citadel of Dol Amroth; silver-rich mountains, the sacred kirinki birds and the Elven haven Edhellond define its character.[file:73]

land.name: Anfalas and Pinnath Gelin
land.biome_hint: low coastal plain with fens, salt marshes, fishing grounds and rolling highland pasture
land.description: A long, thin coastal land west of the Morthond with flat, waterlogged plains, fens and rich fishing grounds; the Pinnath Gelin highlands to the north support wool-producing sheep and a timber-mining economy.[file:73]

land.name: Lamedon
land.biome_hint: forested mountain vales and upland pastures with mineral-rich geology
land.description: Mountain province of the White Mountains rich in iron, copper and silver deposits; a militarized zone in early Third Age history, later transformed into a province supporting mining communities and highland farming.[file:73]

land.name: Cape of Andrast
land.biome_hint: wet Atlantic-type rocky cape with steep valleys, heavy rainfall and primitive settlement
land.description: The rugged, rain-battered westernmost cape of Southern Gondor where the White Mountains bend into the sea; steep-sided green valleys and bare peaks home to the Dunir (Orodbedhrim), essentially untouched by Gondorian civilization.[file:73]

land.name: Ethir Anduin (Great Delta)
land.biome_hint: subtropical-type estuarine delta with marshes, swamps, tidal channels and rich aquatic biodiversity
land.description: The vast, meandering delta of the Anduin where it meets the Bay of Belfalas, created by the Númenórean Downfall's Great Wave; a unique ecosystem of swamps, channels, marsh and tidal flats with crocodiles, fishing cats and swamp tribes.[file:73]

land.name: Tolfalas
land.biome_hint: geologically active island with volcanic soils, hot springs, endemic sacred trees and nesting sea turtles
land.description: A volcanic island in the Bay of Belfalas with dramatic topography, hot springs, active minor eruptions and the sacred oiolair trees; settlement has always been marginal due to geological instability.[file:73]

land.name: Bay of Belfalas
land.biome_hint: warm temperate sea with rich coastal fisheries, marine mammals, whale migration routes and volatile weather
land.description: The great bay forming the southern coast of Gondor, sitting on the continental shelf and rich in marine life; critical for trade, fishing and naval power but plagued by unpredictable storms and Corsair threats.[file:73]

facts.notes: Southern Gondor's natural environment has been extensively reshaped by Númenórean colonization; the biomes encoded here reflect the Third Age T.A. 1640 state, not a pristine natural landscape; the most 'wild' zones are the Cape of Andrast, Ethir Anduin delta, upper mountain vales and Tolfalas. Harondor (the arid plateau south of the Poros) is treated as a separate region.[file:73]

people.description: Southern Gondor is the most populous and civilized part of Gondor, dominated by Dúnedain nobility and the Daen-Dúnedain mixed population of the river plains, with Daen highlanders (Orodbedhrim) in the upland vales, swamp peoples in the Ethir Anduin, and Grey-elves at Edhellond.

aspect.en: Southern Gondor comprises the fertile river valleys, coastal plains, highland vales and mountain flanks between the White Mountains (Ered Nimrais) and the Bay of Belfalas, encompassing the provinces of Lebennin, Belfalas/Dor-en-Ernil, Lamedon, Anfalas and the Pinnath Gelin—the heartland of Númenórean civilization in Middle-earth.

rotation: Westernmost cape of Gondor where the White Mountains plunge into Belegaer in vertical cliffs. Dark fern-and-yew valleys shelter the Orodbedhrim tribe of Drúedain, so invisible in the terrain that Gondor's maps cannot find them.

Westernmost cape of Gondor where the White Mountains drop in vertical cliffs into Belegaer. The Orodbedhrim Drúedain are invisible in the fern-and-yew valleys; Gondor's maps show the coastline but not the people.
Fern, yew and ancient oak in the narrow valleys; exposed heath on the headlands; the sea accessible only through the cliffs or by paths the Drúedain have made and maintained for their own use.
The cape catches the full Atlantic weather with nothing to the west for a thousand miles. The cliffs take the swell; the valleys are sheltered enough for habitation if you know them.
Wet and wild, with the Atlantic climate at its most pronounced. The wind here has direction and purpose. Rain arrives on specific days rather than as a general condition.
Orodbedhrim Drúedain who have been invisible in this landscape since before Gondor existed. Gondor has walked past them for centuries without noticing. They find this arrangement satisfactory.
