aspect.en: Dagorlad is the wide, flat battle-plain north and northeast of Udûn and the main pass into Mordor, once covered with wild grains and grasses and now a bare, declining expanse dotted with cairns and barrows where the Last Alliance fought Sauron at the end of the Second Age.

rotation: The battle-plain before the Black Gate — cracked earth, slag-mounds and reeking pits where the hosts of the Last Alliance fought and nothing has grown rightly since.
North of the plain the Dead Marshes spread — a drowned waste of meres and reeds where corpse-lights burn over the pools and the faces of the drowned wait beneath the green water.
Three pale dusty roads run to the Morannon and no further. The land between them is a graveyard with no graves — the dead are under the pools, or the dust, or nowhere.
A bitter east wind blows here off the heights of the Emyn Muil; it carries the cold smell of decay and turns sharply cold at dusk.
Nothing lives here but carrion-birds and the faint lights on the fen-water. The mounds that should be barrows are pits of filth; the land itself seems to exhale poison.
Before dawn the air sometimes brings a message — a breath from the south with a faint tang of the Sea, as if to prove the world is not all shadow.

land.name: Dagorlad (Battle-plain)
land.biome_hint: dry temperate battle-plain with sparse grasses, thorny shrubs and burial mounds
land.description: A wide, flat, grassy plain north and northeast of Udûn and the main pass into Mordor, once covered with wild grains and now a bare field of cairns, barrows and shallow graves where the Last Alliance broke Sauron’s armies.[file:37]

land.name: Haudh-en-Ohtarrin Morin (Mound of the Black Warriors)
land.biome_hint: low grassy mound on arid plain with subterranean burial chambers
land.description: A long, low barrow on the plain said to hold Black Númenórean captains loyal to Sauron, its doors trapped and its crypts filled with ghoul-animated remains.[file:37]

land.name: Eastern Dagorlad estates and ruins
land.biome_hint: ruined farms and manors on marginal grassland, encroached by marsh
land.description: Former Gondorian estates like Parth Mallin that once tried to use the plain as granary and grazing land, now largely abandoned, flooded or converted into strongholds by bandits.[file:37]

land.name: Tir Nindor and Caras Gwindor corridor
land.biome_hint: fortified stone and timber structures amid lightly settled plains and wetlands
land.description: The crossroads fortress of Tir Nindor and its nearby town Caras Gwindor and waystation Eithel Celebrin, forming Gondor’s main bastion and service hub on the approach between the Anduin, Dagorlad and Mordor.[file:37]

facts.notes: This object treats Dagorlad primarily as the battle-plain and Gondorian frontier immediately north of Mordor; the Dead Marshes, Nindalf and associated wetlands are modeled separately to preserve their distinct flora, fauna and hydrology while still acknowledging that the marshes now overlap and partially drown the eastern Dagorlad graves.[file:37]

people.description: Dagorlad in T.A. 1640 lies between Gondor’s waning eastern power and the encroaching Shadow; it hosts Gondorian soldiers and settlers, Asdriag Easterling herders, urban Northmen merchants, Marshmen refugees at the margins, Orc warbands and Trolls, with Elves and Dwarves as rare visitors and Undead as a growing, unnatural presence.

phrases: Dagorlad under winter is the bleakest face of the world — frost on the slag, ice on the meres, and the dead lights burning cold over the frozen pools.
The cold of Dagorlad is an unnatural cold, the cold of the marsh and the grave; it does not come with the wind so much as rise from the ground.
In heat the plain reeks and shimmers; the pits breathe out their fumes, and the very air over Dagorlad is a slow poison under the red sun.

aspect.en: The Vale of Imladris (Rivendell) is a deeply cloven, hidden valley at the western feet of the Misty Mountains in eastern Rhudaur, carved by the Bruinen (Loudwater). It forms a small but varied enclave of high hills, steep forested slopes and a sheltered inner valley dominated by Elrond’s house. Surrounded by the harsher lands of Rhudaur (Highlands, Trollshaws and Lowlands), Rivendell is an ‘island of refuge’ where Elves and Dúnedain hold back the darkness of Trolls, Hillmen, Wolves and Orcs in the wider region.[file:244]

rotation: The Last Homely House east of the Sea — a hidden valley cleft deep between the moors and the mountains, green and sheltered where everything outside it is bare.
The Bruinen runs loud through the valley — cold mountain water over grey stones, crossed at the ford where the flood, when the Elves will it, rises like white riders.
Pine and heath on the high moors; birch and beech and green shade in the vale. The valley is found late and suddenly, and left with regret.
Warm evenings on the terraces while the lower valley falls into shadow; running and falling water sounds nearby, and the air smells of trees and flowers.
Mist lies silver on the valley at dawn; dew glimmers on yellow leaves, gossamer twinkles on the bushes, and snow whitens the eastern peaks.
A refuge and a border-post at once — the last fair house before the wild, where the memory of elder days is kept and the way east begins at the gate.

land.name: Vale of Imladris (Hidden Valley of Rivendell)
land.biome_hint: sheltered cool-temperate valley with mixed forests, streams and Elven cultivation amid otherwise harsh uplands
land.description: A narrow, deeply cloven valley along the western side of the Misty Mountains where Elrond founded Rivendell after the fall of Eregion; it is accessed by a hidden side road off an uncertain track beyond the Bruinen ford and is protected by both terrain and Elvish enchantments.[file:244] The approach is Absurd to find by accident and still Very Hard even for those who have visited before, while evil or hostile beings suffer increasing discomfort and fear from Elrond’s wards as they near the valley.[file:244]

land.name: Rhudaur Highlands (Ettenmoors, Ettendales, Pinefells)
land.biome_hint: rocky, cool-temperate uplands with sparse soils, boggy basins and large coniferous forests, snow-fed streams and harsh winters
land.description: The Highlands of Rhudaur adjoining Rivendell are formed by the eastern foothills of the snow-capped Misty Mountains and the Giants’ Hills; they include the Ettenmoors (a 'Granite Sea' of boulder-strewn, jagged hills with minimal topsoil), the boggy Ettendales with many springs feeding the Mitheithel, and the heavily wooded Pinefells of evergreen forest.[file:244]

land.name: Trollshaws and Yfelwyd (Evil Woods)
land.biome_hint: patchy temperate woodland and brush with pockets of deep old forest, rough ground and high predator density
land.description: The central part of Rhudaur between Mitheithel and Bruinen, called the Trollshaws, is a hilly region of scattered woodlands and dense tree-groves separated by open ground and heavy brush favoured by wolves.[file:244] Its southern true forest, the Yfelwyd or Evil Woods, is older, deeper and more dangerous, home to Hill-trolls and hazardous plants like the Black Vine.[file:244]

land.name: Lowlands and the Angle (En Egladil) and Oiolad
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate, wind-exposed short-grass plains with thin soils, scattered trees and fertile strips only along rivers
land.description: The Lowlands to the south and west of Rivendell include the Angle (En Egladil) between the rivers Mitheithel and Bruinen, and the great northern plain of Eriador (Oiolad) west of the Mitheithel.[file:244] These are gently rolling, windswept grasslands with occasional wind-twisted trees and generally poor soils where agriculture is only viable along riverbanks and in more fertile silted patches.[file:244]

land.name: Rivers Mitheithel and Bruinen
land.biome_hint: cold, swift mountain-fed rivers with flood-prone stretches and narrow riparian belts of moisture-loving vegetation
land.description: The Mitheithel (Hoarwell) arises in Ettenmoors snow and Ettendales springs, becoming a raging torrent at thaw and freezing over dangerously in the coldest winters; it is difficult to ford between the Last Bridge and the Ettendales.[file:244]. The Bruinen forks, born in the Misty Mountains, are calmer and join at the apex of the Angle, marking the westernmost limit of Elrond’s realm and providing the enchanted ford that guards Rivendell’s approach.[file:244]

facts.notes: Use this region object for any mapping or biome work around the Vale: Rivendell itself should be treated as a small, magically sheltered forested valley pocket embedded inside the harsher upland and woodland mosaics of eastern Rhudaur (Highlands, Trollshaws, Lowlands) described in the module.[file:244]

people.description: The Vale of Rivendell is centred on Elrond’s Elvish household and the Rangers of the North, but the surrounding Rhudaur region also includes Hillmen and Dunlendings, as well as scattered Dúnedain settlements that decline over time. The module treats Rivendell as a self-contained Elven estate with its own internal social order, set amid a sparsely populated and increasingly hostile human landscape.[file:244]

phrases: Rain comes down the valley soft and cold; the Bruinen rises, the mountains vanish in mist, and Rivendell is shut away behind a curtain of silver.
Summer lingers in Rivendell beyond its season — warm air on the terraces, long light in the leaves, and the sound of water falling into evening.
Rivendell in winter is a green heart in a grey land — frost and wind on the high moors, and warm light and falling water in the sheltered vale.

aspect.en: Rhudaur is the eastern successor state of Arnor, a rugged, sparsely settled land between the Ettenmoors, the Trollshaws and the Angle. It stretches from the Ettenmoors and Ettendales in the north down through the Pinefells and Trollshaws to the rolling lowlands between the rivers Mitheithel and Bruinen, forming a harsh frontier of jagged hills, evergreen forests, boggy vales and predator-haunted woodlands.

rotation: The Lone-lands — a wilderness of low rolling hills, tussock and thorn between the last farms and the mountains' feet, where the East Road runs empty for a hundred miles.
This was once ploughed country under the old kingdom; now the only walls are ruins and the only fields are heather and bog. The mounds on the ridges are the graves of forts.
The East Road is the single thread of travel — pale and straight through empty land, with the mountains ahead and nothing behind but the wind.
Willow and alder in the wet bottoms, bare stone on the heights; the streams run loud after rain and the land is all water or all dust by turns.
No villages, no inns, no watch. The sky is the biggest thing here, and the weather owns it — rain and cold and the long searching wind.
After rain the clouds break and a wandering moon shows the drowned country; the Road shines wet and the hills are black on every side.

land.name: Ettenmoors (Môr Ithvaen, 'Granite Sea')
land.biome_hint: cold, rocky highland with minimal soil, scattered hardy vegetation and extreme terrain
land.description: Northernmost highlands of Rhudaur, a landscape of large hills and boulder-strewn terrain created by the uplift of the Misty Mountains. Jagged, little-weathered fells hold very little topsoil; boulders from child-sized to villa-sized lie in 'crazy jumbles' through which passage is impossible for anything larger than a rabbit. The region is bleak, treacherous and ideal for Trolls and other large predators.[file:132]

land.name: Ettendales
land.biome_hint: cool, boggy hill region with springs, stagnant wetlands and patchy grass/heath
land.description: Hill country south of the Ettenmoors, with smaller hills and less granite. The Ettendales hold many springs feeding the Mitheithel but suffer from poor drainage; vales between hills contain stagnant bogs, especially during spring thaw. Despite their water resources, the bogs make travel dangerous and limit settlement.[file:132]

land.name: Pinefells / Coldfells
land.biome_hint: cool evergreen forested hills with well-drained soils and persistent cold winds
land.description: Highlands immediately south and east of the Ettendales, similar in structure but better drained and heavily wooded. Dominated by evergreen forests, the region is known as the Pinefells; others call them 'Coldfells' due to the legendary cool winds and waters. It forms a heavily forested, cold highland belt between the Ettendales and Trollshaws.[file:132]

land.name: Trollshaws
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate mosaic of wooded groves, brush and open grassland in broken hill terrain
land.description: Central Rhudaur between the Mitheithel and Bruinen, rugged hill country with woodland scattered across it. Trees form small dense patches separated by open ground; heavy brush along grove edges extends inward where canopy thins. Popular with wolves, it is also the winter ground for Rhudaur’s vast herds of losrandir and the favored haunt of Hill Trolls.[file:132]

land.name: Coed Drug ('Evilwood')
land.biome_hint: dark, old-growth forest with closed canopy, thick understorey and a supernatural atmosphere
land.description: The most significant forest in Rhudaur, growing on the southern side of the Trollshaws above the Great East Road. An ancient, dense dual stand of woods, it exudes unease and 'latent evil'. Home to Forest Trolls and huge wolves; its immense trees block most sunlight, leaving the interior perpetually dim. Some inner places are said never to be touched by sun or moonlight, and even Elves and Hillmen fear to enter.[file:132]

land.name: The Angle (lowlands between Mitheithel and Bruinen)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate grassland and light woodland with strong winds and limited fertile pockets along rivers
land.description: Rolling grassy hills south of the Coed Drug and between the rivers, broken by jagged fells and occasional stands of trees. Constant northeast winds and rain off the fells strip away topsoil, so agriculture is difficult except along relatively protected and fertile riverbanks. It forms Rhudaur’s main lowland and agricultural zone, albeit poor compared to the rest of Eriador.[file:132]

land.name: Oiolad ('Endless Plain' of the Eredoriath)
land.biome_hint: open grassland/plain adjoining Rhudaur, serving as raiding and travel corridor
land.description: Flat plain west of the Mitheithel beyond Rhudaur’s lowlands, used as raiding ground by the Rhudaurrim and Hillmen into more favored regions. While technically outside core Rhudaur, it is closely linked to its economy and warfare, providing a contrast to the rugged homeland fells.[file:132]

facts.notes: This object isolates Rhudaur as a region within Arnor: The Land, focusing on geographic subzones (Ettenmoors, Ettendales, Pinefells/Coldfells, Trollshaws, Coed Drug, Angle) and mapping the general Flora & Fauna of Eriador onto these specific landscapes. The key Rhudaur-specific ecological elements are the Pinefells evergreens, the Coed Drug ancient 'Evilwood', the losrandir herds and the concentration of Hill and Forest Trolls. Climate and hydrology are dominated by snow-fed highlands (Ettenmoors/Ettendales) and the swift Mitheithel, with constant winds limiting agriculture to narrow riverine bands.[file:132]

people.military: 4,500 Warriors and Eastern Mercenaries, usually grouped according to tribe.
people.population: 50,000: 35,000 Hillmen in thirteen tribes and 15,000 Dunlendings in eleven tribes.
people.description: Rhudaur’s population is sparse and concentrated in hill-country and strategic sites such as Cameth Brin and the Angle. Politically, it is the easternmost and least stable of Arnor’s successor realms, dominated by Hillmen and later influenced or controlled by Angmar. The Arnor book’s detailed cultural and political treatment is split across Arnor: The Land and Arnor: The People; here we focus on the geographic side, noting the Hillmen and Rhudaurrim as the characteristic inhabitants of this harsh landscape.

phrases: The Lone-lands under rain are a drowned and echoing wilderness — every hollow a stream and every stream in spate.
Winter strips the Lone-lands to bone — frozen heath, pale grass, and the empty track of the Road running on to horizons without a light.
The cold here is a great emptiness made palpable; it comes with the wind off the downs and stays long after the wind has gone.

aspect.en: Fangorn is an ancient forest on the southeastern slopes of the Misty Mountains, bordered to the north by the plains running to the Silverlode (Celebrant), to the west by the high peaks, to the east by the Wold and to the south by the open plains of Calenardhon. It is the last great remnant of the immense forest that once covered much of Eriador and Calenardhon and is uniquely tended by the Ents, who act as tree-herds and guardians of this 'giant garden'. The module also treats the surrounding borderlands along the Entwash and Limlight as part of the same regional system.

rotation: Fangorn — the oldest wood left in the world, deep and tangled under its eaves, where the trees are watchful and the paths are the forest's to give or take.
The Entwash comes down through it from the mountains; beside the stream the growth is dark and thick, and the air is stifling and strangely thin beneath the boughs.
The floor is buried in drifts of leaves; shafts of sunlight come down like pillars through the canopy, and bark that looks grey in the gloom gleams brown and ochre where the light finds it.
The shepherds of the trees still walk here — slow, deep-voiced, and older than kingdoms. The wood has a will and a memory, and it does not forget an axe.
Northward the wood thins to birch-groves and bare slopes where gaunt pines stand; a sharp white peak shows beyond the valley like a horn of the mountains.
The forest is not safe for hasty feet or sharp steel; under its green dusk the silence is alive, and the traveller who harms it is watched from the beginning to the end.

land.name: Fangorn Forest (core)
land.biome_hint: cool-temperate, closed-canopy old-growth forest with high humidity, rich soils and low undergrowth
land.description: The core of Fangorn lies under the dense canopy between the southern Misty Mountain foothills and the eastern limestone hills. Rich soil, massive trees and Ent-managed sectionalization define this area, with minimal undergrowth and a dark, humid, terrarium-like atmosphere in summer. Ent homes, nurseries and Huorn groves are scattered throughout.[file:154]

land.name: Eastern limestone hills and Treebeard’s watch
land.biome_hint: rocky limestone hills with short cliffs, forested slopes and patchy soil over bedrock
land.description: On the eastern side of Fangorn, sloping rocky hills of limestone rise from the plains, forming short cliffs as weather and streams erode them. Treebeard’s watch, where Merry and Pippin meet him, is an example of these rock formations, which create natural lookouts and microhabitats within the forest edge.[file:154]

land.name: Misty Mountain foothills (western edge)
land.biome_hint: cool, rocky foothills with mixed forest and open rock, source of major rivers
land.description: To the west, Fangorn quickly transitions into higher mountain foothills as it meets the Misty Mountains. The land rises through sloping, rocky ground into high combs where springs of the Entwash and Limlight emerge. Vegetation shifts toward more cold-tolerant species and open rocky areas near the treeline.[file:154]

land.name: Entwash (Onodló) and Limlight (Limlaith) river corridors
land.biome_hint: riparian forest and wetland strips within the larger forest, transitioning to open river plains
land.description: Two major rivers, the Entwash and Limlight, arise from springs in the combs of the Misty Mountains and flow through Fangorn before entering the plains. Numerous tributaries join them inside the forest, carving channels and creating moist microhabitats along their routes. The Entwash in particular links Fangorn to the plains of Calenardhon and beyond.[file:154]

land.name: The Wold (eastern border)
land.biome_hint: open, windy limestone upland/steppe adjoining forest, with grassland and sparse trees
land.description: To the east of Fangorn lies the Wold, a limestone-based upland or plain whose rocks and soils mirror those of Fangorn’s eastern hills. It is largely open, with grasses and low shrubs and only scattered trees, making a sharp visual and ecological contrast with the dense Entwood.[file:154]

land.name: Calenardhon plains (southern border)
land.biome_hint: temperate grassland suitable for horse-herding and agriculture, with strong wind exposure
land.description: South of Fangorn stretch the open plains of Calenardhon, the future Rohan: broad grasslands used by the Calenardhons for herding and mounted warfare. These plains are broken only by rivers and occasional hills, providing a stark edge to the forest and a major corridor for human movements near Fangorn’s southern eaves.[file:154]

facts.notes: This object treats 'Fangorn Forest and Borders' as a single region with an Ent-managed ancient forest core, flanked by limestone hills and Misty Mountain foothills, and bordered by the Wold and Calenardhon plains. The climate and flora sections emphasize Fangorn’s uniqueness as a 'giant garden' with high tree diversity, sectionalized groves and minimal undergrowth, while the fauna and people sections highlight Ents, Huorns and mixed border populations. For your Middle-earth-over-Europe map, Fangorn should be mapped as a dense, humid, cool-temperate old-growth forest with strong microclimatic buffering, adjacent to continental grasslands and mountain foothills, and serving as a key ecological and cultural node between Rohan and the southern Misty Mountains.[file:154]

people.military: 150 Ents. 2,000 Huorns.
people.description: Fangorn’s 'people' straddle the line between fauna and cultures: Ents and Huorns are central, while human and other groups inhabit or contest the borders along the Entwash and Limlight. The module splits these between 'Politics and Power: Fangorn' (Ents, Huorns) and 'Politics and Power: The Borders' (Calenardhons, Silvan Elves, Barz Thrugrim, etc.).

phrases: In summer Fangorn is a green and golden heart, warm and vast; the light falls through the boughs like a memory of the Elder Days.
Fangorn under winter sleeps with its eyes open — snow on the eaves, stillness under the boughs, and the slow thought of the shepherds moving in the deep wood.
Rain on Fangorn is the forest drinking — a soft hiss on the eaves and a deep smell of wet leaves rising to meet it.

aspect.en: Southern Mirkwood and Southern Rhovanion form a wild, embattled region stretching from the Old Forest Road down to the Dagorlad and the Emyn Muil, dominated by the dark forest around Dol Guldur, the horse-plains of Talath Harroch, and the Anduin vales and Brown Lands that lie between Mirkwood and Gondor. Geology consists of primarily sedimentary strata of limestone and shale, with significant granite projections such as the cinder cone of amon lanc and the mountains of mirkwood.

rotation: Dol Guldur's fortress dominates southern Mirkwood from Amon Lanc. Trees twisted toward darkness, Great Spider webs blocking every path and the smell of decay that stays in the clothes for days. The Brown Lands stretch dead beyond the Anduin.

Dol Guldur's fortress on Amon Lanc, and the forest that serves it. Trees twisted toward the dark hill as if magnetised; Great Spider webs blocking the paths; the smell of decay that comes from something older than rot.

Furry oak and chap-beech grown strange under the shadow — trunks thicker at the base than any forest has a right to be, the understorey killed by the spider-webs that filter what little light reaches the floor.

Amon Lanc at the centre: the volcanic hill that Dol Guldur occupies with the architectural inevitability of something that was always going to be there. The trees grow toward it as if they have no choice.

The climate of Dol Guldur's shadow is perpetual chill even in summer; the canopy blocks both sun and wind so that the air inside is still and cold and smells of things that decompose slowly. The Brown Lands begin across the Anduin.
Great Spiders who have been here since before Sauron returned, and orcs who serve the fortress, and the fortress itself, which serves a purpose that the whole forest bends itself to enable.

land.name: Angaladadh (Northwest quadrant)
land.biome_hint: dense temperate hardwood–evergreen forest with heavy undergrowth
land.description: The deep northern heart of Southern Mirkwood’s forest, north-west of Dol Guldur, where the canopy remains thick, the old rose-tree circles still stand and Elven influence is strongest.

land.name: Aur Esgalabar / Romeniaur (Northeast quadrant)
land.biome_hint: mosaic of forest edge, scrub and plains
land.description: The northeastern wedge where the forest thins and gives way to grassland and the East Bight, mixing woodland, scrub and open country.

land.name: Talath Harroch (The Plains)
land.biome_hint: cool temperate grassland and farmland with scattered homesteads
land.description: The broad plains southeast of Mirkwood, home to horse-herding Northmen, wild herds and culcarnix, with long snowy winters and violent spring rains.

land.name: Nan Lothanduin / Nan Anduin
land.biome_hint: broad river valley with alluvial fields, groves and settlements
land.description: The Anduin vales south of the Old Forest Road and opposite Dol Guldur, containing fertile pockets such as Tharlorien, the North and South Undeeps and Beijabar holdings.

land.name: Dol Guldur (Amon Lanc)
land.biome_hint: rocky volcanic hill with dead trees and corrupted scrub
land.description: A stark, 3649‑foot volcanic cone on the southern eaves of Mirkwood, crowned and ringed by fortress walls and towers, once called the Naked Hill and now the hill of sorcery under Sauron’s control.

land.name: Emyn Guldur (Hills of Sorcery)
land.biome_hint: rocky hills with dark forest patches, caves and cliffs
land.description: Rugged hills and broken country around Dol Guldur, full of caves and shelves where spiders and fell beasts lair, and criss-crossed by secret Orc-paths.

land.name: Old Forest Road (southern sector)
land.biome_hint: forest-margin road through mixed woodland and clearings
land.description: The east–west road along the northern edge of Southern Rhovanion, carrying refugees and trade and linking the western vales with the eastern plains and forest entries.

land.name: Road to the Morannon
land.biome_hint: long overland route across river-vales and dry hills
land.description: The main north–south route from Nan Anduin across the Brown Lands toward the Black Gate, used increasingly by Sauron’s forces shifting from Dol Guldur to Mordor.

land.name: North and South Undeep
land.biome_hint: wide, shallow river reaches with rocky beds and down-like hills
land.description: Shallow fords of the Anduin where the river spreads over rock shelves, forming strategic crossing-points guarded and contested by Gondor and its enemies.

land.name: Brown Lands
land.biome_hint: dry temperate steppe on old terraced hills
land.description: Bleak, brown hills east of the Anduin whose ridges were once raised and irrigated garden beds tended by the Entwives, now covered in short dry grass and scarred by frost and neglect.

facts.notes: This object treats Southern Mirkwood and Southern Rhovanion as a single strategic and ecological unit in T.A. 1640: the haunted southern forest around Dol Guldur, the Talath Harroch horse-plains, the Anduin vales and Brown Lands, and the human and inhuman powers contesting them; individual sites such as Woodmen-town, Rhosgobel, Thorontir and Dol Guldur’s detailed layouts can be represented as separate site objects if needed. The largest forest in western Endor, dominated by oaks, maples, elms, and conifers. It has fallen under a stagnant, heavy shadow since the Necromancer established Dol Guldur, making southern reaches twisted, dark, and home to giant spiders.

people.military: 650 Warriors, led by local chieftains.
people.description: Southern Rhovanion is a country under siege: Beijabar and Wood-men cling to the western eaves, horse-lords and Gramuz Northmen fight for survival on the Talath Harroch, Gondor projects power along the Anduin and into Dor Rhûnen, Easterling tribes press from the east, and above all Dol Guldur and its Necromancer darken the forest and shape the fate of all inhabitants after the Great Plague.

source.supplement: Southern Mirkwood – Haunt of the Necromancer

facts.products: Lumber, hides, nuts, carved wooden boxes.

aspect.en: Lórien, the Golden Wood, is a secluded Elven forest-realm east of the Misty Mountains, ruled by Galadriel and Celeborn and defined by its golden mallorn trees, timeless beauty, and potent yet subtle Ring-lore.

rotation: The Golden Wood of Lórien — the mallorn-forest between Silverlode and Anduin, where the leaves turn gold and do not fall, and the light under the boughs is like everlasting evening.
Cerin Amroth rises at the heart — a green mound crowned with two rings of trees, white-barked without and golden within, where elanor and niphredil star the grass.
The city of the trees stands on a green hill; at night its lights move among the mallorn-leaves until the hill seems filled with stars, and song and the sound of a fountain fill the dark.
Streams thread the wood — Nimrodel's cold bright water at the eaves, the Silverlode running to the Anduin where golden leaves float on the ripples.
Time moves differently under the boughs; rain comes gentle and leaves all things fresh, and winter has no power in the heart of the wood.
The Galadhrim keep the fences; the unwelcome do not pass. Within, the world is gold and green and a music that the memory keeps forever after.

land.name: Lórien proper (Golden Wood)
land.biome_hint: dense temperate deciduous forest with magical mallorn stands along a major river
land.description: Forested realm on the east side of the Misty Mountains, centered on the mallorn woods along the river Celebrant, bounded by rivers and fields that separate it from neighboring lands.

land.name: Celebrant (Silverlode)
land.biome_hint: clear, cold forest river with wooded banks
land.description: Main river flowing through the heart of Lórien, providing water, fog, and reflective vistas beneath the mallorns.

facts.notes: This object treats Lórien as the Golden Wood region as a whole. Tightly defined sites like Caras Galadhon can be modeled as separate site objects if you want finer granularity.

people.symbol: A Golden Mallorn Tree on a Green Field
people.military: 100 Wardens. 1,300 Guardians.
people.description: Lórien is inhabited mainly by Silvan and Sindarin Elves under the rule of Galadriel and Celeborn, with a culture focused on preservation, song, subtle magic, and cautious isolation from the outside world.

source.supplement: Lórien & The Halls of The Elven Smiths

phrases: Winter cannot enter the heart of Lórien — beyond the Silverlode the wind may bite, but under the mallorns the gold leaves hold an older season.
Lórien in high summer is the world's own golden afternoon — light held in leaves, song on the water, and time gone slow.
Rain in Lórien is a soft grey blessing; it passes, and the leaves shine brighter than gold beneath the washed sky.

aspect.en:
The Shire was a country in northwestern Middle-earth, inhabited by the Hobbits. It was located in the region of Eriador, and was under the control of the Reunited Kingdom as a Free Land.
By the late Third Age it was one of the few heavily-populated areas left in Eriador. Its name in Westron was Sûza, "Shire," or Sûzat, "The Shire." Contrary to popular misconception, the Shire was not the birthplace of Frodo Baggins, as he was born in Buckland, which at the time was not formally part of the Shire despite being colonized by Shire hobbits.

rotation: The Shire — the green and ordered country of the hobbits: hedgerow-lined lanes, smial-doors in the hillsides, orchards, and the slow Water under the mill.
Four Farthings of the best farmland in the north — river-meadows, grain-fields, pipe-weed beds, and the high sheep-country of the Northfarthing moors.
The East Road runs through to the Brandywine Bridge; Buckland across the river is a strip of hedged land held against the Old Forest's black wall.
Mild weather and reliable rain; frost is rare and deep snow rarer. The hedgerows hold the wind, and the seasons come soft-footed and on time.
A land that minds its own business; the ways are safe, the doors are round, and the world outside is a rumour that comes late and is not much believed.
In autumn the trees are laden and the bees are busy; in spring the lanes are white with blossom. The year's wheel turns here as it should.

land.name: Forochel and the Icy North
land.biome_hint: arctic coastal tundra and sea-ice
land.description: The far northern portion of Arthedain reaches toward the Ice-bay of Forochel and the Forodwaith, a realm of ice-plains, tundra and bitter cold, inhabited mainly by the Lossoth and visited by Dúnedain only in times of dire need.[file:25]

land.name: North Downs
land.biome_hint: rocky downs with thin soils and open grass-heath
land.description: High rolling hills east of Lake Evendim, forming rocky ridges that march across northeastern Arthedain like massive natural altars; they shelter and overlook Fornost and serve as a defensive barrier toward Angmar.[file:25]

land.name: Lake Nenuial (Lake Evendim)
land.biome_hint: cool upland lake with stony shores and reeds
land.description: A large blue lake in north-central Arthedain, sheltered on three sides by the Hills of Evendim, with the ruined first capital of Annúminas on its southern shore.[file:25]

land.name: Annúminas
land.biome_hint: ruins on windy lake-hills
land.description: Elendil’s original capital of Arnor on the southern shore of Lake Evendim, once a glittering Númenórean city and now a crumbling ruin of marble and stone razed in T.A. 1409.[file:25]

land.name: Fornost Erain
land.biome_hint: fortified hill-city in rocky uplands
land.description: The Northern Fortress of the Kings, built on the southern slopes of the North Downs, ringed by dikes and walls, now the capital of Arthedain and seat of its Royal Court and Seers in T.A. 1640.[file:25]

land.name: Baranduin / Brandywine River
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with mixed woodland and farmland
land.description: A swift yet meandering river flowing over 500 miles from Lake Evendim to the Sea south of Harlindon, forming a major barrier and artery, with key crossings at the Brandywine Bridge and Sarn Ford and providing the Shire with water and fertile valley lands.[file:25]

land.name: Southern Arthedain and the Shire
land.biome_hint: temperate lowland farmland and hedged hills
land.description: The fertile southern part of the kingdom, once neglected by Dúnedain concerned with war, now intensively farmed and settled by hobbits of the Shire, with rolling hills, rich fields and the Green Hill Country.[file:25]

land.name: Weather Hills and Amon Sûl
land.biome_hint: treeless limestone ridges and exposed summits
land.description: Barren rocky ridges in the southeast forming a natural wall along the border, culminating at Weathertop (Amon Sûl), a thousand-foot hill that once bore the chief northern palantír tower and still dominates the Great East Road.[file:25]

land.name: Midgewater Marshes
land.biome_hint: cool, insect-ridden freshwater bog
land.description: Buzzing bogs below the Weather Hills, carved in glacial times and now collecting stagnant water in treacherous pools swarming with midges, making overland travel slow and unpleasant.[file:25]

land.name: White Downs, Far Downs and Tower Hills
land.biome_hint: chalk downs with short turf and coastal influence
land.description: Chalk cliffs and downs in the west of the Shire leading up to the Emyn Beraid (Tower Hills), where three ancient white towers overlook the estuary of the Lhûn and house a westward-looking palantír.[file:25]

land.name: Bree-land and the Greenway
land.biome_hint: temperate hill-country with fields and woodland patches
land.description: Region around Bree-hill where the Great East Road crosses the old North–South road (Greenway); Bree is surrounded by ditches, dikes and hedges rather than walls, and serves as a weathered but still significant stop for travelers and traders.[file:25]

facts.notes: This Arthedain object is meant to capture the realm as described around T.A. 1640 in Rangers of the North, with climate and landforms usable as a base layer for pathfinding, biome assignment and climate modeling; more focused regions like Angmar, Cardolan and Rhudaur are handled in their own supplements.[file:25]

people.military: Royal Forces: 540 Men at Arms. 370 Cavalry. 1,000 Rangers. Noble Forces: 2,150 Men at Arms. 620 Cavalry. 3,000 Levy.
people.population: 50,000 Dúnedain (not including the Shire and Bree-land).
people.description: Arthedain’s population is dominated by the high Men of the Dúnedain, with important minorities including the hobbits of the Shire, the Lossoth of Forochel, rivermen on the northern waters, Bree-landers at the crossroads, and scattered Northmen and Dunlendish groups on the borders.

phrases: The Shire in summer is all abundance — laden orchards, humming bees, fields high with hay, and long warm evenings over the Water.
Under winter the Shire turns quiet — frost on the thatch, snow along the lanes, and warm light in the windows behind the hedgerows.
Rain comes softly and often here; it silvers the hedges, fills the streams, and beads the long grass.
The land looks washed and grateful.

aspect.en: Arthedain is the northern Dúnedain kingdom in Eriador, cradled between the Blue Mountains and the Misty Mountains and bounded by the rivers Lhûn and Baranduin, a cool, sparsely populated realm of rocky hills, downs, marshes, and the Shire, ruled from Fornost as the last Númenórean realm in the North in T.A. 1640.

rotation: A village of Men and hobbits at the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway — a huddle of thatched roofs inside a hedge and dike on the green hill's flank.
Bree Hill rises steep above the gate; beyond the hedged townlands the Chetwood covers the northern slopes and the wild country begins at once to the east.
The Prancing Pony stands at the turning of the ways; behind its windows are firelight, smoke, many voices, and news of all the roads that still carry travellers.
Eastward the Midgewater Marshes spread flat and reedy — pools, midges and hidden birds, and no road through them worth the name.
Bree-land is an island of hearth and bed in a wilderness gone empty; the Greenway is grass-grown, the old kingdom is a story, and the inn is the last bright thing for fifty miles.
Mild but exposed weather — the east wind is bitter in winter, and the rain curtains the hill for days at a time when the westerlies come in.

land.name: Forochel and the Icy North
land.biome_hint: arctic coastal tundra and sea-ice
land.description: The far northern portion of Arthedain reaches toward the Ice-bay of Forochel and the Forodwaith, a realm of ice-plains, tundra and bitter cold, inhabited mainly by the Lossoth and visited by Dúnedain only in times of dire need.[file:25]

land.name: North Downs
land.biome_hint: rocky downs with thin soils and open grass-heath
land.description: High rolling hills east of Lake Evendim, forming rocky ridges that march across northeastern Arthedain like massive natural altars; they shelter and overlook Fornost and serve as a defensive barrier toward Angmar.[file:25]

land.name: Lake Nenuial (Lake Evendim)
land.biome_hint: cool upland lake with stony shores and reeds
land.description: A large blue lake in north-central Arthedain, sheltered on three sides by the Hills of Evendim, with the ruined first capital of Annúminas on its southern shore.[file:25]

land.name: Annúminas
land.biome_hint: ruins on windy lake-hills
land.description: Elendil’s original capital of Arnor on the southern shore of Lake Evendim, once a glittering Númenórean city and now a crumbling ruin of marble and stone razed in T.A. 1409.[file:25]

land.name: Fornost Erain
land.biome_hint: fortified hill-city in rocky uplands
land.description: The Northern Fortress of the Kings, built on the southern slopes of the North Downs, ringed by dikes and walls, now the capital of Arthedain and seat of its Royal Court and Seers in T.A. 1640.[file:25]

land.name: Baranduin / Brandywine River
land.biome_hint: temperate river valley with mixed woodland and farmland
land.description: A swift yet meandering river flowing over 500 miles from Lake Evendim to the Sea south of Harlindon, forming a major barrier and artery, with key crossings at the Brandywine Bridge and Sarn Ford and providing the Shire with water and fertile valley lands.[file:25]

land.name: Southern Arthedain and the Shire
land.biome_hint: temperate lowland farmland and hedged hills
land.description: The fertile southern part of the kingdom, once neglected by Dúnedain concerned with war, now intensively farmed and settled by hobbits of the Shire, with rolling hills, rich fields and the Green Hill Country.[file:25]

phrases: Bree under winter is a huddle of lit windows behind a hedge and a gate; beyond the dikes the bare country waits, cold and patient.
In rain the village smells of wet thatch and woodsmoke; the road is a river of mud, and travellers come in sodden and glad of the fire.
A hard cold settles on Bree-land; the wells rim with ice and the east wind finds every gap in door and shutter.

aspect.en: Dorwinion, or the 'Wineland,' is a wealthy and fertile country located along the northwest coast of the Sea of Rhûn and the lower reaches of the swift River Celduin and the rushing Uldona. Known throughout Middle-earth for producing the finest wines, its culture is dominated by the Dorwinrim, a hardy, adaptable, and highly diplomatic merchant people. Their capital, Shrel-Kain, is the largest port on the sea and serves as the mercantile and diplomatic hub of the entire region.

rotation: The Wineland on the northwest shore of the Sea of Rhûn, producer of the finest wines in Middle-earth. Shrel-Kain is the great inland sea's greatest port; the Dorwinrim are the diplomats and merchants who trade with half the world.
The Wineland on the northwest Sea of Rhûn, producer of the most valued wine in Middle-earth. Shrel-Kain's great port and the Dorwinrim merchants who trade with every kingdom that can reach them.

Terrace-cultivated vineyard estates on the sun-facing hill slopes; mixed woodland on the hills behind; the sea-plain below. The landscape is as organised as a ledger: every slope assigned a variety, every variety a market.

The Sea of Rhûn creates a moderating microclimate that makes viticulture possible this far north and east. The warmth off the inland sea extends the growing season enough for grapes that wouldn't survive twenty miles inland.

Warm summers with enough rain from the sea; mild winters that don't go below the point where the vines suffer. The agricultural calendar here is determined by the grapes and everything else works around them.

Dorwinrim merchants who have made diplomacy and commerce the same thing. They trade with Thranduil's Elves and with the Easterlings and with Gondor and they keep everyone's secrets equally, which is their main commercial advantage.

land.name: Celduin River Valley
land.biome_hint: humid river valley with intensive vineyards and deciduous tree lines
land.description: The fertile life-blood of Dorwinion, snaking over 800 miles and snaking with smaller streams like Angren and Athorn.

land.name: Shrel-Kain Port
land.biome_hint: maritime merchant port with heavy ship traffic and grand stone markets
land.description: The grand capital of Dorwinion and largest port on the Sea of Rhûn, situated upriver from the Celduin's mouth.

facts.notes: Dorwinion's wine trade reaches as far west as Thranduil's halls, using large river-rafts to navigate the Running River.

people.description: Inhabited by the Dorwinrim, a sophisticated, trade-focused Dunadan-allied people who wear bright, gaily-colored clothes and are renowned as shrewd bargainers.

aspect.en: The Drúadan Forest (S: 'Tawar-in-Drúedain') is an ancient, dense, and secretive oakwood situated in northeastern Gondor along the northern slopes of the White Mountains. Bordered by the beacon-hills of Eilenach and Nardol, this forest is the ancestral home of the Woses (Drúedain), a primeval, secretive race of master woodsmen who lead primitive, clan-based lives in hidden hollows and valleys completely apart from Gondorian civilization.

rotation: A dark remnant of the world's first woods, clinging to the feet of the White Mountains — close pines, deep silence, and paths that are not meant for outside feet.
The Stonewain Road runs through it half-buried — grey slabs laid before the City was built, still carrying those who the wood permits to pass.
The Wild Men of the woods live here and are seldom seen; their carved watch-stones stand along the ways, and the drums in the trees are the only greeting strangers get.
The forest is cool and dim even at midsummer; under the pines the air smells of resin and old earth, and sound does not carry far.
Few roads, fewer paths. The wood is a fortress without walls — the trees and their people have held it against every power that came through the valley.
Beyond the dark eaves the land opens to the plain of the City; inside them the world is a green dusk and a held breath.

land.name: Eilenach Glens and Stonewain Valley
land.biome_hint: cool, shaded limestone ravines with dense undergrowth and secret trails
land.description: A network of deep, hidden limestone ravines and narrow valleys where the Woses establish their hidden villages.

land.name: Drúadan Forest Quarries
land.biome_hint: abandoned stone cuts and rock faces with overgrown ivy
land.description: Ancient stone quarries on the edge of the forest, once used to build Minas Anor but now largely overgrown and abandoned.

facts.notes: The Woses no longer work in stone, but they maintain and revere the Pûkel-men stone statues carved by their ancestors, using them to guard their bounds.

people.military: 400 Hunters and Warriors.
people.description: Inhabited by approximately 1,800 Woses (Drúedain) divided among more than 130 family-level clans, with occasional Gondorian quarrymen on the margins.

phrases: Drúadan in winter is a dark pine-silence under the mountain — frost in the moss, rime on the old carved stones, and the unseen folk keeping their watch.
Rain in the Drúadan is a long soft hiss in the pine-tops and a black drip below; the forest drinks and says nothing.

aspect.en: The Isen — cold grey water out of the mountains, running through the Gap of Rohan between the moors. Its fords were famous and fought for; when the wizards' works dammed and turned it, its bed ran dry and silent, and the valley below became a waste of stumps.
The Ringlo runs quick and clear down from the high dales, cold snow-fed water good to drink, chattering over a bed of round stones before it slows toward the lowland fields.
The Lefnui tumbles fast and cold from the White Mountains, clear and sweet at its head but wild and unbridged, its rapids and shifting fords treacherous to any who try to cross without care.
A bright stream running down from the mountains into the sea-lands — cold and clean over dark stones, quick where the land falls, gentle in the green vales below.
The River Running — swift and clear out of the Lonely Mountain, winding south and east past the town of Dale and out onto the plains toward the Sea of Rhûn.
The Langwell runs down clear and icy from the northern heights, one of the young streams that feed the great river; sweet snow-melt over clean stone, cold enough to numb the hand that dips into it.

The Hoarwell — strong grey water out of the northern snows, swift and cold, crossed by the Last Bridge where the Road comes down to the wild. Its voice is the last sound of the settled lands before the Lone-lands begin.

The Loudwater of Rivendell — cold mountain water rushing loud over grey stones, rising from the snows of the Misty Mountains. It is crossed at the ford below the hidden valley, and when the lords of the vale will it, its flood rises like white riders to carry enemies away.
A shallow clear river across the empty lands — cool and quiet, forded where the old roads cross it, and flowing down to the fens of the Swanfleet where the reeds are a grey sea.

The Blackroot — dark cold water out of the mountain's root, running down the green vale under the shadow of the cliffs. It is born in the high snows and passes the dark wood of the Dimholt, and its name is remembered with the door that no foot returns from.
The Ciril runs quick and cold from the mountains, clear water over dark stone, foaming in its narrow upper course before it broadens and calms toward the vales below.
The Sirith runs gentle and clear through green country, cool and clean over gravel, an easy and pleasant stream to ford or drink from as it winds unhurried toward the great river.
The Erui runs swift and bright, the fastest of Gondor's streams, cold and clear and dangerous in flood; its clean water is good to drink but its rushing fords have drowned the careless.
The Serni runs shallow and slow toward the sea, warm and clear over sand, its braided channels easy to wade; the water turns brackish near the coast where the tide reaches up its mouth.
The Poros runs along the southern border, warm and sluggish, its muddy water low in the dry season and swelling brown and fast with the rains; a frontier river, its fords watched from both banks.
The Forest River — dark strong water under the black eaves of the Wood, passing beneath the bridge at the Elvenking's doors and winding out through marsh and cascade to the Long Lake.

The Onodlo winds broad and green through the grasslands, slow and placid, its reedy banks alive with birds. The water is soft and good, and its many shallows make it easy to wade where the current spreads wide and gentle.

The Rist Angsiril cuts a cold, quick channel through broken country, its clear water fast over rock, the banks steep and stony; a hard crossing, but the water runs clean and sharp with mountain chill.
The Lefnui tumbles fast and cold from the White Mountains, clear and sweet at its head but wild and unbridged, its rapids and shifting fords treacherous to any who try to cross without care.
The Lefnui tumbles fast and cold from the White Mountains, clear and sweet at its head but wild and unbridged, its rapids and shifting fords treacherous to any who try to cross without care.
The Mirilgasir glitters as its name suggests, a bright quick stream running clear over pale stones, cold and clean and pleasant to drink where it catches the light between the trees.
The Morgulduin — the stream of the vale of the dead city, cold and cruel in its sound, steaming where it runs, and poisoned where it passes. The white flowers that grow by it are luminous and deadly.

The Isen — cold grey water out of the mountains, running through the Gap of Rohan between the moors. Its fords were famous and fought for; when the wizards' works dammed and turned it, its bed ran dry and silent, and the valley below became a waste of stumps.
The Angsiril is a small, quick stream running clear and cold over a stony bed, too shallow and rough for any boat but sweet to drink where it spills down from the heights.
A shallow clear river across the empty lands — cool and quiet, forded where the old roads cross it, and flowing down to the fens of the Swanfleet where the reeds are a grey sea.
Clear icy water rushing down out of Harrowdale over its stones — loud and fast past dark Dunharrow, under the green walls of Edoras, and away to join the Entwash on the plain.

The Great River of Wilderland — a vast grey flood running south from the northlands, misty at dawn and hiding its far shore under curtains of rain. Below the rapids of Sarn Gebir it opens on the still lake of Nen Hithoel, passes between the Pillars of the Argonath, and plunges over Rauros in thunder. In its lower course it glitters in the sun past the Pelennor and away toward the Sea, and its banks know both green lawns and dead brown shores.
The Lokosir winds long and slow across the eastern lands, wide and muddy where it idles, its warm shallow water silty and better boiled than drunk; a lazy river of reed-beds and shifting sandbars.
The broad river of Lindon — cold water out of the Blue Mountains running down to the Gulf and the Grey Havens. The swan-ships pass its bar, and the sea-wind follows it far inland.

The Lake of Twilight — wide still water among the grey hills of Evendim, where the capital of the old kings stood on its shore. At dusk the lake is silver and the hills are blue, and the city's memory sleeps under the water's edge.

The Great Sea — grey and boundless water west of all lands, where the waves sigh and murmur against the shores of Middle-earth without ceasing. Out of the Havens the white ships take the Straight Road west; for all else the sea is a wall of distance and the end of the world.

The Brandywine — wide and slow, stained faintly red-brown by the upland soils it drains. Mist hangs above its reeds at dusk, the ferry creaks at Bucklebury, and its slow gurgling current is the boundary of the Shire's eastern edge.

presence.en: The Prancing Pony at Bree, the great meeting-house of the north, where Men and Hobbits crowd the common-room and the fire never dies. A hot meal, dark ale, a warm bed upstairs, and the low roar of a dozen conversations carrying every rumour on the road. Barliman's folk keep the beds aired and the door barred at night.

A hot meal, dark ale, a warm bed upstairs, and the low roar of a dozen conversations carrying every rumour on the road. Barliman's folk keep the beds aired and the door barred at night.

presence.en: There is no true rest at the Gates of Moria. Whether huddled at the West-gate or venturing the dark within, the silence presses and the black water of the mere lies still and watchful. Every echo carries too far. Sleep, if it comes, is thin and cold.

text.en: There is no true rest at the Gates of Moria. Whether huddled at the West-gate or venturing the dark within, the silence presses and the black water of the mere lies still and watchful. Every echo carries too far. Sleep, if it comes, is thin and cold.

presence.en: A Hobbit-hole or roadside farm opens its round door: a plate by the fire and a quilted bed. Homely and utterly safe.

text.en: A Hobbit-hole or roadside farm opens its round door: a plate by the fire and a quilted bed. Homely and utterly safe.

presence.en: A Sindarin settlement of the Grey-elves: cool ancient courtesy, soft light, a spare and lovely room, food simple and restoring. No tavern-clamour, only the stillness of a people who measure time in ages. Sleep is calm and clear.

text.en: A Sindarin settlement of the Grey-elves: cool ancient courtesy, soft light, a spare and lovely room, food simple and restoring. No tavern-clamour, only the stillness of a people who measure time in ages. Sleep is calm and clear.

presence.en: A Sindarin haven-city by the sea, graceful and quiet: a clean spare room above the quays, the sound of tide and rigging, and a stillness so old it steadies the heart.

text.en: A Sindarin haven-city by the sea, graceful and quiet: a clean spare room above the quays, the sound of tide and rigging, and a stillness so old it steadies the heart.

presence.en: A scattered Elven dwelling among the trees: a bed of woven things, starlight through leaves, distant Elvish song. Reserved but gracious; rest soothes more than the body.

text.en: A scattered Elven dwelling among the trees: a bed of woven things, starlight through leaves, distant Elvish song. Reserved but gracious; rest soothes more than the body.

presence.en: A Sindarin lord's house, spare and beautiful: grave welcome, restoring food, a lovely quiet room. The hospitality is measured but deep, and rest is clear and calm.

text.en: A Sindarin lord's house, spare and beautiful: grave welcome, restoring food, a lovely quiet room. The hospitality is measured but deep, and rest is clear and calm.

presence.en: A hidden Elven hamlet of the Grey-elves: a handful of timber-and-stone houses among the trees, quietude and careful order, and a rest that eases the spirit.

text.en: A hidden Elven hamlet of the Grey-elves: a handful of timber-and-stone houses among the trees, quietude and careful order, and a rest that eases the spirit.

presence.en: The Wood-elves give shelter on their terms: a platform among the boughs or a screened hollow, spare woodland fare, watchful half-wild courtesy. Rest is light and green-scented, never wholly off-guard.

text.en: The Wood-elves give shelter on their terms: a platform among the boughs or a screened hollow, spare woodland fare, watchful half-wild courtesy. Rest is light and green-scented, never wholly off-guard.

presence.en: A Silvan gathering-hall deep in the wood, lit by hanging lamps, the wood-elves feasting and singing late. A traveller is tolerated more than welcomed, given a corner and food, lulled by song into pleasant but watchful rest.

text.en: A Silvan gathering-hall deep in the wood, lit by hanging lamps, the wood-elves feasting and singing late. A traveller is tolerated more than welcomed, given a corner and food, lulled by song into pleasant but watchful rest.

presence.en: A wood-elf outpost among the great trunks: a screened camp, a share of forest fare, and the watchful courtesy of a half-wild people. Green and light, if never quite at ease.

text.en: A wood-elf outpost among the great trunks: a screened camp, a share of forest fare, and the watchful courtesy of a half-wild people. Green and light, if never quite at ease.

presence.en: A house of the High Elves, all grace and quiet power: the guest lodged with grave honour, food that restores the spirit, the very air lightening the heart. Sleep is deep and healing, and shadow loosens.

text.en: A house of the High Elves, all grace and quiet power: the guest lodged with grave honour, food that restores the spirit, the very air lightening the heart. Sleep is deep and healing, and shadow loosens.

presence.en: A night on the Rohan grass is open and clean: the wind combs the turf, the stars wheel vast overhead, and a small fire of dung or gathered wood holds off the dark. The horse-country feels free and wide, and rest comes easy for those the Riders count as friends.

text.en: A night on the Rohan grass is open and clean: the wind combs the turf, the stars wheel vast overhead, and a small fire of dung or gathered wood holds off the dark. The horse-country feels free and wide, and rest comes easy for those the Riders count as friends.

presence.en: A High-Elven city of light and song: lodging of rare beauty, restoring food, and a peace so profound that weariness and dread fall away together. Rest here truly heals.

text.en: A High-Elven city of light and song: lodging of rare beauty, restoring food, and a peace so profound that weariness and dread fall away together. Rest here truly heals.

presence.en: A High-Elven refuge hidden from the world: grave welcome, healing rest, and the sense of stepping briefly outside of time and sorrow.

text.en: A High-Elven refuge hidden from the world: grave welcome, healing rest, and the sense of stepping briefly outside of time and sorrow.

presence.en: A Dunlending steading gives grudging shelter: a corner of the byre, coarse bread, and the wary unfriendly eyes of a people with long grudges. Cold welcome, uneasy night, but the roof keeps off the rain.

text.en: A Dunlending steading gives grudging shelter: a corner of the byre, coarse bread, and the wary unfriendly eyes of a people with long grudges. Cold welcome, uneasy night, but the roof keeps off the rain.

presence.en: A rough Dunlending hall-town where a stranger is served last and watched hardest: plain fare, sour ale, talk that stops when an outsider listens. Keep your back to the wall.

text.en: A rough Dunlending hall-town where a stranger is served last and watched hardest: plain fare, sour ale, talk that stops when an outsider listens. Keep your back to the wall.

presence.en: A lone Dunlending croft in the hills: grudging shelter, coarse fare, and suspicious eyes. Uneasy but dry.

text.en: A lone Dunlending croft in the hills: grudging shelter, coarse fare, and suspicious eyes. Uneasy but dry.

presence.en: A Dwarf-hold beneath the mountain: stone chambers warm with forge-heat, strong ale, roast meat, the deep song of the delvings. A rock-cut bunk and gruff solid welcome; the dark is total, the safety absolute, rest heavy and sound.

text.en: A Dwarf-hold beneath the mountain: stone chambers warm with forge-heat, strong ale, roast meat, the deep song of the delvings. A rock-cut bunk and gruff solid welcome; the dark is total, the safety absolute, rest heavy and sound.

presence.en: A Dwarf-town at the mountain's foot: stone halls, forge-glow, strong drink and blunt hospitality. A traveller sleeps safe and warm behind doors of iron-bound oak.

text.en: A Dwarf-town at the mountain's foot: stone halls, forge-glow, strong drink and blunt hospitality. A traveller sleeps safe and warm behind doors of iron-bound oak.

presence.en: A Dwarven waystation or guard-post at a mine-road: spare stone quarters, strong ale, and blunt but genuine welcome. Safe and sound.

text.en: A Dwarven waystation or guard-post at a mine-road: spare stone quarters, strong ale, and blunt but genuine welcome. Safe and sound.

presence.en: A coastal fisher-family shares its stone house: a place by the driftwood fire, fish and hard bread, a pallet smelling of salt and net-tar. Humble and quiet Dunir folk; the sea rocks the traveller to sleep.

text.en: A coastal fisher-family shares its stone house: a place by the driftwood fire, fish and hard bread, a pallet smelling of salt and net-tar. Humble and quiet Dunir folk; the sea rocks the traveller to sleep.

presence.en: A lone fisher's hut in a sheltered cove: driftwood fire, salt fish, the boom of surf through the night. Humble shelter, plain rest.

text.en: A lone fisher's hut in a sheltered cove: driftwood fire, salt fish, the boom of surf through the night. Humble shelter, plain rest.

presence.en: To sleep in Angmar is to sleep in the enemy's own land: bitter cold that no fire fully answers, grey cloud smothering the stars, and the constant sense of being hunted. Rest is grudging and broken; the shadow of the Witch-king lies heavy on every hour.

text.en: To sleep in Angmar is to sleep in the enemy's own land: bitter cold that no fire fully answers, grey cloud smothering the stars, and the constant sense of being hunted. Rest is grudging and broken; the shadow of the Witch-king lies heavy on every hour.

presence.en: If the Woses permit it, shelter at the edge of their hidden hollows: a screened hollow, forest fare, and the unseen watchfulness of a secretive people. Wary but not unkind to a proven friend; rest light and green.

text.en: If the Woses permit it, shelter at the edge of their hidden hollows: a screened hollow, forest fare, and the unseen watchfulness of a secretive people. Wary but not unkind to a proven friend; rest light and green.

presence.en: A Druadan hidden camp among the pukel-stones: a screened hollow, silent hosts, and the watchful hush of the deep wood. Safe if they allow it.

text.en: A Druadan hidden camp among the pukel-stones: a screened hollow, silent hosts, and the watchful hush of the deep wood. Safe if they allow it.

presence.en: A night in the sickened south of Mirkwood is a vigil, not a rest: the trees crowd close, black and webbed, the air thick and sour, and unseen things move in the dark. No fire feels safe. The dread of Dol Guldur seeps through the trunks and sleep will not come clean.

text.en: A night in the sickened south of Mirkwood is a vigil, not a rest: the trees crowd close, black and webbed, the air thick and sour, and unseen things move in the dark. No fire feels safe. The dread of Dol Guldur seeps through the trunks and sleep will not come clean.

presence.en: Even in the healthy north of the wood, sleeping under Mirkwood's eaves means keeping to a small camp and a smaller fire; the canopy shuts out the stars and the forest is never wholly still. Rest is watchful but not unkind where the Wood-elves hold sway.

text.en: Even in the healthy north of the wood, sleeping under Mirkwood's eaves means keeping to a small camp and a smaller fire; the canopy shuts out the stars and the forest is never wholly still. Rest is watchful but not unkind where the Wood-elves hold sway.

presence.en: There is no rest in Mordor, only endurance. The air tastes of ash and sulphur, the ground radiates old heat or dead cold, and the red glow of the Mountain never truly leaves the sky. A traveller does not sleep here so much as wait, hollow-eyed, for a dawn that brings no relief.

text.en: There is no rest in Mordor, only endurance. The air tastes of ash and sulphur, the ground radiates old heat or dead cold, and the red glow of the Mountain never truly leaves the sky. A traveller does not sleep here so much as wait, hollow-eyed, for a dawn that brings no relief.

presence.en: A night in Nurn is spent among salt-fens and slave-fields under a smoke-stained sky. Less utterly dead than the north of Mordor, it is still a joyless, watched country; rest is shallow and the bitter sea-wind carries the misery of the land.

text.en: A night in Nurn is spent among salt-fens and slave-fields under a smoke-stained sky. Less utterly dead than the north of Mordor, it is still a joyless, watched country; rest is shallow and the bitter sea-wind carries the misery of the land.

presence.en: To sleep beneath Dol Guldur is scarcely possible; the Hill of Sorcery bleeds dread into the whole wood. The dark is absolute, the silence wrong, and the will itself feels weighed and probed. No fire, no rest, only the longing for morning and distance.

text.en: To sleep beneath Dol Guldur is scarcely possible; the Hill of Sorcery bleeds dread into the whole wood. The dark is absolute, the silence wrong, and the will itself feels weighed and probed. No fire, no rest, only the longing for morning and distance.

presence.en: A night in Forochel is a battle with the cold: no wood to burn, only the shelter a body can scrape from snow and rock, the wind constant and the aurora cold overhead. Yet the silence is clean, not evil, and one who survives the chill wakes to a world of blinding white.

text.en: A night in Forochel is a battle with the cold: no wood to burn, only the shelter a body can scrape from snow and rock, the wind constant and the aurora cold overhead. Yet the silence is clean, not evil, and one who survives the chill wakes to a world of blinding white.

presence.en: The Old Forest does not rest easy around a sleeper: the trees lean and mutter, the paths shift, and a drowsy heaviness creeps in that is not quite natural. Best to keep to open ground away from Old Man Willow's reach, and not to sleep too deep.

text.en: The Old Forest does not rest easy around a sleeper: the trees lean and mutter, the paths shift, and a drowsy heaviness creeps in that is not quite natural. Best to keep to open ground away from Old Man Willow's reach, and not to sleep too deep.

presence.en: Rivendell, the Last Homely House east of the Sea. Here weariness falls away like a set-down pack: clear voices sing in the hall, the food restores more than the body, and sleep comes deep and dreamless under Elrond's roof. Whatever shadow a traveller carries loosens its grip within these walls.

text.en: Rivendell, the Last Homely House east of the Sea. Here weariness falls away like a set-down pack: clear voices sing in the hall, the food restores more than the body, and sleep comes deep and dreamless under Elrond's roof. Whatever shadow a traveller carries loosens its grip within these walls.

presence.en: A night at large in Enedhwaith is a lonely one: wind-flattened heath rolling empty to the horizon, a faceless standing stone the only landmark, and no sound but the wind. The bleak beauty is real, but so is the solitude; rest is plain and undisturbed, if cold.

text.en: A night at large in Enedhwaith is a lonely one: wind-flattened heath rolling empty to the horizon, a faceless standing stone the only landmark, and no sound but the wind. The bleak beauty is real, but so is the solitude; rest is plain and undisturbed, if cold.

presence.en: A settlement clinging to the edge of Dagorlad is a grim, half-abandoned thing of earthworks and watchful eyes, its people hard and few, the battle-plain's dread pressing at the palisade. A roof, yes, but little rest and less warmth.

text.en: A settlement clinging to the edge of Dagorlad is a grim, half-abandoned thing of earthworks and watchful eyes, its people hard and few, the battle-plain's dread pressing at the palisade. A roof, yes, but little rest and less warmth.

presence.en: A settlement clinging to the edge of Dagorlad is a grim, half-abandoned thing of earthworks and watchful eyes, its people hard and few, the battle-plain's dread pressing at the palisade. A roof, yes, but little rest and less warmth.

text.en: A settlement clinging to the edge of Dagorlad is a grim, half-abandoned thing of earthworks and watchful eyes, its people hard and few, the battle-plain's dread pressing at the palisade. A roof, yes, but little rest and less warmth.

presence.en: Any dwelling in Angmar is the enemy's own: a slave-town or war-camp under the Witch-king's hand, cold stone and colder faces, watched by warrior-priests. To pass a night here is to hide in plain sight and pray to go unnoticed.

text.en: Any dwelling in Angmar is the enemy's own: a slave-town or war-camp under the Witch-king's hand, cold stone and colder faces, watched by warrior-priests. To pass a night here is to hide in plain sight and pray to go unnoticed.

presence.en: Any dwelling in Angmar is the enemy's own: a slave-town or war-camp under the Witch-king's hand, cold stone and colder faces, watched by warrior-priests. To pass a night here is to hide in plain sight and pray to go unnoticed.

text.en: Any dwelling in Angmar is the enemy's own: a slave-town or war-camp under the Witch-king's hand, cold stone and colder faces, watched by warrior-priests. To pass a night here is to hide in plain sight and pray to go unnoticed.

presence.en: The only 'settlements' in Mordor are barracks, slave-pens and orc-holds. To shelter in one is to risk everything on not being seen; there is no hospitality here, only walls and the constant nearness of the enemy.

text.en: The only 'settlements' in Mordor are barracks, slave-pens and orc-holds. To shelter in one is to risk everything on not being seen; there is no hospitality here, only walls and the constant nearness of the enemy.

presence.en: A Nurn slave-village of mud and reed along the bitter sea: wretched, watched, and joyless. A traveller might pass unremarked among the broken folk, but rest is thin and the overseers' eyes are everywhere.

text.en: A Nurn slave-village of mud and reed along the bitter sea: wretched, watched, and joyless. A traveller might pass unremarked among the broken folk, but rest is thin and the overseers' eyes are everywhere.

presence.en: A woodman's stockade in southern Mirkwood, palisaded against the dark, its folk grim and few and quick to bar the gate at dusk. Shelter of a sort, but the whole settlement holds its breath against the wood.

text.en: A woodman's stockade in southern Mirkwood, palisaded against the dark, its folk grim and few and quick to bar the gate at dusk. Shelter of a sort, but the whole settlement holds its breath against the wood.

presence.en: Mithlond, the Grey Havens, where Cirdan's people keep quiet hospitality by the sea. A guest is given a spare, clean room above the quays, the sound of tide and rigging through the window, and a stillness so old it steadies the heart. Sleep here is calm and salt-scented.

text.en: Mithlond, the Grey Havens, where Cirdan's people keep quiet hospitality by the sea. A guest is given a spare, clean room above the quays, the sound of tide and rigging through the window, and a stillness so old it steadies the heart. Sleep here is calm and salt-scented.

text.en: A woodman's stockade in southern Mirkwood, palisaded against the dark, its folk grim and few and quick to bar the gate at dusk. Shelter of a sort, but the whole settlement holds its breath against the wood.

presence.en: A woodmen's or wood-elf settlement in the healthier north of Mirkwood: a guarded clearing, a shared fire, wary but real welcome. Safe enough behind the palisade, though the forest presses close.

text.en: A woodmen's or wood-elf settlement in the healthier north of Mirkwood: a guarded clearing, a shared fire, wary but real welcome. Safe enough behind the palisade, though the forest presses close.

presence.en: A Lossoth village of the ice: houses of packed snow and whalebone, seal-oil lamps, and a hardy folk who take the traveller in against the killing cold. Cramped and smoky, but astonishingly warm, and the welcome is genuine.

text.en: A Lossoth village of the ice: houses of packed snow and whalebone, seal-oil lamps, and a hardy folk who take the traveller in against the killing cold. Cramped and smoky, but astonishingly warm, and the welcome is genuine.

text.en: A Lossoth village of the ice: houses of packed snow and whalebone, seal-oil lamps, and a hardy folk who take the traveller in against the killing cold. Cramped and smoky, but astonishingly warm, and the welcome is genuine.

presence.en: A Rohirrim village of the plains, timber halls and horse-paddocks under the wide sky. The Riders give rough, warm hospitality — mead, meat and a place by the fire — to any they do not count an enemy. Rest is easy on the open grass-land.

text.en: A Rohirrim village of the plains, timber halls and horse-paddocks under the wide sky. The Riders give rough, warm hospitality — mead, meat and a place by the fire — to any they do not count an enemy. Rest is easy on the open grass-land.
